documents.t: *If you are using LocalDB, this indicates that Microsoft did not properly update the LocalDB instance on your machine. To correct the issue, close TCMax® and from the Windows Start Menu open the 'Registry Editor' then follow the steps below:
documents.s: TCMax® displays the following message box when I try to launch, how do I fix this?

documents.t: On the Left Side of the screen, expand HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE. Expand SOFTWARE. Expand Microsoft. Expand Microsoft SQL Server Local DB. Expand Installed Versions. Note which Version(s) you see here, you may see multiple, we will use the highest version.
documents.s: To determine the installed version of LocalDB

documents.t: Scroll back to the top and Expand HKEY_CURRENT_USER. Expand SOFTWARE. Expand Microsoft. Expand Microsoft SQL Server. Expand User Instances. You will see different characters in here that signify the logins for the users. Find the correct {****-****-****-*****} that is the logged in user to the computer. You will know you have the correct one, as when you click on the User you will see information appear on the right side of the screen. Note on the right side of the screen a listing for Parent Instance in the Name column. From the Parent Instance line, refer to the Data column, and verify what it reads, MSSQL##E.LOCALDB. The numbers highlighted blue correspond to the configured version for that user. If it varies from the noted version earlier, right click on the Parent Instance and press Modify. Update the Parent Instance to read MSSQL##E.LOCALDB and inputting the correct version number. Once that is changed, close Registry Editor and restart the computer for the changes to take effect. If you are still encountering issues, contact Soaring Software Solutions, Inc. at ((419) 442-7676) for additional assistance. info This process may need to be repeated for several users on the computer due to how Windows manages registry keys in the operating system. For users that are connected to a shared Database, you will need to contact COMM or your IT department to verify the status of and credentials for the Microsoft SQL Server® instance.
documents.s: To change the users configured version of LocalDB

documents.t: *If using LocalDB, you can restore to the backup from the TCMax® client. From the Main Screen go to File > Database Maintenance. From the Database Maintenance screen, select the Backup Database tab. On the Backup Database tab, select the Restore Database button. You will be asked to confirm you want to restore as doing so will overwrite any existing data. After confirming, you will be shown a windows file picker where you can navigate to and select the backup file you would like to restore to. TCMax® will prompt you when the restoration process is complete. File > Database Maintenance | Backup Database (Tab) *If connected to a server, the file will have to be restored within Microsoft SQL Server® Management Studio (SSMS). Once logged into SSMS with server administrator credentials, right click on the Databases folder in the object explorer then select Restore Database. On the Restore Database screen, select the Device radio button then select the ellipsis button on the right side of the Device input box. Select the Add button from the 'Select backup devices' screen and use the file picker to select the Database file you want to restore then select OK. Review the backup file(s) you selected and select OK again to return to the Restore Databases screen. You will now see the Destination Database and Restore plan. Click OK to unpack and finish restoring.
documents.s: How do I Restore to my Backup (.bak) File?

documents.t: Database sharing is enabled through Microsoft SQL Server®. You can configure/enable the server sharing through SQL Server Configuration Manager and configure the database access and permissions through Microsoft SQL Server® Management Studio. Microsoft SQL Server® is a separate program from TCMax®. This would need downloaded and installed outside of TCMax® first. Once installed, below are steps to configure the server for TCMax®. Within the configuration manager under SQL Server Services; make sure that the SQL Server and SQL Server Browser are in a Running state and the Start Mode is set to Automatic. You will also want to enable all Server and Client Protocols for the SQL Server Network Configuration node as well the 32bit and standard SQL Native Client Configuration nodes. Within Microsoft SQL Server® Management studio, under the Security > Logins folder you will want to verify that the Login\Group being used to authenticate with the server is mapped and has the appropriate permissions to gain access to the database. Right click on the Login/Group and select Properties. On the User Mapping page, put a check next to your TCMax® database in the Map column. Select the database roles db_datareader, db_datawriter, & public. Press OK when finished. Login Properties > User Mapping Still within Microsoft SQL Server® Management Studio, make sure remote connections are enabled. Right click on the Server Name [Not the Database Name] and select Properties. Select the Connections section and make sure 'Allow remote connections to this server' is checked. Click OK once done. Allowing Remote Connections to the Server Then, when launching TCMax® and within the connection properties window, you will need to point TCMax® to your properly configured server and database.
documents.s: How do I Share a Database with Version 9?

documents.t: If you have TCMax® already installed, you can view the license information by going to Help > About from the Main Screen. If your software is not yet licensed you can find your license information on our website, https://soaringsoftware.com, by logging in to your linked account and viewing the license information section. Contact Soaring Software Solutions, Inc. at (419) 442-7676 for additional assistance.
documents.s: Where do I find my TCMax® License Information?

documents.t: Option 1: You can find your license information on our website, https://soaringsoftware.com, by logging in to your linked account and viewing the license information section. Option 2: If your TCMax® installation is licensed, navigate to the Windows C Drive and go to the following directory, C:\Users > Public > Public Documents > TCMax > Documentation. Once in the Documentation folder, locate your License Details file. The License Details file will allow for you to view your Company Name and Support Id. For further assistance on trying to obtain your License Information, please contact Soaring Software Solutions, Inc. at (419) 442-7676.
documents.s: How do I find my TCMax® License Information if TCMax® Won't Open?

documents.t: This section of the Documentation will contain instructions on moving a TCMax® installation to a new workstation. If you are not moving TCMax® to a new computer, skip this section. If you are upgrading from TCMax® Version 8 to Version 9.X, please follow the installation instructions, then refer to the Migrations section to bring the Version 8 Data into the Version 9 Database.
documents.s: How to Move TCMax® to a New Computer?

documents.t: To transfer the TCMax® installation from one computer to another, you will need to determine what your current configuration is and what settings/files need brought to the new computer.
documents.s: Transferring TCMax® to a New Computer

documents.t: To bring the TCMax® settings to your new computer, save them to the Database. Open Settings > Options and select the Captions and Presets tab. Save the settings in the Database with a name of something meaningful to you so you can recall the settings later. In the "Custom Option Presets" group box, select New Preset then select the Save Custom Preset button. You will then be prompted to enter a name. Type the name of your settings and hit OK. Remember this to restore your settings later.

To move the attachments folder, you must first identify if the attachments TCMax® is referencing are stored locally or on a network location. To identify this, access Settings > Options and expand the Display Options section. At the bottom of this section, you will see a group box for Picture and Attachment Path. If the path starts with C:\ it is most likely a local path. For other drive letters, you will need to reference your Windows settings to see if they are network drives.
documents.s: Moving the Attachments and Pictures Folders

documents.t: If the attachments are saved locally, copy the folder (in this case, the folder is called Images) to your transfer media. Once the new computer is set up, you will retrieve this folder from this media.

If your attachments and pictures are stored on a network drive, and if you are reconnecting to this network, make note of the folder path so you can manually connect to it from the new client install. If you do not plan on reconnecting to this network and would like to cease sharing the files, follow the steps for Local Attachments Folder.

To identify what type of Database you are connected to, open the Help > About screen. Near the top of this screen, below your license and support information, you will see Data Source and Database fields. If your Data source fields includes "(LocalDB)" and you can see the Database Location field, then you are connected to a LocalDB instance. If the Database location field is not visible, then you are connected to a Microsoft SQL Server® instance.

If you are using a LocalDB, you can use the backup feature of TCMax® to create a copy of your Database. File > Backup Options > Current Path will display the location where your backups are being stored. Make a backup by selecting the Backup Database menu option or pressing F11 on your keyboard. Retrieve your backup from this folder (it will be titled the Database name with the date and time) and place this on your transfer media.

If you are using Microsoft SQL Server® and plan to use this Database locally, you will need your Database Administrator to create a backup of the Database using Microsoft SQL Server® Management Studio. If you plan to reconnect to the networked SQL Database, you will only need to know your login information for the Microsoft SQL Server® connection. You can find this information from the About screen (except for passwords).

To remove your TCMax® license from the machine which you will no longer be using, you will need to launch the Soaring License Manager from the Programs > TCMax folder of your Windows Start Menu, or you can launch the program from C:\Program Files\Soaring Software Solutions, Inc\TCMax. You will need administrative privileges on this computer to use this utility. To Deauthorize this computer, select the Deauthorize button on the license you would like to remove.
To prepare the new computer, install TCMax® on the computer. Once installed, you will have the files necessary to continue. Do not start TCMax® yet.

To restore a LocalDB, you will first need to connect to a new blank Database, then from within the software, you can restore to your backup from the previous computer. For ease of use, place the backed-up Database from your transfer media to a safe place on your new computer, and start TCMax®. It will ask you for the Database you would like to connect to. By default, you should see settings for a LocalDB connection. Version 9.8 and older Version 9.9 and newer If your window appears as one of the images above, hit OK. If there is not a Local Database in the location specified, you will receive the following message. Select Continue and TCMax® will create the Database files in the designated location. TCMax® will now ask you to license your installation, this will require administrative privileges to start the Soaring License Manager. From within the License Manager, select the Add/Modify button and you will be presented with the licensing screen. Your company/unit license credentials can be located from the license certificate or by viewing the license information page from the Soaring Software Website (www.soaringsoftware.com).These credentials are case/space sensitive and the License Manager will display a green checkmark when the information has been entered successfully. Once a green checkmark is displayed, select Activate to apply the license. TCMax® will now ask you to include Demo Data. To proceed with the restore it is advised to include Demo Data as this will speed up the process of restoration. tip If Demo Data is not included, TCMax® will ask you to create a Shop Code and an Administrator User. TCMax® will now tell you ‘No Shop Codes Selected’. Press OK through the No Shop Codes Selected screen, where you will select a Shop Code. TCMax® will now display a Sites and Shop Codes Screen. If you did not include Demo Data, you will need to create a new shop code here. If you included Demo Data, you will see the 'TCMax Demo Shop' that can be selected. After you have selected the 'TCMax Demo Shop' or the newly created Shop Code, press Save. If you did not include Demo Data, TCMax® will ask you to create an Admin User. Select Yes. TCMax® will display the User and Item Barcodes screen. This screen will allow for you to configure the User's and Item's barcode character counts. Press Save once/if information is modified. note This information can be changed once the restore has been completed. For ease of use, just accept the defaults and make note that a '2' digit Barcode Id can be used to create your temporary Admin User. You will then be prompted to create an Admin User and Password. Make sure to note the User Id and Password as you will need them to log in and perform the restore from the next steps. If you included Demo Data, see the steps below for further guidance. TCMax® will now ask you to log in to the Database. Log in using the built-in Demo Admin. The User Id is “01” without the quotes, and the User Password is also “01” without the quotes or log in with the Admin User credentials that were created in the previous step. Once logged in, go to File > Database Maintenance. TCMax® will display another login screen to verify permissions to the Database Maintenance screen. Log in using the built-in Demo Admin. The User Id is “01” without the quotes, and the User Password is also “01” without the quotes or log in with the Admin User credentials that were created. Once logged in to the Database Maintenance screen, go to the Backup Database tab. Once on the Backup Database tab, select Restore Database. TCMax® will display a Restore Database screen verifying you want to restore your current database, select Yes. Once Yes is selected, TCMax® will open a File Explorer window where you will find and select your backup file to restore to. Once the backup file has been selected, TCMax® will display a Backup Restored screen. Hit OK. TCMax® should restart (in the event the Software does not relaunch automatically, go ahead and relaunch the Software manually). Once the Software has relaunched, you will see a 'No Shop Codes Selected' screen displayed. Press OK through the No Shop Codes Selected screen. TCMax® will now display a Sites and Shop Codes Screen where you can select your Shop Code(s). Once your Shop Codes have been selected, press Save. You will now be prompted to log in to the Database. Log in to the Database with your User account credentials from your previous TCMax® client.

If you are connecting to an instance of Microsoft SQL Server®, have your Database administrator restore your Database using Microsoft SQL Server® Management Studio, and when prompted, enter the information to connect to your Database. You will then need to license your software.

Once you are reconnected to your Database, open Settings > Options and click on the Captions and Presets tab. In the Custom Options Presets group box, you will see the drop-down list of your saved settings. Select the setting you created in the previous steps and choose Load Custom Presets.

If you are connecting locally to attachments, place your attachments folder from the transfer media to a public location on your computer (most commonly C:\Users\Public\Documents\TCMax). In the General Options tab of Settings > Options, expand the Display Options. Find the Picture and Attachment Path then select the Set Path button, making sure to select the folder that was just copied from the transfer media.
The Minimum, Recommended, and Feature Requirements are outlined in the Requirements and Recommendations section. Select the link to be taken to that page to view the specific Requirements.
documents.s: What are the Requirements and Recommendations for TCMax®?

documents.t: If you were previously connected to a Database and are seeing the Connection Properties Window, either someone has changed your connection string or the Server/Database you were connected to has changed in some way. If you were connected to a Database on a Server, you will need to contact your onsite IT and have them provide you the connection information for your Database. The default LocalDB connection information for TCMax® is displayed below. Version 9.8 and older Version 9.9 and newer If you are Local, make sure under 'Attach a database file' or 'Attached File' that you are pointed to your Database. If you are not, select the 'Browse' button or 'three elipses' to locate your Database. Make sure the 'Logical Name' or 'Database Name' matches your Database name. If you are still experiencing issues after confirming connection and trying to connect, contact Soaring Software Solutions, Inc. at (419) 442-7676 for additional assistance.
documents.s: What to do when Connection Properties Window Appears?

documents.t: TCMax® can be downloaded from our website at https://soaringsoftware.com. If you are visiting the website for the first time, you will need to create an account then verify your email. Once the account has been created and you are logged in, you will need to link your current TCMax® license to your account. Once you have done that successfully, you will have access to download the TCMax® installers from the Product Downloads page of the website. This is where you can choose the Version of TCMax® you would like to download.
documents.s: Where can I Download the TCMax® Software?

documents.t: Asset History Tracking is a feature that allows a user to track certain modifications made to items and can be used to restore an item to a previous state if the modification was made in error. To use this feature, it first must be enabled for the shop code the item(s) exist in through File > Database Maintenance > Asset History Tracking. To open the Asset History screen, display an item on the Main Screen and then hit Ctrl + H on your keyboard. If the item has no history associated with it or if Asset History Tracking is not enabled, you will see the following prompt. Version 9.9 and Newer Version 9.8 and Older To open the Asset History screen, display an item on the Main Screen and then hit Ctrl + H on your keyboard. If the item has no history associated with it or if Asset History Tracking is not enabled, you will see the following prompt. If the item does have history associated with it then the Asset History screen will open. On the left side of the screen the item is displayed along with all available restore points for that item. The restore points are ordered by the date and time that the modifications have been made. When a restore point is selected you will see how many changes were made at that time. When a restore point is selected the left side of the screen will display the item's history value prior to the modifications and the item's current values. If you would like to restore the item to its previous status, click the Review Commit button in the bottom right hand corner of the screen. When you click the Review Commit button, a Review screen will be displayed that allows you to see what Data will be reverted. The values highlighted in green from the selected restore point will be pushed to the item’s current state. If you are satisfied with the changes to be made, click the Commit Changes button to revert the item. Once the changes have been made, you will be taken back to the Main Screen of TCMax®. Clear the Main Screen of TCMax® and redisplay your item to refresh the changes that were made. Clicking the Cancel Commit button will cancel the reversion and take you to the Asset History screen restore points. To open the Asset History screen, display an item on the Main Screen and then hit Ctrl + H on your keyboard. If the item has no history associated with it or if Asset History Tracking is not enabled, you will see the following prompt. If the item does have history associated with it then the Asset History screen will open. On the left side of the screen the item is displayed along with all available restore points for that item. The restore points are ordered by the date and time that the modifications have been made. When a restore point is selected you will see who was logged in at the time the change was made and how many changes were made at that time. When a restore point is selected the left side of the screen will display the item status prior to and after that modification has been made. If you would like to restore the item to its previous status, click the Review Commit button in the bottom right hand corner of the screen. When you click the Review Commit button, a Review screen will be displayed that allows you to see what Data will be reverted. The values highlighted in green from the selected restore point will be pushed to the item’s current state, and the Data highlighted in red will be overwritten. If you are satisfied with the changes to be made, click the Commit Changes button to revert the item. If you commit the changes, you will be presented with the following prompt indicating that the change completed successfully: Once the changes have been made, you will be taken back to the Main Screen of TCMax®. Clicking the Close button will cancel the reversion and close the Asset History screen.

If you are using a Local Database, backups for your Database will be done directly through TCMax®. This is done by hitting F11 or going to File > Backup Options. From File > Backup Options you can set / change the backup path. From File > Backup Options you can also view your current backup path. info If you are using a SQL Server to host the Database, the backup will need to be done directly from the Server. This action cannot be performed within the TCMax® software. When connected to a SQL Server, the Backup Options menu will not be available.

Use this screen to create a backup of a Database, change a Database Connection String, restore TCMax® Demo Data, migrate options used in TCMax® Version 8 into TCMax® Version 9.X, clean-up the EventLog table, or delete Sites and Shop Codes. To access the Database Maintenance screen, you must first be logged in as someone who has the Access Database Maintenance permission and go to File > Database Maintenance. You will be prompted to enter your TCMax® credentials again. This is to verify that you, the Admin, is still present when attempting to access such a critical screen. This additional login removes the chance of an Admin forgetting to log out and having someone else make changes on their behalf. Once you’ve loaded the Database Maintenance screen, select the appropriate tab from the top tool bar and perform your desired action. Each tab is explained in the following sections. To exit the Database Maintenance screen at any point, click Close located in the bottom right hand corner of the window. This will exit out of the screen and go back to the TCMax® Main Screen.

info This is only available if you are connected to a Local Database. This tab can be used to set your backup path, create a backup, or restore from a backup. To set a backup path click the Set Backup Path button and use the browser that pops up to select your backup location. info When selecting a backup path, make sure it follows your organizations best practices for handling backups. It is advised that the backups be stored in an area accessible to all users of the machine that TCMax® is installed on. It is also advised that a copy of the backups be kept independent of the machine, i.e., copied to a removable hard drive or CD/DVD-RW, in the event of the loss of the machine, a copy of your Data will still be available for recovery. To create a backup, click the Backup Database button. Upon completion, you will be presented with the following message indicating where the backup is stored. To restore from a backup, click the Restore Database button. Upon doing so you will see the following warning: Clicking Yes will then open a Windows File Explorer that you can use to find and select your backup. When you select your backup, TCMax® will begin the restore process. When it finishes you will be presented the following message: Clicking OK will cause TCMax® to close and restart. If TCMax® doesn’t automatically restart it can be launched from the desktop shortcut.

Click the Change Database Connection button and enter the necessary connection information in the Connection Properties window that appears. If the Database is a Local Database, you can detach the current Database from LocalDB by clicking on the Detach Current Database (LocalDB Only) option. tip When connecting to a new Database, TCMax® will need to restart before any changes take effect.

Upon initial install, the option to include Demo Data will be presented to the user, so depending on the initial setup of TCMax®, the ‘TCMax® Demo Shop’ could be installed in the current Database. The TCMax® Demo Shop is a preprogrammed shop code which includes demo users and items built into the Database for training purposes. Use the TCMax® Demo Shop Data with our Quick Start PDF guide to help familiarize you with how TCMax® runs and operates. You can restore or include the Demo Data by clicking the Restore Demo Data button on this tab.

info The Migrations tab will no longer be available in Versions 9.9.0 and newer of TCMax®. Use this tab to migrate any special options used in TCMax® Version 8 over to TCMax® Version 9. Special options include: Shop Code Selection, Times Used Inspections option, Air Force captions, Navy HazMat option, and Air Force Security Forces captions. If you used any of those options in TCMax® Version 8, this screen will allow you to migrate them over to be used in TCMax® Version 9. The Migrations screen shows up as part of your Data migration on the Import/Export screen, however, if you need to migrate those special options after your import has completed, you can do so from this tab.

info Deleting log records will be applicable to Versions 9.8.9420.23888 or older of TCMax®. In Versions 9.8.9580.24506 or newer of TCMax®, log records will need to be deleted from the Server end. Database Tools can be used to purge old historical Data from the Database. Event log records created prior to the date selected in the date selection box can be deleted upon clicking the Deleted Logs button. note It is advised that a backup of the Database be created prior to deleting any EventLog records. Rebuild Indexes can rebuild indexes in your TCMax® Database if they have become corrupted. This may lead to an increase in performance of the Database if it has become slow due to internal SQL errors.

warning All changes made to shop codes are instant and permanent. To delete a shop code, select the row of the shop code you want to delete. This should highlight the whole row blue (see image below). After the row is selected click the Delete Selected Shop Code button. tip You cannot delete a shop code that is set as your Primary Shop Code. To adjust the primary shop code, go to Settings > Sites and Shops. A message box will appear asking to confirm your action. If No is selected TCMax® will cancel the selection and exit back to the Database Maintenance screen. If Yes is selected TCMax® will present another screen where you will have to confirm the selection and type a message displayed word for word like the example below to confirm the deletion of the shop code. Once the message is typed out and complete click OK. The Shop Code will be deleted and will no longer exist. If you click Cancel TCMax® will exit to the Database Maintenance screen. info Deleting a Shop Code will alter historical EventLog Data generated in that shop which might prevent those records from appearing on some reports.

warning All changes to sites are instant and permanent. Deleting a site out of the Database will make all shop codes assigned to the particular site available for all computers to access until assigned to another site. To delete a site, select the row of the site to be deleted; this should highlight the whole row blue (see image below) after the row is selected click the Delete Selected Site button. You will only be allowed to delete a site or sites that you are not currently connected to. tip You cannot delete a site that is set as your site you are viewing. To adjust the site, go to Settings > Sites and Shops. A message box will appear asking to confirm your action. If No is selected TCMax® will cancel the selection and exit back to the Database Maintenance screen. If Yes is selected TCMax® will present another screen where you will have to confirm the selection and type the message displayed word for word like the example below to confirm the deletion of the site. Once the message is typed out and complete click OK. The site will be deleted and will no longer exist in TCMax®. If you click Cancel TCMax® will exit to the Database Maintenance screen.

Asset History Tracking allows a user to track certain modifications made to items and can be used to restore an item to a previous state if the modification was made in error. Asset History Tracking is enabled per Shop Code. To activate Asset History Tracking for a Shop Code, highlight the chosen shop from the Deactivated Shops list and click the >> button to move the shop to the Activated Shops list. You will then be prompted to set the number of days you would like to track modifications for that shop. Enter the number of days that you wish to set (leaving it as 0 sets it to the default value) and click OK. Once you do this, the shop will appear in the Activated Shops list with the number of days a user can restore to displayed next to it. To deactivate Asset History Tracking, click on the shop listed in the Activated Shops list and click the << button to move the shop code to the Deactivated Shops list. To view further information in regards to Asset History Tracking, please click the following link.

You can set a default preset to load when a specific shop code is set as a machines default shop code. This allows you to standardize the options that are set in Settings > Options for all machines in a given shop. Select the shop code you would like to assign the preset to, use the Presets dropdown to assign the preset to that shop and click the Save button on the bottom right hand corner of this screen.
info The options in this menu will vary based on the permissions of the logged in user and the Database Connection configuration.
Clicking this option will log out the current logged in user and display the log in screen to allow another user to log in. This feature is also tied to the F12 hotkey.
This will log out the currently logged in user.

This will generate a new item barcode using the preset configuration in Settings > Options > User And Item Barcodes in the Barcode Id Configuration section. There are two types of presets that can be configured, primary and secondary. A primary item will draw its Barcode Id from the primary barcode configuration and the secondary item will draw its Barcode Id from the secondary barcode configuration. The F3 hotkey creates an item from the primary configuration setting and the Ctrl + F3 hotkey creates an item from the secondary configuration setting.
This will generate a new user barcode using the preset configuration in Settings > Options > User And Item Barcodes in the User Id Configuration section. This feature is tied to the F4 hotkey.
Clicking this will close the TCMax® program.

info Deployment Connection Options will be applicable to Versions 9.8.8922.28031 or older of TCMax®. Versions 9.8.8992.16156 or newer of TCMax® will implement a new screen called Deployment Data Manager. Deployment Connection Options will fall under a legacy mode in those Versions. Users will have the ability to switch to legacy mode, if needed. Versions 9.9.0 or newer of TCMax® will no longer have the capability to switch to legacy mode. danger There are compatibility constraints when deploying a Database, therefore it is essential when using the legacy deployment system that your home station and deployment systems are utilizing the same Microsoft SQL Server® / Microsoft SQL Server® LocalDB versions as well as TCMax® product versions.

This screen is used to manage connections to Deployment Databases. To access the Deployment Connection Options screen, go to File > Deployment Connection Options. Upon selecting Deployment Connection Options, you will be prompted to enter your User Id and Password ("Access Database Maintenance" permission is required). From this screen, you can establish a new connection to a Deployment Database, import Data from another Deployment Database, or make a copy of the Database you are currently connected to. info This screen is intended to be used on the Deployed instance of TCMax®. If you are packing for a Deployment from your home-station machine, you want to create the Deployment from Tools > Temporary Item Transfer / Deploy.
documents.s: Importing Deployment Data/Connecting to a Deployment Database

documents.t: Clicking the Connect button in the New Database Connection section will display an explorer window that will allow you to navigate to the Database you wish to connect to. In this window, you will navigate to the SEDF file you created when exporting the Deployment. Once you have selected the new Database (the SEDF file), TCMax® will restart and establish a connection to the selected Database. It is worth noting that TCMax® will not connect to the new Database in the location you pointed it to. It will copy that Database to the C:\Users\Public\Documents\TCMax folder, mount that Database to an instance of Microsoft SQL Server® LocalDB, and connect to that Database. If you are connected to a full instance of Microsoft SQL Server® or Microsoft SQL Server® Express, you will be presented with a message box that says if you continue with the operation you will then be connected to a Local Database (LocalDB).

Clicking the Merge button in the Merge Deployment Data section will populate a Deployment Merge screen. From the Deployment Merge screen, select the Set Source button. A File Explorer window will open and allow you to select the Database to merge information from. You will point TCMax® to your SEDF file you created when exporting for Deployment. This will not create a new Database, but this will merge the information from the exported Deployment into the existing Database on this computer. Once selected, click the Merge button to complete the action. This is typically used when several units are deploying to one location. From that one deployed version of TCMax®, you would come to this screen and import each of the deployed unit’s Databases to consolidate them all into the one you’re currently using. info If you’re connecting to a new Database or importing into an existing Database, if the Deployments contain shops that haven’t been set up on the Deployment machine, you’ll need to go to Tools > Sites and Shops to reconfigure TCMax® so that these new shops can be visible from this machine.

Clicking the Copy Database button in the Copy Current Database section will create a copy of the Database you are currently connected to and save it to the location you specify. This creates the SIDF file you would take back to home station. This can then be imported back to their Database after the Deployment to update it with the information generated while deployed. This function is only available if TCMax® is connected to a Local Database. If you are not connected to a Local Database, you will need to take a backup of the Database directly from Microsoft SQL Server® Management Studio and copy the backup (BAK) file manually to bring back to home station.

Create a Deployment Database via Tools > Temporary Item Transfer / Deploy, then put that SEDF file on a disc or drive you can access from your Deployed location. tip If you have the computer that TCMax® will be used on while Deployed, you could connect the Database before physically deploying. Once you get settled into your new deployed location, you need to decide how you’re going to setup TCMax®. You have some options: You can connect directly to a copy of that Deployment Database. This is typically used when one unit is deploying all by themselves and there is no need to keep old Data from the last Deployment. You can keep your existing Data and merge the deployed assets/personnel into an existing TCMax® Database. This is typically used when several units are deploying to one common location or if the Deployed location is using TCMax® with existing assets when you arrive. Once your Deployment is over and you’re ready to pack up your assets and head home, you’ll want to copy your current Database and throw it on an external drive, disc, network location, etc. that can be accessed by the home-station. Once they have a copy of your Deployment Data, they will go to Tools > Temporary Item Transfer / Deploy and follow the steps in the Returning From Deployment section.

info Deployment Data Manager will be applicable to Versions 9.8.8992.16156 or newer of TCMax®. Versions 9.8.8922.28031 or older of TCMax® will still utilize the Deployment Connection Options. If you are using 9.8.8922.28031 or older on either machine (Deployment or Home Station), you will need to revert to the legacy mode, which can be accessed from File > Deployment Data Manager > File > Open Legacy Deployment Mode. TCMax® Version 9.9.0 and newer will no longer have the capability to revert back to the legacy mode.

This screen is used on your Deployment Database to manage connections to Deployments. To access the Deployment Data Manager screen, go to File > Deployment Data Manager. Upon selecting Deployment Data Manager, you will be prompted to enter your User Id and Password ("Access Database Maintenance" permission is required). From this screen, you can Import a Deployment File brought from Home Station, or Export a Deployment that is being taken back home. info If your Deployment file is a .sedf file and not a .xdef file, that signifies the legacy version of creating a Deployment file was used. In Deployment Data Manager you will need to select File > Open Legacy Deployment Data Connections then refer to Deployment Connection Options for connecting to the .sedf file. note This screen is intended to be used on the Deployed instance of TCMax®. If you are packing for a Deployment from your home-station machine, you want to create the Deployment from Tools > Temporary Item Transfer / Deploy.

Before importing a Deployment, you will want to ensure you have switched to a new Database that will not conflict with any Shop Codes or Users from your Deployment file. If you are currently connected to a Local Database and need to connect to a new Database, go to File > Deployment Data Manager. From Deployment Data Manager, go to File > Connect to a New Database. After selecting Connect to a New Database, a New Database File Connection screen will appear. From here you can adjust the Database location, if needed, and enter a Database Name. tip For the Database Name it is advised you enter a Name that has not been used in the past. When the directory has been confirmed and the Database Name has been entered, press Save. TCMax should restart and provide you with a Connection Properties window that is set to the desired Database. Proceed with generating this new Database. Don't Include Demo Data It is advised to not include Demo Data to prevent Shop Code and User conflicts. It is recommended to add a placeholder Shop Code and User that are unrelated to your Deployment you will be importing. If you are currently connected to a SQL Server Database and need to connect to a new Database, go to File > Database Maintenance. From Database Maintenance, navigate to Change Database Connections.

Clicking the Enable Deployment Database button will enable the Deployments section of the Deployment Data Manager screen. When Enable Deployment Database is selected, you will receive a popup asking if you are sure you want to enable Deployments on this Database. Before clicking Yes, verify you are on your Deployment Database then select Yes. info When Enable Deployment Database is enabled, the Deployment tab from Tools > Temporary Item Transfer / Deploy (Ctrl + T) will be hidden. note As long as a Deployment has not been imported from the Deployments section, you will have the ability to Disable Deployment Database. When a Deployment has been imported, there is no way to disable Deployments.

Select Import Deployment and a File Explorer window will open to allow you to navigate to your Deployment file brought from home station (.xdef file). Locate/select the file from the File Explorer window then press open. You will receive a loading status popup while the Deployment is being imported. Once the import is finished you will be on the Deployment Data Manager screen and you should see your Deployment listed in the grid from the Deployments section. You can import multiple Deployments into one Deployment Database, but you must import them one at a time selecting Import Deployment each time. note If multiple Deployments will be imported, ensure no Shop Code or User conflicts arise. If the same User Id exists in multiple Deployments, it will only accept the first imported User as User Ids must be unique in a Database. Additional Option(s): This option is utilized if you are planning on creating new items while on Deployment. This option will allow a prompt when you add new items asking which Deployment you would like the item to be a part of. This will ensure when bringing the Deployment back home that the newly created item is brought back home and added to inventory at home station. Once you have imported all your Deployments, click Close. You will be presented with the Sites and Shop Codes screen. You should see your Shop Codes the items on Deployment are from. Check the box next to any and all Shop Codes you need to view while on Deployment and select Save. You will be brought back to the Main Screen of TCMax® where you can now interact with the items you have brought on Deployment.

When you are done on Deployment and ready to go back home, you will refer to Export Deployment within Deployment Data Manager. First, you will need to refer to the Deployments section and select the Deployment you would like to Export to return home. With the Deployment selected and highlighted you can now Export the Deployment. Under Export Deployment, there is an option to Export Logs. Checking Export Logs will export all event logs that were created on Deployment (issue / turn-in records, item modified records, etc.). If you choose not to select Export Logs, your items will still be exported along with any modifications you have made to the deployed items, however, no event logs will be returned home (issue / turn-in records, item modified records, etc.). With the Export Logs option checked or unchecked, click Export. A File Explorer will open and you will navigate to where you would like to save the exported file (.xdif file). By default, a name will be provided that matches the file you imported, this can be changed, if desired. Once you select Save on the File Explorer window, you will receive a loading status while the Deployment is being exported. Once the Export is finished you will be on the Deployment Data Manager screen. You can now close out of this screen and take your .xdif file back to home station. info If you have imported more than one Deployment, you will need to export EACH Deployment in order to properly return the individual Deployments at home station.

The Import/Export screen allows a user to populate the current TCMax® Database with Data from another Version 9 Database, an Excel spreadsheet, or from a Version 8 TCMax® Database. To access this feature the user must have a valid User Id and Password and have the Access Import/Export permission in User Options.

The TCMax® Data Copy tab provides the ability to copy Data from one TCMax® Database to another. This feature was previously referred to as Version 9 to 9 Copy. To configure the transfer, select Set Source to define the source Database and Set Destination to define the destination Database. Enter the required Database information in the corresponding fields to establish the appropriate source and destination connections. Version 9.8 and older Version 9.9 and newer The copy can be done for all shop codes or for a specific shop code by selecting the appropriate shop code option(s) from the Shop Code Selection drop down box.

There are several options that dictate how Data will be copied from the source to destination Databases. Copy All Users From Source: This option, when enabled, will force all users in the source Database to be copied to the destination. When not enabled, only users assigned to your selected site and users who have not been assigned a site will be copied over. For conflicts, Overwrite Destination Data: This option will overwrite any Data in the destination Database that has the same unique constraints (Shop Code and Barcode Id) as an item in the source. Update Previously Copied Data: This option updates Data that has already been copied from the selected source to the selected destination. This Data is identified by the ‘SyncId’ applied to the item in the TCMax® Database. Table Exclusions: These tables can be skipped during the copy the process. Event Log is excluded by default. Once you have your source and destination databases set and your shop code(s) and options selected you can click the Start Copy button to copy Data from the source to destination. The Copy Event Logs button allows the user to copy the event logs independently if they were excluded from the initial data copy. The Event Log table can be quite vast and separating the movement of data allows for a more efficient use of available computing resources and improved performance during this operation. During the Copy process, you will see several progress bars appear in the Copy Status section. If there are any errors during the copy you will be notified there as well. info Regardless of how you have brought new Data into your system, if you did not import information into an already existing/selected shop code you will need to select the newly imported shop code from the Settings > Sites and Shops screen to have visibility of the items.

info Additional logging information has been added in Version 9.9.0 and higher when using Excel Import. The Excel Import tab is used to import well formatted Excel spreadsheets of information into TCMax®. Using Excel spreadsheets, you can import Items, Users, Item Inspections, and User Certifications. To load a spreadsheet for import, click the Load Spreadsheet button which will open a Windows Explorer window that you will use to navigate to and select the spreadsheet. Once you have selected the spreadsheet, the Data from the sheet will be displayed in the grid of this tab. Review the Data in this grid and make any changes necessary prior to import. The text section in the bottom left hand corner of this screen will provide more information as to why specific pieces of information may not be imported into TCMax. When you are ready to import the Data, click the Import button. When the import has finished the results will be displayed in the grid. If a field is highlighted in red then the Item was not able to be imported, the reason for which is found in the Result field of the grid. Make sure you check the results to ensure the items were imported. tip The spreadsheet import is limited to importing up to 10,000 records at a time. You can also create template spreadsheets for Items, Item Inspections, Users, and User Certifications by selecting the template you would like to create from the dropdown menu in the Create Spreadsheet Template area and clicking the Create Spreadsheet button. When using the template you created, do not delete any of the columns, as TCMax® needs those to read the Data properly. info Regardless of how you have brought new Data into your system, if you did not import information into an already existing/selected shop code you will need to select the newly imported shop code from the Settings > Sites and Shops screen to have visibility of the items.

The Migrations tab allows you to bring Data from Version 8 of TCMax® to Version 9 of TCMax®. This function can migrate Data from both SQL Server and Microsoft® Access Databases. info The Migrations tab will no longer be available in Versions 9.9.0 and newer of TCMax®. Migrating from Microsoft® Access Migrating from Microsoft® Access is no longer an option in Version 9.8.7853 and higher of TCMax®. If you do not see this option available and are trying to migrate, contact our Customer Support Center (419) 442-7676 for additional assistance.

info When performing an 8 to 9 Migration, we require that the Source and Destination Database be on the same Server. If your Version 8 Data is in a Microsoft SQL Server® Database, select the SQL Server radio button and then click the Set Source button which will bring up a Connections Properties window. Version 9.8 and older Version 9.9 and newer Enter the information for your Server, log in method, and Database. If available, click the Test Connection button and if it says “Test connection succeeded” you can click the OK button to proceed. If it gives any other result than “Test connection succeeded,” take note of the error indicated and correct the connection information. Click the Set Destination button and follow the same steps, except in this case you will enter the destination Server’s information. The Database you are currently connected to is selected by default. Step One - Verify Source Database: To verify that your source Database is up to date and all datatypes are correct you will need to click the Verify Source Database button. This step is not optional and must be completed before progressing to step two. Step Two - Sync Data: At this point you can click the Sync Data button to move the Data into your destination Microsoft SQL Server® Database. Once this button is clicked, TCMax® will ask if tool chits were used in the previous version of TCMax®. If tool chits were entered in TCMax® Version 8, click yes, otherwise click no. During the sync, information will appear on the screen letting you know what step of the process you are on. After the sync is complete, you will be prompted with the Migrate Special Options Data screen which you can read more about below. Step Three (Optional): You can remove any old Database objects that will no longer be used by TCMax® by clicking the Remove Old Data button.

Migrating from Microsoft® Access Migrating from Microsoft® Access is no longer an option in Version 9.8.7853 and higher of TCMax®. If you do not see this option available and are trying to migrate, contact our Customer Support Center (419) 442-7676 for additional assistance. If you are using a Microsoft® Access Database select the Microsoft® Access radio button and then click the Browse button which will bring up a Windows Explorer window that can be used to navigate to your Microsoft® Access Database. Find and select your Microsoft® Access Database and click the Open button on the Explorer window. This will put the file path in the Source Database area. Click the Set Destination button to set your destination. After you have chosen your Microsoft® Access Database and your destination SQL Database you would proceed to Step One: Transfer Access Database to SQL Server. This process requires you to have SQL Server Migration Assistant (SSMA) installed on your computer. This is part of the complete TCMax® Version 9.X installation but can also be installed separately by going to Microsoft’s website and downloading the installer. A temporary copy of your Database is made, and that copy is the one that is interacted with, so no changes will be made to your Access Database. This process also requires some form of the Microsoft® Access Database Engine which can also be downloaded and installed by going to Microsoft’s website. Transfer Access Database to SQL Server​ Once you click the Transfer Access Database button, TCMax® will launch a command window (below) which will show text explaining all of the things it’s doing but you will need to interact with it once it stops and has a green line of text. If There Are Errors​ If you don’t see the screen below, the import process completed without any errors and you can skip to Step Two: Verify Source Database. If you see the screen below, SSMA failed to bring some of the Data over from Access. If the errors contain text stating that a key column does not allow DBNull.Value, you can click the Attempt Automatic Repair button at the bottom of the window. info This can only be done if you have Microsoft Office 2010 or higher installed on this machine. Otherwise, contact Soaring Software Solutions, Inc for help. When you click the Attempt Automatic Repair button, TCMax® will display a message explaining this process and when you click OK it will attempt to tell Microsoft® Access to Compact and Repair the temporary copy of your Microsoft® Access Database which should remove the records without primary key values. Microsoft® Access will ask you to enter your Database Password. Depending on your operating system and Windows setup you might not see this password input box. If you just see a spinning wheel / wait cursor try hitting Alt + Tab until you find the password input box. It will not be displayed on your taskbar but should look like the image below. Once the Database Password has been correctly input and you have clicked OK you will see the black command prompt window again. It should stop on the green line of text and you’ll have to enter your password once again. If you still see the SQL Server Migration Assistant Errors window, contact Soaring Software Solutions, Inc for help. Step Two - Verify Source Database: Once SSMA has moved all of your old Version 8 Access Data into temporary tables in your new Database you can proceed to Step Two which is Verify Source Database. Clicking the Verify Source Database button will allow TCMax® to verify that the old Microsoft® Access Data is complete and ready to be synchronized. Once this step has completed proceed to Step Three: Sync Data. Step Three - Sync Data: At this point you can click the Sync Data button to move the Data to your Microsoft SQL Server® Database. During the sync, information will appear on the screen letting you know what step of the process you are on. Step Four (Optional) - Clear Old Data: You can remove any old Database objects that will no longer be used by TCMax® by clicking the Clear Old Data button.

During the Migration process, a Migrate Special Options Data window will appear. This window is used to let us know how the Data needs to be copied based off of the options you were using in Version 8 of TCMax®. Select the Shop Code(s) that you would like to run the tool against and click the Migrate button under the Special Options that you were using. Once this is finished you can click the Close button to close this window and return to the Import/Export screen. note Regardless of how you have brought new Data into your system, if you did not import information into an already existing/selected shop code you will need to select the newly imported shop code from the Settings > Sites and Shops screen to have visibility of the items.

Printer Settings is located from File > Printer Settings. tip If you are using TCMax Version 9.7.7202.16222 or older then Printer Settings will be located from Settings > Options > Labels and Printers.

The Printer Settings area is used to point TCMax® to the correct printer. There are options for Label Printer, Page Printer, and Receipt Printer. As long as proper drivers are installed and the computer can see the printer, TCMax® will have the printer available from the dropdown. Label Printer – The printer that is used when printing labels such as User and Item Barcodes. Page Printer – The printer that you will send all reports to. Receipt Printer – The printer used when printing item receipts.

The Label Definition area is where you can set / configure your label definitions. If Modify Label Definition is selected, you will be taken to a Label Configuration screen. From the Label Configuration screen, TCMax® will display three tabs, Label Definition, Page Layout, and Barcode / Label. Label Definition​ The Label Definition tab allows you to select a predefined label definition or save a definition file. The Load From File button can be used to select a predefined label definition (saved into your C:\Users\Public\Documents\TCMax\Label Definitions folder by default). We distribute several label definitions for the most popular printers and label sizes used with TCMax®. The Save To File button allows you to save a label definition you create or alter to the same location. Page Layout​ The Page Layout tab allows you to define the unit of measure for the labels, the margin range, and if printing full pages, the columns, rows, and distance between the two. Barcode / Label​ The Barcode / Label tab allows you to adjust the label and barcode settings.

The Label Details area is where you set what information will be printed where on your label with respect to the barcode that’s printed. Select the field of information you want to be printed from the dropdown box in the position you would like that Data to appear on the label.

Print Item Label is located from File > Print Item Label or by hitting Ctrl + P on your keyboard. This will print a barcode for the item currently displayed on the Main Screen. The Item Label will be printed out of the selected Label Printer in Printer Settings.

Print User Label is located from File > Print User Label or by hitting Ctrl + Shift + P on your keyboard. This will print a barcode for the user currently displayed on the Main Screen. The User Label will be printed out of the selected label printer in Printer Settings.

Print Current Work Location Label is located from File > Print Current Location Label. This will print a barcode for the work location currently displayed on the Main Screen. The Current Work Location Label will be printed out of the selected label printer in Printer Settings.

There are two ways that Data can be added into the TCMax® Database. The first method is entering the Data manually and this is covered in the next paragraph. The second method is by importing your Data using the ‘TCMax Items Spreadsheet’ directly into the Database. The instructions for this method can be found in the Excel Import section of this manual. To add a new item in TCMax® you must be in Issue/Turn-In mode. There are 3 ways you can manually add items into the system; scan an existing Barcode, type in the desired Barcode, or let TCMax® assign the next available Barcode for you. If you have a scanner and the item already has a Barcode on it that you want to use, you can scan that Barcode into the main input box. You can also type in the Barcode Id value that you want to use for this new item into the main input box and hit the Enter key on the keyboard. Another option is that you can setup the Barcode Id configuration you would like to use in Settings > Options > User and Item Barcodes. Once configured, you can hit the F3 key on the keyboard every time you want to add a new item. When using any one of these methods, TCMax® will say 'New Item' and populate the Barcode Id field on the right-hand side of the screen with the Barcode that was input. tip To cancel a new item that was created by mistake, hit the ESC key before completely filling out the new item information. You should also see that all the other fields are open and editable on the right-hand side of the screen, so you can now enter the additional information about this item. All the fields on the different tabs (Quantity & Status, Inspections, Additional Details, etc.) are also editable so you can record any inspections this item has or attach files/photos for the item as well. Once you have recorded the information needed, click the Save button in the upper right corner of the screen. tip If you do not have all information available that you would like to record about the item, you can go back and edit the item later.
documents.s: Adding and Deleting Items in TCMax®

documents.t: Items can be assigned to a kit by entering in a Parent Barcode Id. As an example, let’s say you have a torque wrench (Barcode Id 114 in the ‘Demo’ Database) that you store in a toolbox (Barcode Id 120). If you put the toolbox’s Barcode Id (120) in the Parent Barcode Id box of the torque wrench, you have added the torque wrench to the toolbox, creating a kit. You can have an unlimited number of child items in any toolbox or kit. Appropriate warnings will be given if any item is missing, imminent/overdue calibration, or imminent/overdue inspection when the parent kit is entered on the screen. You will want to assign a toolbox/kit its own Barcode Id. Items in that box will have their own Barcode Id’s. For any items that are located within the toolbox, place the toolbox’s Barcode Id in each item’s Parent Barcode Id box. See the Kit Builder section of the manual for ease of use with larger kit configurations. Parent/Child relationships apply to many things other than simple toolboxes. A building for example could have individual rooms or floors acting as a parent and all items in that room or floor are children. Shipping/storage containers, trucks, fire department apparatus, warehouses, anything that other stuff is stored in can be setup with parent/child relationships and then be easily inventoried or managed from within TCMax®.
documents.s: Parent-Child Relationships with Items or Kitting

documents.t: Whenever a parent item is issued that generates an overdue or missing warning due to one of its children, a Child Details tab appears on the bottom portion of the item information area. Clicking on this tab will display a list of all those items that caused the warning. Any item that caused a warning will be listed with the reason why and the items information.

To delete items from the Database, navigate to the Item Search screen. Click File > Enable Editable Item Search. The row and column headers that are editable will turn green. You can use the search boxes in the top portion of the screen to locate the item(s) that you wish to delete. Once you have located the item, click in the green row header on the left-hand side to select the entire row, then hit Delete on your keyboard. The item has now been deleted.

To add a Course in TCMax® you must be in one of the Course Modes of Operation, Training Completion or Add / Remove Training. Adding a Course to the Database is quite easy and very similar to adding an item. Either type or scan the Course Id you would like assigned to the Course in the input box. The value entered will follow the same character count settings that are in place for items and users (Settings > Options > User and Item Barcodes). The value you enter in the input box, if available, will be assigned as the Course Id. If the Course you are adding is a Child Course you can enter the Parent Course’s Id into the Parent Course Id: field. The Course can also be provided a Name, Number, and Internal. If the Course is used to certify any item(s) you can enter the item’s Part Number(s) into the Part Number column under Part Numbers to Certify. You may also enter a training interval (based on days) in that grid if the certification is annual or repeating. The Certify Part Numbers based on Child Course Completion option will apply the certifications only if the Child Courses have been completed. The Curricula section is an area where you can describe the Course, i.e. goals, topics/skills covered. When you are satisfied with the Data that has been entered, you can click the Save button to save the Course. You can view the full guide by checking out our Modes of Operation Training section.

To delete a Course in TCMax® you must be in one of the Course Modes of Operation, Training Completion or Add / Remove Training. Navigate to the Course Search screen. Click File > Enable Editable Course Search. The row and column headers that are editable will turn green. You can use the search boxes in the top portion of the screen to locate the course(s) that you wish to delete. Once you have located the course, click in the green row header on the left-hand side to select the entire row, then hit Delete on your keyboard. The course has now been deleted.

By default, TCMax® differentiates between a user and an asset based on the length, or character count of the Barcode Id used to identify it. The default character lengths for User Barcode Ids are 2, 5, 16, and 18 characters. Any other character count up to 50 characters will be considered an asset. For example, “01” is considered a user because it has 2 characters, the zero and the one. We recommend using Id numbers that may already be assigned to your employees or barcodes that they may have on company Id badges. The 5-digit CAMS number assigned to many USAF aircraft maintenance troops as well as the 16-character barcode on the front of any DOD Common Access Card (CAC) or the 18-character barcode on the back of any DOD CAC are a few popular examples. Barcode Ids can be alpha-numeric or any desired character length that you would like to use. For configuration adjustments, go to Settings > Options > User and Item Barcodes tab and consult the User Id Configuration section of this manual. Now we are ready to add you as a user. Type the desired Barcode Id and hit the Enter key on the keyboard or scan the physical barcode of the user in the input box. TCMax® should say, 'New User' and a User Details screen will populate. Type your name into the Username field (we recommend using the Last, First M format) and hit the Enter key or select the ‘Save’ button. You are now in the system and are ready to be issued assets, this is all you need to do to add individuals who do not need to login to TCMax®. If you’re going to be set up as an administrator or tool crib attendant, you’ll need to give yourself a password and some permissions, which we will outline in the next section. tip To cancel adding a new user that was created by mistake, hit the ESC key or Cancel button before clicking Save.

The ability to access different aspects of the software is determined by the permissions a user has assigned. Once a user has been added into TCMax® they can be assigned a password (required if the user will log-in to TCMax®) and permissions. Permissions and passwords are assigned via the User Setup screen, accessible by selecting Settings > User Options from the menu bar. Select the user from the dropdown in the top right corner or enter their Id number in the User Id field and hit the Enter key. Once a user has been selected, they can be assigned permissions and/or a password. Below is a view of what the default Admin has as permissions and this is what we recommend for a full administrative permissions set. To set a user’s password put the cursor in the Password box and Enter the desired password, you will see the box populate with dots as the password is entered. Once the password is input, hit the Enter key and type the password again in the Confirm Password box. You will see 'Match' in green text, when this is done successfully, hit the Enter key again. Hitting the Enter key again will set the Password and you will see text that states, 'Password is Set'. Click the Save button in the lower right corner of the screen to save the changes you have made.

From the Main Screen of TCMax® hit the F12 key or go to File > Log In/Out. The Login box will appear, and you will be prompted to 'Enter a User Id'. Enter or scan your Id and password then click OK. If you’ve done everything correctly, you should hear 'Logged In'. Remember, passwords are case sensitive so be mindful if your Caps Lock is on. Caps Lock will also affect barcodes that are scanned so keep that in mind as well. You should also see your name in the top left corner of the main screen as 'Logged In'.

note To install the TCMax® software, the person logged into the machine must have administrative privileges that allow them to write to/modify the computer’s registry entries. Version 9.9 and Newer Version 9.8 and Older Upon launching the TCMax® installer you will see the following screen: Select the Next button. Fully read the Software License Agreement and if you agree to its terms, select "I accept the agreement" and press the Next button. Verify the installation directory and select Next. On this screen, you will need to select the type of install you want: Choosing Install All Features will install TCMax®, the TCMax® Dashboard, Microsoft® SQL Server Local DB. Choosing Choose Features will allow you to select only the components you wish to install. Below is a screenshot of the custom install screen: Choose the type of install and select Next. You will be asked if you would like to include Desktop Shortcuts. This includes the TCMax® Asset Management Software and the standalone TCMax® Dashboard. The installer is now ready, select Next to install. Depending on your computer’s User Account Control (UAC) Settings, you may see this window. If you do, select Yes to continue. The TCMax® installation process will begin, you should see the screen below with a progress bar. When TCMax® has been successfully installed, you will see the following screen: Select the Finish button. Upon launching the TCMax® installer you will see the following screen: Select the Next button. Fully read the Software License Agreement and if you agree to its terms, select "I accept the terms in the license agreement" and press the Next button. Verify the installation directory and select Next. On this screen, you will need to select the type of install you want: Choosing Complete will install TCMax®, the TCMax® Dashboard, Lumidigm Device Service (for fingerprint readers), PPC Sync (for use with pocket PCs and TCMaxMobile), and SQL Server Migration Assistant (required only if migrating from a TCMax® Version 8 Access Database, removed after version 9.8.7802). Choosing Custom will allow you to select only the components you wish to install. Below is a screenshot of the custom setup screen: Choose the type of install and select Next. On this screen, you will need to select if you want the TCMax® application to be available to anyone who uses this computer or just the currently logged in user. Once you have made your selection select Install. Depending on your computer’s User Account Control (UAC) Settings, you may see this window. If you do, select Yes to continue. The TCMax® installation process will begin, you should see the screen below with a progress bar. When TCMax® has been successfully installed, you will see the following screen: Select the Finish button. info Due to the intricacies of Windows’ security settings, if the installation stops or fails during the above steps you may need to run the installer as an administrator by right clicking the TCMax® Setup icon and selecting Run As Administrator. You may need to do so even if you have logged into the machine with an administrator’s account.

If you chose to include the Demo Data, you can login using the built-in admin user. The User Id is “01” without the quotes, and the User Password is also “01” without the quotes. If you successfully logged in you should see “Richard A Lederman [Demo Admin] Logged In” if you used the 01 User Id/Password. info If you did not include the Demo Data and if the Database you are connected to does not have an admin user added to the users table already, you will be prompted to create an admin user before we can proceed. Clicking Yes will open the User and Item Barcodes tab in Settings, allowing you to setup how you would like to identify your users. Configure your user settings or accept the default values and then select Save. The "Create Admin User" dialog box will then appear. Enter the name of the user who will be added as an Admin and you will then be prompted to enter a User Id for this user. Finally, you will need to assign a password to the user. Hit the Enter key after you have confirmed your password and then hit the Save button. You will then be presented with the login screen to login with your newly created Admin.

The first time you run TCMax®, you will need to provide connection information for your Database. For users that are upgrading from Version 8, TCMax® no longer supports Microsoft® Access as a primary Database. This new replacement is called Microsoft SQL Server® LocalDB, which can be run on an individual computer. Microsoft SQL Server® LocalDB cannot be shared over a network. For networked installations, you will need to use Microsoft SQL Server®. The following sections will walk you through connecting to whichever Database type you chose.
documents.s: Opening TCMax® for the First Time

documents.t: When TCMax® is first launched, you will be asked to provide Database connection information. If this is a stand-alone install you can select the OK button and TCMax® will attempt to connect to the Local Database file. Version 9.8 and older Version 9.9 and newer If there is not a Local Database in the location specified, you will receive the following message: Select Continue and TCMax® will create the Database files in the appropriate location. To proceed with the setup, you can skip to the Demo Data section of this guide.

tip You may need to contact your IT department or your DBA to provide you with the information necessary to connect to the Microsoft SQL Server® instance. Version 9.8 and older Version 9.9 and newer If you would like to change your connection to an existing Microsoft SQL Server® Database, if available, you can select the drop-down arrow for the Server Name and choose from the list of servers your computer can detect. Otherwise enter the server name. If you’re using a named instance you need to include the name of the instance as part of the Server Name. If you’re using a default instance (SQLEXPRESS or MSSQLSERVER, depending on your license of SQL) you may leave the instance out. You will then want to select the proper authentication mode and Database for that Server. It is not necessary to check the "Save my password" box. In TCMax® Version 9.8 and older, if the drop-down arrow to "Select or enter a database name" appears empty, there is likely an issue with the way the server is configured or the SQL Browser Agent. The bottom line is the connection cannot find any Databases at that "server\instance" location that the supplied credentials have access to read. If you select the drop-down arrow and see your desired Database then the Server has already accepted your credentials. Select your Database and hit Test Connection. Once the connection has succeeded, press OK on the message box then select OK on the Connection Properties window to allow TCMax® to continue.
documents.s: Shared Network Install Using Microsoft SQL Server®

documents.t: If the Database you have connected to has no Data in it, you will be asked if you would like to include Demo Data. The Demo Data contains a variety of item types and a few users to allow new TCMax® users to familiarize themselves with the software in a test environment. You will then be prompted with a box asking if you want to apply your software license. For users that are new to TCMax®, having the Demo Data in the Database will allow you to familiarize yourself with the TCMax® functionality before going live with your own Data. The Demo Data can easily be deleted or disabled when you are ready to start using TCMax® with your own Data.

tip To run the Soaring License Manager, the user logged into the machine must have full administrative permissions as the application makes entries to the machine's registry. If you click Continue, the TCMax® login screen will appear and you can license the software later. note If the software is not licensed before the 90-day trial expiration, you will be presented with the message box below and TCMax® will not open until a valid license has been applied. If you click License, the License Manager window will appear. You will need to click the Add / Modify button which will display the window where you enter your licensing information. Once you have entered all the criteria, you should see a green checkmark to the right of the License Key field. If it is a red “X” then something has been entered incorrectly. Missing License Information If you do not have the required information for this screen or do not have the 25-digit License Key, please contact Soaring Software Solutions, Inc. If everything was entered correctly click the Activate button. Now that your license has been applied, you can click Close. You should then be presented with a message box that says there are “No Shop Codes Selected.” Selecting OK will display the Sites and Shop Codes screen. If you installed Demo Data, you can select the TCMax Demo Shop. If you did not install the Demo Data, you will need to type at least one shop code into the "Create a new shop code" field and click the Create Shop Code button. After adding a shop code, you can click Save and then the Login screen will appear.
