The Existing User Data Migration Manual menu option will direct you to our Version 8 to Version 9 Data Migration Guide. This Manual will assist in the migration process from TCMax® Version 8 to TCMax® Version 9.X.
The Issue/Turn-In Instructions menu option outlines the issue and turn-in process for items in TCMax®.
The Shortcuts menu option will display different shortcuts/hotkeys that are available for use within TCMax®. The Shortcuts menu option can also be access by hitting F1 on your keyboard.
The User Manual menu option will direct you to our digital User Manual that contains different guides, instructions, and information regarding the TCMax® software.
The About menu option will contain several important pieces of information regarding TCMax®. Provided below are the fields of what is displayed on the About menu.
The Build Date field signifies when the current installed Version of TCMax® was published.
The Product Version field is used to identify the current installed Version of TCMax®. The Database Version field is used to identify what Version of TCMax® your Database is upgraded to.
The Licensed To field signifies the company/unit that the TCMax® installation is licensed to.
The Support Id field is an identifier for your company/unit. Often times when reaching out to our Customer Support Department you will be asked to provide your company/unit Support Id.
The Status Code field is used for internal purposes at Soaring Software Solutions, Inc.

The Data Source field is used to identify how your current TCMax® installation is connected. Typically, if connected to a Stand-Alone, Local Database you will see the following information in your Data Source. If connected to a Microsoft SQL Server® you will typically find a bunch of letters or numbers in your Data Source displaying the SQL Server Name.
The Database field is used to identify what TCMax® Database your installation is currently connected to.
The Connected By field is used to identify if your TCMax® Installation is connected by Windows Authentication or SQL Server Authentication.

The Database Location field is often only displayed if the Data Source is set to (localdb)\MSSQLLocalDB as the Database itself is stored locally. When connected to a Microsoft SQL Server®, you will not find a Database Location option as the Database is not stored on the local workstation. Within the About menu, you will also see a Software License Agreement and a Run in Debug Mode option. The Run in Debug Mode option should only be changed when instructed by a Soaring Software Representative.
The Visit TCMax Online menu option will direct you to our Soaring Software Solutions, Inc. website.

Introduction to TCMax® Asset Management Suite. TCMax® is Asset Management and Item Control Software that Talks™. It will help you digitize your tool box, shop, or entire enterprise, ensuring that items or equipment never go into the work area unaccounted for. It virtually guarantees that users will not use uncalibrated items. Its ability to give audio feedback, telling the user exactly what the program has done with the item with a single scan, will reduce costs with minimum impact to the user as they seldom need to look directly at the computer screen, they just scan, listen, and go. It only takes a few minutes to learn how to use TCMax®, permanently eliminating manual paper trails, generating digital Data so you can track all items used, where they were used, and when. Multiple security levels allow you to permit individual users to use all functions and turn in their own items, OR with a couple of clicks require someone else to turn them in verifying the turn in process. Multiple similar items can all have a single barcode and be issued to different users (not for aviation use). Items can be issued individually or marked to be issued in any quantity. Although not mandatory, you should have speakers connected to your computer and listen to the audio prompts to get the highest level of item control.

TCMax® provides an extensive suite of features applicable across a wide range of industries. While the breadth of functionality may initially appear overwhelming, the software remains highly intuitive and user-friendly. Our Customer Support Team is readily available to assist with any inquiries regarding system configuration and to ensure the software is optimally tailored to meet your organization’s operational requirements.

The Add/Remove Training mode of operation allows you to assign training to individual users. Example: if there is a new hire you can assign the specific training, they will need to perform their duties. Once assigned, you can access the Show Assigned Courses screen and that will display all users who have training assigned to them. tip You can create and edit courses in either the Training Completion mode or the Add/Remove Training mode. It is designed so that if you know how to create an item in TCMax® you will know how to create a course.

In the Training Completion or Add/Remove Training mode, start by entering or scanning your desired Course Id and TCMax® will say “New Item”. On the right-hand side of the screen, you will be able to add additional details for this course, such as the Parent Course Id, Course Name, Course Number, and Course Interval (when the course will be due again). You will also be able to add details in the Curricula box and Part Numbers to certify Users on when the course is completed. When setting up a Parent/Child relationship through courses, if you use the "Certify Part Numbers based on child course completion" checkbox, whomever is assigned the training will be assigned the child courses, not the parent course. In order for a user to become certified on the part numbers used within the parent course, all children courses will need completed, not just one.

If this is a parent course that will have individual labs, lectures, or training sessions underneath them you can set this up by doing the following: Step 1: Enter the individual training id into the main input box. TCMax® will say “New Item”. Step 2: Enter the master training course number in the Parent Course Id box (this links this child to its parent course). Step 3: Enter the name of this course in the Course Name box. Step 4: If this course has a specific course number enter it into the Course Number box. Step 5: In the Interval box, enter the number of days until the course will become due again. (Example: If it is a yearly training, you will enter 365) This will be used to set an expiration date on the certification of when the course will be due again to be certified again. Step 6: Click Save note Courses aren’t required to have a master (parent) course.

Step 1: Click on the Course User Defined Date menu option and select the date the training needs to be completed on from the date picker. Step 2: Scan the Id of the User you need to assign training to, TCMax will say 'User'. Step 3: Scan the Barcodes of the Training Courses that you would like to add for this user to later complete. Step 4: TCMax® will say 'Added', this confirms that this User now has training assigned to them. tip You can scan or enter the Course Id in first, followed by each user to add users to a single course one after another or you can enter a user first and scan each course that you want to add for that user. If you want to assign a new course to a new person, hit the ESC key on your keyboard to clear the screen then you can bring up your next user and course in whichever order is most convenient. If you need to view a Report that shows what courses are currently assigned and if/when they were completed, go to Reports > Training and select the desired Report(s). When a User is displayed on the Main Screen before or after scanning a Course Id, the lower left will display courses that are assigned to the User. This allows you to view any courses the user has overdue, coming due, or newly added.

If you have assigned training to a user and they no longer need to receive it, you can easily remove it. Step 1: Scan the Id of the user you need to remove training from. TCMax® will say 'User'. Step 2: Scan the Barcode(s) of the Training Courses that need to be removed. TCMax® will say 'Removed'.

If you need to see a list of what courses have been assigned to users, select Show Assigned Courses from the top menu bar. If you use shifts and organizations, you can use the filters to filter by Shift or Organization. There are also filter options for Certification Shop Code and Certification Organization. You can Add a User Filter to filter specific users out of the grid (When the grid has Enabled filter status selected), filter the grid for only specific users selected in the filter (When the grid has Reversed Filter Status selected). To ignore the filters, you can set your grid to a Disabled Filter Status to view all assigned courses.

To see a list of all courses, select Course Search on the top menu bar. Use the search options to narrow down the grid and find specific courses. You can also Print Barcode Labels for courses directly from Course Search by selecting the course, and with the course highlighted, select Print.

To edit a course, scan the Course Id on the Main Screen and select Edit. You can also go to Course Search on the top menu bar. Find your course and select the course you would like to edit then click "Display selected course on main screen" You can edit multiple courses at one time in Course Search as well. Go to Course Search and select File > Enable Editable Course Search (or press Ctrl + E on your keyboard). When enabling editable course search, any column header highlighted in green is a field that can be edited or modified. Once edits are complete you can Disable the Editable Course Search by unchecking the option in File > Enable Editable Item Search, or pressing Ctrl + E on your keyboard again. You can also just close the Course Search without disabling the editable mode and all changes will still take effect. note The logged in user will need proper permissions to edit a course. If they do not, there will be no available option in the File menu to Enable Editable Item Search. Course modifications are instant. There is no go back or undo button, so double check and verify you are modifying the correct course.

To delete a course, go to Course Search on the top menu bar. Select File > Enable Editable Course Search (or click Ctrl + E on your keyboard). The column all the way to the left with no header will be highlighted green. Search for and locate the course you would like to delete. Select the column all the way to the left that has no header and this will highlight the entire row for the course. Press DEL on your keyboard and the course will be instantly deleted. note The logged in user will need proper permissions to delete a course. If they do not, the column on the left with no header will not be highlighted green, and when trying to select the course and press DEL on the keyboard, no changes will appear. Course deletions are instant. There is no go back or undo button, so double check and verify you are deleting the correct course.
To exit Add/Remove Training mode, go to Mode= on the top menu bar and switch to the appropriate mode of operation.

The Display Only mode of operation is used when you want to display an item on the Main Screen. This mode is often used to edit or view an item(s) and ensure that you do not accidentally issue or turn-in the item. info The hotkey of Ctrl + Shift + D is available which is used to force Display Only when in Issue / Turn-In mode. When Ctrl + Shift + D is pressed, in the input box, <DIS ID =''/> will be entered, which allows for you to enter, inside of the single quotations, the Barcode Id of the item you want to display on the Main Screen. Display Only will always show a red input box. This is an indication that you can not create, issue or turn-in an item from this mode.
To exit Display Only mode, go to Mode= on the top menu bar and switch to the appropriate mode of operation.

Issue/Turn-In is the normal mode of operation and is used for all the issuing and turning in process. When you switch to another mode of operation you can return to Issue / Turn-In by clicking the mode menu option. When you shut down and re-start TCMax®, it always reverts to the default Issue / Turn-In mode (unless an option is checked to have TCMax® start in a different mode). Issue/Turn-in Instructions can also be viewed by pressing next to the input box

Enter or scan a User Id in the input box for the user who is receiving items. When a user is displayed, the Event Log table (lower left quadrant) switches modes and displays all the items that this user currently has issued to them.
documents.s: Step 1: Enter the User Id of the User Receiving the Items

documents.t: Scan or type in the Location that the user is taking the item(s) to.

Enter or scan the Barcode Id(s) of the items the user is taking. If the item’s Issue multiple of this item with single scan check box is checked from the Quantity and Status tab on the Main Screen then you will hear the audio Enter Quantity and an input box will appear on the screen asking you how many items you want to issue. Enter the appropriate quantity and press the Enter key. If the item is not yet issued out, then the audio Issue is heard telling you that the item has been issued. If the item was previously issued and was not properly turned in, then TCMax® responds with the audio Turn In telling you that the item has now been returned. In this case immediately re-scan the item. The Issue audio is now heard, and the item is properly issued. If the item that you are issuing is overdue calibration or has a “child item” that has an overdue calibration, then the Overdue Calibration audio warning is heard. It is followed by the Issue audio if the user the items are being issued to has permission to adjust calibration dates otherwise the item is only displayed. If the item that you are issuing has a “child item” that has already been issued (like a torque wrench sent to the calibration lab) then the Caution-Item Removed audio warning is heard followed by the Issue audio. If the item that you are issuing has an inspection that is overdue, then the Inspection Overdue audio warning is heard. That is followed by the Issue audio if the option has not been turned on to prevent the issue of overdue inspection items. If you have set the warning lead time in Settings > Options for calibrations or inspections to a specific number of days other than zero and this item calibration or inspection date falls into the lead time area (but it is not overdue) then a Calibration Imminent or Inspection Imminent warning appears, and the item can be issued.
After issuing items to the displayed user, hit the ESC key to clear out the current User Id or scan the next user that you need to issue items to.
documents.s: Step 4: Clear User from Main Screen

documents.t: To check in an item, all you need to do is enter the item(s) Barcode Id. If you are turning in items, it is not necessary to enter a User Id (unless Settings > Options > General Options > Turn in Options requires it). While turning in items, if the User Id is first entered then the Event Log table (lower left quadrant) switches to display the list of items that are out. This helps spot items that the user failed to turn in. If you happen to be turning in someone else’s items, then after turning in the first of their items the table will display the list of items still issued to the other person helping to show you if they forgot to give you all of them. Items that have the Multiple items with this same barcode number and Issue multiple of this item with single scan boxes checked as you see below may require a slightly different turn in process. TCMax® must know whose items you are turning in. If you are turning your own items in and your username is on the screen, then TCMax® will default to turn yours in on the Multi-item screen. If you are turning in another user’s items, highlight the row for the user you are turning items in for and click either the Turn-In Selected button (if you need to turn-in items for multiple users) or the Turn-In and Close button (if you are turning items in for one user). note For companies using the wireless scanners with keypads on them (Datalogic Powerscan): The Multi-item screen will attempt to figure out whether you’re issuing or turning in this item. Depending on that decision when the screen opens, the cursor may be in the turn-in box or the issue box. Regardless of which box the cursor starts in, you can enter the plus sign + followed by a number to attempt to force TCMax® to issue more items out. Using a negative symbol – before the number will tell TCMax® you intend to turn items in. If the item is issued to more than one person, you will be asked to select the person whose items you’re turning in but using the + and – prefixes will prevent accidentally issuing or turning items in when you’re not looking at the screen. There is also an option in Settings > Options > General Options > Item Quantity Options to force the cursor to start in the same box each time.

The Receive Inventory mode of operation is used when receiving inventory on existing multi-quantity items. Receive Inventory will always show a red input box. The only action that can be taken while in this mode is receiving inventory to update quantities of an item(s). When you scan or type a barcode, TCMax® will respond with “Enter Quantity”. This quantity will be added to the value in the Qty On Hand and Qty Available fields to give you the total quantity of this item and the text “Quantity Updated” will be displayed in blue above the Main Input Box. When updating quantities in Receive Inventory, you will have the capability to update quantities by units. To do this, when entering a quantity to receive, press the checkbox to ‘Change Qty to Units’ and enter in the number of units you are receiving. info A ‘Unit’ increments the quantity added by the value entered in the Qty in Unit field on the Quantity and Status tab within the Item Details section. For example, in the image below adding ‘2’ will increase the total quantity to '100' (Qty in Unit for this item is set to 50 (Box)). info The Change Qty to Units checkbox can be defaulted within Settings > Options > General Options > Inventory Options - Default receive inventory mode to update quantities based on unit quantity.
To exit Receive Inventory mode, go to Mode= on the top menu bar and switch to the appropriate mode of operation.

The Training Completion mode takes advantage of TCMax® ease of use to assign training to a user and then complete individual courses for that training with one or two barcode scans. tip You can create and edit courses in either the Training Completion mode or the Add/Remove Training mode. It is designed so that if you know how to create an item in TCMax® you will know how to create a course.

In the Training Completion or Add/Remove Training mode, start by entering or scanning your desired Course Id and TCMax® will say “New Item”. On the right-hand side of the screen, you will be able to add additional details for this course, such as the Parent Course Id, Course Name, Course Number, and Course Interval (when the course will be due again). You will also be able to add details in the Curricula box and Part Numbers to certify Users on when the course is completed. When setting up a Parent/Child relationship through courses, if you use the "Certify Part Numbers based on child course completion" checkbox, whomever is assigned the training will be assigned the child courses, not the parent course. In order for a user to become certified on the part numbers used within the parent course, all children courses will need completed, not just one.

If this is a parent course that will have individual labs, lectures, or training sessions underneath them you can set this up by doing the following: Step 1: Enter the individual training id into the main input box. TCMax® will say “New Item”. Step 2: Enter the master training course number in the Parent Course Id box (this links this child to its parent course). Step 3: Enter the name of this course in the Course Name box. Step 4: If this course has a specific course number enter it into the Course Number box. Step 5: In the Interval box, enter the number of days until the course will become due again. (Example: If it is a yearly training, you will enter 365) This will be used to set an expiration date on the certification of when the course will be due again to be certified again. Step 6: Click Save note Courses aren’t required to have a master (parent) course. When displaying a User on the Main Screen before scanning a Course Id, the lower left will display courses that are assigned to the User. This allows you to view any courses the user has overdue, coming due, or newly added.

Click on the Course User Defined Date menu option and select the date the training took place or today's date, if this was just completed. To complete training requirements for a User, scan the User’s Id while in Training Completion mode. Then scan the course(s) that they have completed, after each scan you will hear TCMax® say “Completed.” tip You can scan or enter the Course Id in first, followed by each user to complete Users on a single course one after another, or you can enter a User first and scan each course that user has completed. For Parent courses that do not have the "Certify Part Numbers based on child course completion", if you scan the Course Id barcode for the master (parent) course, TCMax® will automatically update all its child courses to reflect being completed as well. You can also scan each child course individually and when the last child is completed the master (parent) course will reflect as being completed. For Parent courses that have the "Certify Part Numbers based on child course completion" selected, you will need to scan the Course Id barcode for each child course to be completed in order for the certification to be applicable. If you need to view a Report that shows what courses have been assigned and if/when they were completed, go to Reports > Training and select the desired Report(s).

You can use the Training Completion mode to certify Users on items that require certification before use. This is done using the part numbers to certify grid. While editing or adding a course, you can enter an item's part number into the Part Numbers to Certify grid and provide the training interval (the interval being how long the certification lasts). The Certify part numbers based on child course completion option will restrict the completion of a course that has children to only be completed when all the child courses have also been completed. Example: If you have a weapons’ certification it may consist of multiple training courses such as marksmanship and use of force training. A User will not be certified to use the weapon until they pass both (or all) parts of the certification requirements.

If you need to see a list of what courses have been assigned to users, select Show Assigned Courses from the top menu bar. If you use shifts and organizations, you can use the filters to filter by Shift or Organization. There are also filter options for Certification Shop Code and Certification Organization. You can Add a User Filter to filter specific users out of the grid (When the grid has Enabled filter status selected), filter the grid for only specific users selected in the filter (When the grid has Reversed Filter Status selected). To ignore the filters, you can set your grid to a Disabled Filter Status to view all assigned courses.

To see a list of all courses, select Course Search on the top menu bar. Use the search options to narrow down the grid and find specific courses. You can also Print Barcode Labels for courses directly from Course Search by selecting the course, and with the course highlighted, select Print.

To edit a course, scan the Course Id on the Main Screen and select Edit. You can also go to Course Search on the top menu bar. Find your course and select the course you would like to edit then click "Display selected course on main screen" You can edit multiple courses at one time in Course Search as well. Go to Course Search and select File > Enable Editable Course Search (or press Ctrl + E on your keyboard). When enabling editable course search, any column header highlighted in green is a field that can be edited or modified. Once edits are complete you can Disable the Editable Course Search by unchecking the option in File > Enable Editable Item Search, or pressing Ctrl + E on your keyboard again. You can also just close the Course Search without disabling the editable mode and all changes will still take effect. note The logged in user will need proper permissions to edit a course. If they do not, there will be no available option in the File menu to Enable Editable Item Search. Course modifications are instant. There is no go back or undo button, so double check and verify you are modifying the correct course.

To delete a course, go to Course Search on the top menu bar. Select File > Enable Editable Course Search (or click Ctrl + E on your keyboard). The column all the way to the left with no header will be highlighted green. Search for and locate the course you would like to delete. Select the column all the way to the left that has no header and this will highlight the entire row for the course. Press DEL on your keyboard and the course will be instantly deleted. note The logged in user will need proper permissions to delete a course. If they do not, the column on the left with no header will not be highlighted green, and when trying to select the course and press DEL on the keyboard, no changes will appear. Course deletions are instant. There is no go back or undo button, so double check and verify you are deleting the correct course.
To exit Training Completion mode, go to Mode= on the top menu bar and switch to the appropriate mode of operation.

The Update mode of operation allows for updating information on items that have Inspections, Odometer readings, and Hourmeter readings. The Update mode will always show a red input box. The only action that can be taken while in this mode is updating Inspections, Odometer, and Hourmeter readings of an item(s).

The Inspection Update mode is utilized to update inspections for an item. When an item is scanned that has a single inspection, the inspection date is automatically updated to the appropriate value per the inspection settings. If there are multiple inspections assigned to this item, then TCMax® displays a window with a list of the inspections. From there, select the inspections you want to update and click the Update button, or you can update them all by clicking on the Select All button then clicking the Update button. TCMax® will say “Inspection Updated”.

The Odometer Update mode is utilized to update odometer values for an item. When you scan an item, TCMax® will ask you to enter the current odometer value. The Database is updated and if the new value causes an inspection to become overdue, the overdue inspection warning is given.

The Hourmeter Update mode is utilized to automatically update the hourmeter value for an item. When you scan an item, TCMax® will ask you to enter the current hourmeter value. The Database is updated and if this new value causes an inspection to become overdue, the overdue inspection warning is given.
To exit Update mode, go to Mode= on the top menu bar and switch to the appropriate mode of operation.

This feature can be used during a shift change or to transfer the custody of issued items. You can enable/disable this option in: Settings > Options > Display Options > Show the “Item Quick Turn” menu. You may transfer items from a specific user or from a specific location. Step 1: Select the Item QuickTurn @ Shift Change menu option located at the top of the TCMax® toolbar. Once in Item QuickTurn @ Shift Change, scan, select, or enter a User Id / Location for the items in the Transfer Items From section. All items issued to that user or location will appear in the table. Step 2: Enter or Scan the User Id of the person to receive custody of the items in the box labeled Transfer Items To. You may also enter a new location for these items to be forwarded to. If you are manually entering the User Id, you will need to hit Enter on your keyboard after inputting the User id. The User will then be displayed in the Issuing To: section. tip If a User is displayed on the Main Screen, the Issuing To: may already be filled out. If a Location is entered on the Main screen, the Destination Location: may already be filled out. Step 3 (Optional): By default, all items that are not restricted from transferring will be selected. Uncheck the Transfer checkbox located on the left side in the bottom grid to deselect any individual items you do not want to transfer to a different user. There are also Check All and Uncheck All buttons in the upper right corner of the screen for ease of selecting / deselecting multiple items at once. Step 4: Click the Transfer Checked Items button to perform the transfer of custody. TCMax® will play the “Transferred” audio prompt and return back to the Main Screen. info If a User and a Work Location are already displayed on the Main Screen of TCMax®, then that User and Location will be inherited as the Transfer Items To section. tip You can exclude certain part numbers from being able to be transferred by going to Tools > Catalog Setup and checking the Restrict Quick Turn box for the part numbers you wish to exclude. note If any of the items require certification and the User the items are to be transferred to is not certified for them, they will be highlighted in Red from the grid. Hover over the highlighted item and a tool tip will display telling you what is preventing the transfer. You can verify the change of custody by scanning or typing the User Id that these items were transferred to in the Main Input Box on the Main Screen or checking the Show Issued Items screen. That user will be displayed (if scanned) and the issued items grid in the lower left of the screen will show that they have custody of these transferred items.

Selecting the Item Search menu option from the Main Screen allows you to browse your entire inventory across one or more shops. In the Item Search menu, you will notice drop-down boxes that allow you to filter your results and narrow your search. note The search parameters are AND search boxes not OR search boxes, so the more Data that you enter, the more fine-tuned the search becomes.
The File menu option located in the upper left-hand corner will allow you to enter our Enable Editable Item Search mode or Close the Item Search screen.
The Reports menu option located in the upper left-hand corner will allow for the user to generate various reports with the results that are displayed in the table.

Item Search gives the user several search options. These Search Options can be located from the upper left-hand corner of the Item Search screen. Search Options > Look Across All Sites will include all sites and shops in its search results. Search Options > Load Grid with Blank Search Criteria will display the first 5000 results without any search criteria and allow you to filter the results. By default, when the Load Grid with Blank Search Criteria is left unchecked the Item Search screen will display zero results in the grid, because you haven’t searched for anything yet. This is optional due to the potentially heavy load times on this screen with slower networks. Search Options > Save Search Values will save your search criteria when you exit Item Search. This will allow your criteria from the last session to be present the next time this menu option is opened.

The Export to Excel menu option located in the upper left-hand corner will allow for the user to export the results that are displayed in the table to an Excel spreadsheet. tip You can also right-click in the table at any time and send the displayed Data to an Excel spreadsheet.
The Help menu option located in the upper left-hand corner will contain information on Search Filters, Color Legends, Grid Limit, and Viewing Items Issued to Multiple Users.

To utilize the Search Parameters in Item Search, enter text in any of the search fields and hit Tab or Enter. The grid below immediately displays any results that have matching text or checkbox values for that field. Example: Entering Sock in the Item Name box causes the grid to immediately display any items that contain the letters Sock (wildcards are included in all search fields). The Item Search screen also allows you to filter your search by Shop Code(s), Items issued to a specific User, or items issued to a specific Location.

If you want to display an Item on the Main screen, select the Item from the results grid then click the Display selected item on Main Screen button located in the lower right-hand corner of the Item Search screen. The Item Search screen disappears and the Item is displayed on the Main Screen of TCMax®.
documents.s: Display Selected Item on Main Screen

documents.t: If you want to print an Item label, select the Item from the results grid then click on the Print Item Label button located in the upper right-hand corner of the Item Search screen. TCMax® will send the label to your selected Label Printer.

The Total Items button will display the item totals based on what is displayed in the results grid. info The Total Items button will count the total quantity of items in your results, not the total number of barcodes (or unique items). Therefore, multi-quantity items will be counted as more than one single item if you have more than one of that item. Example: If Barcode Id '701' is displayed which is a multi-quantity item (Screws) you will notice when selecting Total Items the total is 100 not 1. The Total Value button will display the cost totals based on what is displayed in the results grid. info The Total Value button will count the total quantity cost of items in your results. Therefore, multi-quantity items will be counted as more than one single cost if you have more than one of that item. Example: If Barcode Id '701' is displayed which is a multi-quantity item (Screws) you will notice when selecting Total Value my cost is $20.00 not $0.20. note Remember the Item Search screen is limited to the first 5000 results, so you may not see a correct total value or item count of your inventory.

To enter the Editable Item Search mode, go to File > Enable Editable Item Search or press Ctrl + E on your keyboard. note TCMax® Users that do not have access to edit or delete items will not see this option in the File menu. When in Editable Item Search, hitting the question mark in the far left-hand column will display the Editable Item Search information box. Provided below will be an example of what the Item Search screen will look like when in Editable Item Search mode.

If you have the user permission Allow Editing of Items then you will be allowed to edit Data from the Item Search screen. To edit an items information, select the cell you wish to edit and begin typing to overwrite the old information in the cell. You can also double click into a cell to change or modify just part of the field. tip If you make any mistakes while editing, hit the Esc key on your keyboard before you change rows to cancel any unsaved changes. Once you change rows the Data has been changed and saved to the Database. note In version 9.10.0 and newer of TCMax®, date fields within Editable Item Search are treated as a text field, where a valid date must be entered.

If you have the user permission Allow Deleting of Items then you will be allowed to delete items from the Item Search screen. To delete an item from the Item Search screen, highlight the row by clicking in the left-most column (this will highlight the whole row in blue) and hit the delete key on your keyboard. warning Before hitting the Delete key on your keyboard make sure that the highlighted row is the row you would like deleted as the change will be instant and permanent.

Selecting the Show Issued Items menu option from the Main Screen or pressing Ctrl + I on your keyboard will display a new screen of all the items that are currently issued out. There are several features from this screen that can help you manage and adjust the view of your issued items. The Shop Code selection box located in the top right-hand corner will allow for you to limit this screen to a specific shop code, or allow you to look across all of your selected shops. info The Issued Items table can be sorted by clicking on any of the column headers and ordering the items either ascending or descending by the value of that column. The Reports menu option located in the upper left-hand corner will allow for the user to generate various reports with the results that are displayed in the table. tip You can also right-click in the table at any time and send the displayed Data to an Excel spreadsheet. The Help menu option located in the upper left-hand corner will contain descriptions on how the different filters are designed to work. The Display on Main Screen button located in the lower right-hand corner will display the item you have selected from the table on the Main Screen. The Show Issued Items screen can be filtered by the user(s) and/or location(s) an item is issued to or by the status of an item. These filters will appear in the Filtered Users or Filtered Locations/Status tables. When the Filter is Enabled, the table will only display items that do not have one of the selected filters applied to them.

To filter out items issued to a User, select the Add User Filter button which will bring up a User Search window. From the User Search window, you can search by the users Username or User Id. Once you’ve found the user(s) you want to filter by, double click on the user in the User Search List or Select the User then utilize the >> to move the user to the Selected Users table. Hit OK on the User Search window and the user(s) you’ve selected to filter by will be in the Filtered Users list. You can quickly check and uncheck individual names in the filtered users list to enable/disable individual filters on the fly. You can also remove a user filter by clicking on the Username to select it and hitting 'Delete' on the keyboard.

The Filtered Locations/Status table can be customized to include any work location you would like. To add a location / status filter, place the cursor into the text box above the Add Location Filter button and enter in the work location / status that you would like to filter by. Once the information is input, click the Add Location Filter button and you will see the Location / Status added to the table. You can also remove the filter by clicking on it in the list and hitting the 'Delete' key on the keyboard. You can apply a color to this filter by right-clicking the color field and selecting a Basic Color or defining a Custom Color. See example below:

From the Show Issued Items menu option you can adjust / select different statuses for the items that are currently issued out. The statuses that are available from this menu option are Broken, Unserviceable, Lost, and Long Term. To mark an item as Broken, Unserviceable, Lost, and Long Term, click in the appropriate row from the results table. Then click the matching status button above the table to apply that status. tip While applying a status to an issued item, you can right-click the statuses (Broken, Lost, Unserviceable, Long Term) to add a log note and include any additional details about the occurrence. info An Item status filter will always override a location filter, so if you have an item that has a filter for both its status and location, the item will display as the color set for the status of the item (Lost, Broken, Unserviceable, Long Term).

The Filter Status button is a three stage button that allows you to adjust the view of your issued items. The Filter Status can be Enabled, Disabled, or Reversed. info By default all items that do not have a filter applied will be displayed.

The Disabled Filter Status displays all issued items regardless of their filters. You will still be able to distinguish the items that have a filters applied to them as they will continue to be highlighted in their filter color.
The Reversed Filter Status will display only the issued items that have a filter applied to them. This will allow you to disregard your non-filtered items.

The Enabled Filter Status will remove all items from the table that have a filter applied to them. To exit out of the Show Issued Items screen click the Close button located in the bottom right corner of the screen or go to File > Close.

From the Reports screen, you will see different options under the Tools menu. The Tools menu will allow for you set the path that reports will be saved to, view where the current location reports are saved, and also allow for you to set your favorite reports for quicker access to them in the future.

To set or modify the report save path, select Tools > Report Path > Set / Modify Report Save Path. A Browse for Folder box will appear allowing you to set the location for where your reports will be saved. To view the current location of where reports are saving to, go to Tools > Report Path > Current Path.

TCMax® allows for Users to save Favorite Reports. This will allow for quicker access to the reports that are most commonly used. To set your favorites reports, select the Tools > Set Favorite Reports menu option on the Reports screen. Once Set Favorite Reports has been selected you will notice that all of the available reports have a checkbox next to their name and there is a Save Favorites button located in the bottom right-hand corner of the screen. To set your Favorite Reports, place a checkmark in the box next to the report(s) you wish to mark as a favorite. Once you have finished selecting the report(s), click the Save Favorites button. Once you save your favorites for the first time, a Favorites tab will appear on the Reports screen. The Favorites tab will display a list of your selected reports.

Report Options give you the ability to adjust various display and caption Data points for many of the built in DoD reports. When each report is selected, you will see a Report Description section listed with a brief description of the report including any grouping, sorting, and/or display options that are available. All reports in TCMax® can be saved in PDF and Excel format. Once you have ran the report there is an Export menu option in the upper left-hand corner of the Report Viewer screen. When you select the format to Export the report to, you will see a File Explorer window pop up. The File Explorer window will be defaulted to the Report Path that is currently configured from Tools > Report Path > Current Path. Provide the report with a name and click Save to complete the Export. Reports in TCMax® can also be printed directly from the Report Viewer screen by clicking the Printer icon located next to the Export feature in the upper left-hand corner.

If you have an approved signature pad connected to your TCMax® system you can electronically sign for any report with a signature parameter. Once you run a report, you will see an Add Signature(s) menu combo box. From the Add Signature(s) menu option you can select what line you would like to sign on by selecting the appropriate supervisor from the selection list. When you do so your signature pad should become active and a Signature Capture section appears below the Report Parameters. You can then sign the report and hit OK on the signature pad. Your signature will be added electronically to the report.

Tools Chits are required when an item has the Needs Chit For Issue checkbox enabled from the Additional Details tab on the Main Screen of TCMax®.

To access Chit Manager, select Settings > Chit Manager from the Main Screen of TCMax®. Chit Manager allows you to assign chits to users for their use in TCMax®. To assign chits, select their name from the Username drop down box or enter their Id number in the User ID field. Once a User is displayed, highlight an unassigned chit from the Unassigned Chits box and click the Add button. If you do not have any chits created, refer to the Creating Chits section before continuing with the next steps. Once a chit is assigned to a User, that User’s Name is placed in the User field of the grid. The grid is located at the bottom of the Chit Manager screen. To un-assign a chit from a User, select their name from the Username drop down or enter their Id number in the User ID field. Highlight the chit you would like to un-assign and select the Remove button. The chit will now be removed from the selected User and their name will be removed from the User field in the Chit Manager grid. Once a chit has been assigned to a User it can then be utilized for issue purposes. note If a chit is not assigned to a user, the first time a chit is used to issue out an item to a user, it becomes assigned to that user.

To add a new Tool Chit to your system, enter the Id for the chit in the New Chit Id input box. The name of the new chit can be entered in the Chit Name field. When all the information for the new chit has been entered, select the Add New Chit button.

To delete a Tool Chit from your system, refer to the Chit Manager grid. Select the row of the chit you wish to have deleted. Once the chit is selected, press Delete on your keyboard. The chit will then be removed from the Chit Manager screen. info From the Chit Manager, you will see an option that states Ignore User Assignments. This option allows for any chit to be used by any User in TCMax®.

To access Dashboard Limits, select Settings > Dashboard Limits from the Main Screen of TCMax®. The Dashboard Limits / Captions Configuration screen allows you to set the captions and warning thresholds for the Dashboard’s Status Trackers.

To change the captions, select the word(s) you want to modify and enter the new caption. info When captions are modified it does not alter the information they display. For example, no matter what you change the caption to, the Overdue Inspections tracker will always show items with Overdue Inspections.

To change the warning limit, click in the box to the right of the caption and enter a number. This will then give a visual and verbal warning, so your attention is brought to the threshold being monitored. Once you are finished, you can click Save to apply the changes.

Dashboard Limits are recognized within the Status Tracker tab of the Dashboard. When a Dashboard Limit has been met the specific subcategory under the Status Tracker will be highlighted red. When a Dashboard Limit has been met TCMax® will also play an “Attention” audio prompt when each of these limits have been triggered (This can be disabled within Settings > Options > Dashboard Options). If you want to create new Status Trackers that pull specific information you must create your own by going to Tools > Custom Tracker Builder.

TCMax® offers a standalone application called the TCMax® Service Installer (available through our website) that when configured correctly on a Server, allows for emails to be generated and sent off once triggered. This can range from daily reports to when specific items or users perform tasks. In order to setup your emailer once the Sync Console has been properly configured on the host, navigate to Settings > Email Options. The Data entered in these fields will be Shop Code specific unless certain options are enabled. note The emailer will only work with email servers configured to use SMTP.

Start by selecting the category you would like to setup automatic emails for. When expanding the category you will see the settings for the recipients along with other options such as Subject Line, Message, and Occurrence, Part Number, Report etc. The following image shows the details and options within the Calibration category. Based off of the above settings, an email will be generated every Monday morning at 7:00 AM Local Time, warning the recipients of calibrations that will be due within the next 7 days.

To choose the recipient(s), select the box Select Email Recipient(s) and a new window will display, allowing you to select from already established email addresses associated with your users. Simply select the email(s) you wish to assign to the trigger and move them to the right box by selecting the button. Adding New Emails​ If you would like to provide an email that is not a current user in the Database, you can do so by selecting Add New Email. Once you are satisfied with the email addresses associated with the trigger. Select Accept to return to the Emailer Configuration window. You have now successfully set-up your first email trigger. You may set up as many as you would like.

Several of the email triggers have Part Number settings that can be implemented. In the grids that contain the Part Number and warning level, you can set it so that you will only be notified of a Part Number’s status if the number of items associated with the Part Number entered has reached the warning level. The Only send an email for the following part numbers checkbox will cause the emails to be sent out only for the Part Numbers entered into the grid that exceed the warning level. info Part Numbers are not required, and if the checkbox to Only send an email for the following part numbers is left unchecked than an email will be triggered for all items being marked as lost, broken, etc.

Several of the email triggers have a schedule that can be implemented. In the Email sending schedule you can configure when and how often an email gets sent regarding the trigger. info By not providing an Occurrence, you can configure an email to be sent one time on the date and time of your choice.
The Lost Category will send out emails concerning items that get marked as Lost.
The Broken Category will send out emails concerning items that get marked as broken.
The Unserviceable Category will send out emails concerning items that get marked as Unserviceable.
The Long Term Category will send out emails concerning items that get marked as Long Term.

The Reorder Category will send out emails concerning items that have dropped below their reorder quantities. The emails can be sent out either at a specific time of day or periodically, depending on which option you select.

The Issued Items at End of Shift Category will send out emails concerning items that remain issued out to a user once the end of their shift has elapsed. For this to be effective you must be using the shift feature in TCMax® found by going to Settings > Shift Setup from the Main Screen. You must have the shifts created, assigned times. and the employees must be assigned to a shift. You can set the amount of time after the end of the shift to send a warning email to the relative user and the amount of time after the end of shift to send out emails to the designated recipient(s).
documents.s: Issued Items At End of Shift

documents.t: The Calibration Category will send out emails concerning items that are overdue for calibration or becoming overdue within a window of days.
The Inspection Category will send out emails concerning items that are overdue for inspections or becoming overdue within a window of days.
The Transfer Alert Category will send out emails concerning items that have been transferred either into or out of the Shop Code that the email has been set up for.

The Secure Inventory Category will send out emails concerning items that work in conjunction with CompX® locks provided by TCMax® Systems to notify the user about unauthorized access and unsecured closures of the lock system.

The Custom Reports Category can send user generated reports as emails if the report requires no input from the user (parameters). You can select the report you would like emailed from the list on the left side of this section and input the recipient and email information in the appropriate areas. You can then set the date and time for the initial email as well as the schedule for the email. This section also allows you to Add Event(s) for the trigger. Allowing you to have a set schedule along with immediate attention after a specific trigger occurs.

info Available in TCMax® Version 9.8.9314.18668 or newer. An IUID Data Matrix (Item Unique Identification) is a two-dimensional barcode used by the U.S. Department of Defense (DoD) to uniquely identify assets that are in compliance with the MIL-STD-130N. These matrices compactly combine multiple data regions—such as issuing agency code (CAGE), part number, serial number, etc. into a single barcode that ensures unique identification and traceability of items across their entire lifecycle.

To access IUID Item Field Configuration, select Settings > IUID Item Field Configuration from the Main Screen of TCMax®. By default, a preconfigured mapping will exist for PNO → Part Number within the TEI Format. Select your format type to configure the mappings. TCMax® supports formats 5 (AI: Application Identifier), 6 (DI: Data Identifier), and 12 (TEI: Type Entity Identifier). These formats are outlined in the MIL-STD-130N Change 1.

Once a format is selected, selecting Add will display a new window allowing you to add new mappings. When creating new mappings, input the region you want mapped from the IUID Barcode as the Data Qualifier and select the field you want that mapped to in the Item Field drop down. Selecting OK will add the newly mapped region to the Configure tab list, example SEQ → Serial Number. Below is a screenshot of the Configure tab with the newly added SEQ (Serial Number) Data Qualifier.

IUID Data Matrices can be verified and decoded by scanning the barcode using the Validate tab. Below is a sample IUID barcode: When the sample IUID barcode is scanned into the Validate tab from the Configure IUID Map screen in TCMax®, we will display the decoded input value and the validation results of what is embedded into the barcode. You can see the UII (which we use as the BarcodeId) and the three regions available for mapping (CAG, PNO, SEQ).

To delete an IUID Data Qualifier, use the drop-down menu to select the Format you need to delete from. When the Format is selected, select the specific Data Qualifier you wish to delete. This will highlight the line item. Hit Delete on your keyboard. This will produce a popup stating "Confirm Delete. Are you sure you want to delete this item?". Select Yes. This will remove the Data Qualifier.
documents.s: Deleting a Configured IUID Data Qualifier

documents.t: The Lock Configuration is used to configure the setup of the lock types and what user(s) can access the lock(s). The setup for Lock Configuration can be found from the Main Screen of TCMax® by going to Settings > Lock Configuration. A user must have the "Access TCMax, Lock, and Dashboard Options" permission enabled to utilize this feature. info ATC Sync is a depreciated feature that is still accessible for uses who have the older-generation Sync device. This feature will only work with the older-generation Sync, which is no longer sold.
The Hardware section can be used to select what type of lock you are using. The configuration options will change based on your selection.

When selecting any of the Snap-on locks, you will need to enter the proper baud rate for your lock and the comm port that it is connected to. To ensure your settings are correct, you can click the Test Connection button.

When selecting the ekPROTRACK lock, the connection configuration screen will change. TCMax® can automatically detect and configure the connection for this lock type. Clicking the Add Connected Lock will prompt the user to setup the lock on the Lock Setup tab.

When configuring a lock, whether it is new or existing, the user can change what Shop Code the lock belongs to, the name of the lock, manual configuration of the lock, the lock type, and the lock timeout. Lock Types can be created and configured to allow for controlling the access of a lock to a specific list of users. A Lock timeout can be set to close the lock automatically after the designated time has passed.

Users' lock access is managed in one of three ways: lock type (pre-configured user list), individual access (specific user list per lock), or open access (open to all users). A) - Lock Type​ Use this section to configure users' access to the selected Lock Type. Click the Add User(s) button and use the User Search screen to configure the Selected Users list. You will be able to search for the User(s) you would like to add by Username or User Id. Move the desired User from the User Search List to the Selected Users list. Once all Users are added for this lock type, click 'Ok'. B) - Individual User​ To assign individual users to a lock, select the lock from the list on the left side of the Lock Configuration Screen. Click the Add User(s) button on the User Access tab. You will be able to search for the User(s) you would like to add by Username or User Id. You will be able to search for the User(s) you would like to add by Username or User Id. Move the desired User from the User Search List to the Selected Users list. Once all Users are added for this lock, click 'Ok'. C) - All Users​ To allow open access to the lock, select the lock on the list on the left side of the Lock Configuration Screen. Select the User Access tab and check the box to “Allow all TCMax® users to access the selected lock.” in section C).

The Audio Prompts tab is used for customizing the audio/verbal prompts in TCMax®. The Audio Prompt tab allows you to set what audio is played after different interactions within the software. The Audio Language dropdown box allows you to select what language audio files will be used in or to disable the sound functionality altogether. Each audio prompt has two options for what will be played, either Use Text To Speech or Use Audio File. The Use Audio File option will play a wave file that is stored in your C:\Users\Public\Documents\TCMax\Audio folder that corresponds to the given action. You can use any wave file for audio prompts. As long as you can Browse and can see that wave file, it can be used. The Use Text To Speech option is a new addition and allows you to type in what you would like the prompt to say in the text input box and to select the voice used (depending on your version of Windows). Once you type in an audio prompt you can click the Play Sample to play the audio file as a preview. note The text to speech functionality uses the speech engine provided by Microsoft in their Windows OS, depending on what operating system (OS) you are using voices may sound different from machine to machine.

For example, the TMDE field in TCMax® can be used to play a .wav file. As an example, one customer has a “52 Card” inspection signature due on certain items. Edit the “TMDE” caption to “52 Card” from the Captions and Presets Tab. From the Audio Prompts tab, locate the Item Prompts section. Once in the Item Prompts section, find the TMDE Prompt. In the TMDE Prompt section, you can utilize the text to speech option and type in what you would like to hear. Or you can create your own audio file then click the Browse button and navigate to that wave file. Once those changes have been made, press Save. Now any item with the TMDE checkbox will automatically have the .wav file played when the item is either issued or turned back in.
documents.s: Example of Customizing Wave Files for Certain Items

documents.t: The Captions and Presets tab will provide different captions that can be customized along with different preset options that can be selected and customized.

From the Captions and Presets tab, you will have the capability to customize the default captions in TCMax®. The captions can be changed by editing what you see in the text box next to the caption, once those changes have been made, they will then be displayed throughout the software upon save. Not all captions in TCMax® can be customized, but a wide variety can be customized. Provided below will contain the different field captions that can be modified. info Changing the caption will not change the functionality of the field; it will only change how that caption is displayed.

TCMax® has several preconfigured option sets that have been developed over years of interactions with our customers. The preset buttons, when clicked, will apply the options and captions set that we have found to be the most standard amongst specific types of installations.

As the options and captions in TCMax® are stored and referenced on your local machine, if you would like to save your captions and options for later or for easier Deployment across multiple machines you can load, create, delete, and save your custom presets by using the corresponding buttons. info Presets can be automatically loaded against specific Shop Codes to maintain standardization on server hosted Databases by configuring Auto Load Presets.

The Custom Captions tab allows you to edit the captions for the CheckBoxes, TextBoxes, and ComboBoxes that are available on the Main Screen from the Custom tab. This allows for additional details to be added to items that may not already be available within TCMax®. In addition to modifying the captions from the Custom Captions tab, you can also enter values that you want displayed for the two ComboBoxes that are available. If the Custom tab is utilized in TCMax®, one of the advantages is an audio (wave) file is available and can be played whenever an item is issued if any of the CheckBox options are checked. This works as all the other audio files work. On the Audio Prompts tab, under the Item Prompts section in blue, there are audio prompt settings for the User CheckBox values from this screen. These audio prompts will play when interacting with items that have the corresponding checkbox checked.

Enable Fingerprint Scanner​ Enable the use of our fingerprint scanner within TCMax®. When this option is enabled, you are presented with options as to how the fingerprint scanner will operate as well as a new tab to assign fingerprints to users within User Options. Match Threshold​ The match threshold dictates how many points on your fingerprint need to match up with the fingerprint record in the Database. Secure is the most secure option as it matches up the most points. The Convenient option can speed up the fingerprint recognition process since it does not need to match up as many points. Spoof Detection Level​ The spoof detection level protects against someone taking a picture or image of your fingerprint and using it to gain access to the system. Secure offers the most protection while convenient will read and process more quickly. Usage Type​ The usage type dictates how the fingerprint scanner will operate within the system. Verification mode will ask you for a fingerprint instead of a password on the various log-in screens. Identification mode will use your fingerprint as both your user id and password on various log-in screens. This mode works in conjunction with the F2 shortcut on the Main Screen. Use Fingerprint Authentication for Issue Turn-In​ This option will allow you to use the fingerprint scanner to display users on the Main Screen for the issue/turn-in process.
Serial Port Barcode Scanner is Connected On​ To use a serial port scanner, you must indicate the comm port that the scanner is connected to in this field.
Display Weight in Metric Units​ This will display weights in metric units throughout various parts of TCMax®.

The User and Item Barcodes tab tells TCMax® how to process scanned inputs and how to decide whether you are entering an Item Barcode or a User Id.

From the Barcode Id Configuration section, you will see Primary and Secondary Prefix and Suffix values. The Primary and Secondary Prefix and Suffix are used as a shortcut on the Main Screen to create new item Barcode Ids with a single keystroke. TCMax® will use these values to find the next available Barcode Id, keeping the newly created items in sequential order. The Prefix value can be alpha/numeric. The Suffix value must be numeric only. info The Suffix is how TCMax® will increment to find the next available Barcode Id, TCMax® cannot increment alpha characters. Once a Primary or Secondary Prefix and Suffix is set, the hot keys to create an item on the Main Screen can be utilized. The F3 key can now be utilized to create a new item from the Primary Prefix and next available Primary Suffix. The Ctrl + F3 key can now be utilized to create a new item from the Secondary Prefix and next available Secondary Suffix. Partial barcodes can be generated as well by hitting the F9 key from the Main Screen. TCMax® places the Prefix from the Primary barcode sequence in the Main Input box so you can type your own Suffix. Hitting Ctrl + F9 adds the Prefix from the Secondary barcode sequence.

If you want your item Barcode Ids to be all numeric then leave the Prefix box blank. If you want your Barcodes to be six digits long but want to start with the number one thousand, then you should enter 001000 in the Suffix box. If you want to use three-digit Barcodes and want to start with the Barcode Id one, then you should enter 001 in the Suffix box.
documents.s: Example Scenarios of Barcode Id Configuration

documents.t: The User Id Configuration section will provide options on how to specify how users will be distinguished in TCMax®. The User Id Configuration section will provide four different barcode lengths, prefix and suffix values, along with additional configuration settings that can be selected.

User Id Lengths 1-4 are the four different barcode length values that can be filled in to identify the character count of your users. If no additional configuration settings are configured in the User Id Configuration section, this method will be used by default. The number of characters in the User Id must be different than your items in TCMax®. When utilizing User Id Lengths 1-4, when anything is scanned, TCMax® counts the characters. If the length matches any of the numbers in these four boxes, then TCMax® treats it is a user. Anything else will be considered an item. note To only use some of the pre-defined lengths, zero (0) out the remaining fields. For example, if you only want to recognize two-character User Ids then zero (0) out lengths 2 through 4.
documents.s: User Id Length 1, User Id Length 2, User Id Length 3, User Id Length 4

documents.t: This option is used when you use U.S. Military Id cards and have a 2-D barcode scanner. It makes both front and back barcodes read the same value. If you check this box, make sure one of the User Id Length values equal 15.
documents.s: Use first 15 digits of Id card only, U.S. Military

documents.t: This option is used when you use U.S. Military Id cards and the first character on the front and back are different. With this option selected, TCMax® will skip the first character and move on to the second character. If you check this box, make sure one of the User Id Length values equal 15.
documents.s: Use 2 – 15 digits of Id card only

documents.t: This option is used when User Ids begin with the same character(s). When this option is enabled, enter the Prefix your User Ids begin with in the Prefix box. When a user barcode is scanned that begins with the Prefix, TCMax® will treat that barcode as a user, no matter the length of characters.
documents.s: Any Barcode Starting with the User Prefix will be Treated as a User

documents.t: Differentiate Item/User Based on Leading Character allows you to tell TCMax® the first character style of all users and items. Checking the top box, First character Alpha = User,Numeric = Item, recognizes anything scanned that's first character is a letter between 'A' to 'Z' as a user. Anything beginning with a number between zero and nine is recognized as an item. Checking the bottom box, First character Numeric = User,Alpha = Item, recognizes anything scanned that’s first character is a number between zero and nine as a user. Anything beginning with ‘A’ to ‘Z’ is recognized as an item. info The User Id length counts 1-4 will no longer matter when using one of these options, as TCMax® will determine if the entered value is a user or item based on the leading character.
documents.s: Differentiate Item/User Based on Leading Character

documents.t: To check the number of characters in any barcode, click in the box at the bottom of the User and Item Barcodes tab and scan the barcode. Once the barcode has been scanned, the character count will appear to the right in the textbox along with how TCMax® currently recognizes that barcode (item or user).

Available in TCMax® Version 9.8.9116.26749 or newer. The Serial Event Configuration is used to configure the setup of serial devices. The main purpose of this feature is for anyone who wishes to configure issue, turn-in, and user events from the Main Screen and bridge it with a hardware device. A user must have the "Access TCMax, Lock, and Dashboard Options" permission enabled to utilize this feature.
The setup for Serial Event Configuration can be found from the Main Screen of TCMax® by going to Settings > Serial Event Configuration.

To create a Serial Event Configuration, select Click to Edit Event Configurations. This will produce a Serial Event Manager Confirmation screen. Select Add Config. Give the Event Configuration a name in the Event Config Name field; Names must be unique. Once a Configuration is added, you then have the ability to use the default for events or you can adjust the information that will display. info The only information that can be selected for each specific Event is what is listed in the Available Objects under each Event. If information is adjusted and you need to resort back to defaults, there is a Reset to defaults button to go back to the original configuration.
The following Events are available once a Configuration is created: User Logged In User Logged Out User Scanned User Cleared Item Issued Item Turned In

To select an Event Configuration, refer to the Selected Event Configuration section and select the drop down menu to view all Configurations. Choose the Configuration you would like to use. Once the Configuration is selected, you are able to adjust your Com Port, Baud Rate, and Flow Control. Flow Control is a serial communication feature used to manage and configure how data is transmitted through serial ports. By default, we populate any Com Ports we find a connection to or you are able to manually enter a Com Port if you know which one you will be using. When the Com Port, Baud Rate, and Flow Control have been configured, press Done to Save those changes.

To delete a serial event configuration, select Click to Edit Event Configuration. This will produce a Serial Event Manager Confirmation screen. Select the Configuration you would like to delete by choosing it on the left-hand side of the screen. This will highlight the Configuration blue. With the Configuration highlighted, press Delete on your keyboard. When that is completed, select Save for changes to take effect.
Shifts can be setup within TCMax® to further track your employees and records.
To access Shift Setup, select Settings > Shift Setup from the Main Screen of TCMax®.
To create a shift, click the New Shift button and then enter a Shift Name, Start Time, and End Time. To save the shift, select the Save button in the Shift Information section.
To delete a shift, highlight the shift you would like to remove and click the Remove Shift button.

To add a user to a shift, highlight the shift you would like to add the user to, then highlight the user you would like to add to the shift. Once the shift and user has been selected, click the Add -> button to add the user to the selected shift. After selecting the Add -> button, the user will be displayed in the Users On Selected Shift section.

To remove a user from a shift, highlight the user you would like to remove then click the <- Remove button. After selecting the <- Remove button, the user will be displayed back in the Users Without Shift section.
To access Sites and Shops, select Settings > Sites and Shops from the Main Screen of TCMax®.

Shop Codes are used to keep assets organized between separate locations within the same facility. Sites are used to narrow down the scope of Shop Codes and Users that can be viewed on a particular workstation. Often times Sites are used when the TCMax® Database is shared across multiple facilities within the same organization.

From the Sites and Shop Codes screen, refer to the Selected Site section. In the Selected Site section, refer to the Create a new site textbox. Type in the preferred name of the new Site then hit Enter on your keyboard or press Create Site. Upon pressing Enter or Create Site, your newly created Site will be displayed from the Site to Join dropdown list.

From the Sites and Shop Codes screen, refer to the Selected Shop Codes section. In the Selected Shop Codes section, refer to the Create a new shop code textbox. Type in the preferred name of the new Shop Code then hit Enter on your keyboard or press Create Shop Code (Unassigned) or Create Shop Code (Site). When a Shop Code is added to the Create Shop Code (Unassigned) section then that indicates the Shop Code in which you are adding is not assigned to your selected Site. This will allow the Shop Code to be seen or selected by all Sites in the dropdown. When a Shop Code is added to the Create Shop Code (Site) section then that indicates the Shop Code in which you are adding is assigned to your selected Site from the Selected Site section. This allows the Shop Code to only be seen by the Site it was assigned to. Other Sites will not see this Shop Code info Shop Codes can be moved between the Shop Code(s) Unassigned a Site section and Shop Code(s) Assigned to a Selected Site section by highlighting the Shop Code(s) and using the left ( << ) or right (>>) arrow buttons.

From the Sites and Shop Codes screen, refer to the Primary Shop Code section. In the Primary Shop Code section, refer to the Primary Shop Code drop down box. Select the Shop Code you wish to have as the default Primary Shop Code when the TCMax® application is launched. Once the Shop Code has been selected, you will notice in the Primary Shop Code section an option appears that states, ‘When launching TCMax, start by viewing all of your selected shop codes'. If this option is enabled when the TCMax® application is launched it will view all Selected Shops instead of just the primary shop. Once all desired Shop Codes and Sites are entered and a specific Shop Code is set to the Primary Shop Code, press the Save button located in the bottom right-hand corner of the Sites and Shop Codes screen.

info If you are using both the Password Options from Settings and the Account Security Policy feature from User Options, passwords must satisfy both options (both validations will be applied). Beginning in TCMax® Version 9.9.0, the Password Options previously located under Settings were removed, and password management is now handled exclusively through the Password Policy feature within User Options.
documents.s: Account Security Policy (formally known as Password Enforcement Policy)

documents.t: To enable Password Policies, navigate to Settings > User Options > Configure. Depending on the specific Version of TCMax® that you are using, you may see Password Enforcement Policy or you may see Account Security Policy. info Versions 9.8.9160.18261 through 9.8.9420.23888 of TCMax® will state Configure > Password Enforcement Policy. info Versions 9.8.9580.24506 or newer of TCMax® will state Configure > Account Security Policy. In Versions 9.8.9160.18261 through 9.8.9420.23888, only a Password Enforcement Policy screen will be available, whereas Versions 9.8.9580.24506 or newer will contain both a Password Enforcement Policy and an Account Lockout Policy. By default, both policies are disabled. To enable either policy, select the appropriate tab then select Enable for that policy.

The Password Enforcement Configuration window allows you to set rules regarding passwords in TCMax®. Minimum Length - The minimum length a password can be. Maximum Length - The maximum length a password can be. Complex Password - Password must contain at least 1 lower case letter, 1 upper case letter, 1 number and 1 special character. Different Characters - Password must include this number of different characters from your last password. For example, if set to 2 and your password was previously 'password1' you could not use 'password2' as that is only 1 difference in characters. Days Until Password Expires - The number of days that may pass before a user is prompted to change their password upon login. Minimum Password Life (Hours) - The number of hours that must pass before a user can change their password. For example if set to 24 then a user cannot modify their password again until 24 hours has passed.

The Account Lockout window allows you to define how the TCMax® software responds when a user enters incorrect login credentials too many times. Number of Failed Login Attempts - Number of failed loin attempts in the minutes defined below before the account gets locked out. When a value of zero (0) is entered, the feature is disabled. Timespan for Failed Logins (Minutes) - Number of minutes to look for failed login attempts before the account gets locked out. When a value of zero (0) is entered, the feature is disabled. Force Reset After User Reactivation - Forces a password reset when reactivating any deactivated accounts.

The Group Setup tab is where you can create user groups and assign individuals to different groups. Groups are typically only used when items are issued to groups of people. Responsibility for those items are shared by everyone in the group.

To create a new group, click the Add New Group button. The following will be displayed after clicking that button. Enter the Group Name and Id Number for the new group. info The Group Id should follow the same character count or prefix rules for employees that were set in Settings > Options on the User and Item Barcodes tab. Once both parameters are entered, click the Add button to add the group to TCMax®.

To add a user to a group, select the user from the dropdown box in the top right. Then, highlight the group from the All created groups grid and hit the Add User to Group button. This will add the selected user to the selected group.
To remove a user from a group, highlight the group in the All created groups grid, click on the user and press Delete on the keyboard.

To completely delete an entire group, highlight the group in the All created groups grid, and press Delete on the keyboard. note Creation, Adding / Removing Users, and Deletion of Groups are not permanent until pressing SAVE in the bottom right corner.

To access User Options, select Settings > User Options. The User Options screen is user dependent and will change based on the User you are currently displaying. Take note of the dropdown box in the upper right-hand corner of the screen, you may select the user you would like to edit from here or scan / type in their User Id in the upper left-hand corner of the screen.
