Access to the User Options screen offers full control over TCMax®. Any user who can access this screen will have the permission to edit all users and assign any permissions to themselves or others. For this reason, it is recommended to use User Profiles to assign permissions to users and limit the users who have access to this screen.

info Fingerprints are utilized when the option Enable Fingerprint Scanner is checked within Settings > Options > Hardware And Third Party Service Options > Biometrics from the Main Screen of TCMax®. The Register Fingerprint tab will only appear if you have a fingerprint scanner attached and the fingerprint drivers are installed. info If the device is connected and proper drivers are installed for TCMax®, but the Register Fingerprint tab is not visible from Settings > User Options, we suggest to restart the TCMax® software for changes to take effect. This screen is used to load an employee’s fingerprints for use with their TCMax® User Id.

To add a user’s fingerprint to the system, enter their User Id in the User Id field or select their name from the Username dropdown box. In Step 1, select the finger you would like to enroll by clicking on the image of that finger. Once the finger has been selected, the Capture button under Step 2 becomes active. Once the Capture button is selected you will be prompted to place your finger on the fingerprint scanner. You will need to scan each finger three times. If there are any issues or errors with the process, you will be notified in the Enrollment Instructions/Details section. Each User can have up to ten fingerprints. For any changes to take effect, you must hit the Save button before exiting the screen.

In order to remove a fingerprint, display the user you would like to remove a fingerprint for in the Register Fingerprint tab within User Options. Mouse over the finger that has a print registered and observe the marker turns to a visible red x. The tooltip off to the right also indicates "Right-click to delete enrollment". By right-clicking the marker you will be given a prompt verifying if you would like to remove the fingerprint or cancel. Select Yes to remove the fingerprint. Fingerprint disenrollment is only needed to remove a fingerprint registration entirely. If you want to update or change a fingerprint simply perform the steps in Adding a Fingerprint and you will be prompted to overwrite the registered print or cancel.

If the logged in user has the Add/Edit/Delete User Accounts permission, the User List tab will be visible. The User List grid can be limited to a specific individual by entering the appropriate information into either the User Id or Username fields.

To change user information, highlight the Data in the field you want to edit and type or scan in the new information. Permissions can be changed by either checking or unchecking the permission’s checkbox.
There are two ways a user can be deleted in TCMax®.
Highlight the row of the user you wish to delete and hit the Delete key on your keyboard.

Right click on the user you wish to delete and select Delete User. Changes or Deletion of Users are not permanent until pressing SAVE in the bottom right corner. note The logged in user, highlighted in gray, cannot be modified.

The User Options screen is user dependent and will change based on the User you are currently displaying as discussed in User Options. This tab is where Permissions can be assigned to individual users. info If you are using Profiles, the Profile will trump individual User Permissions. You will not be able to add individual User Permissions when a Profile is set, but you will be able to see the Permissions that are checked and associated with that Profile.

Allows the logged in user to add new users, hit the edit button above a user’s name on the Main Screen to make changes to the username, and delete users from the User List tab provided they have access to the User Options screen.
Grants the logged in user the ability to hit the edit button above a user’s name on the Main Screen and choose to deactivate the user.
documents.s: Allow Deactivating Users Outside of User Options

documents.t: Grants the logged in user the ability to assign a user profile to a user from the Main Screen. The logged in user cannot assign a profile that contains more permissions than they currently have.
documents.s: Allow Profile Assignment Outside of User Options

documents.t: Makes the user inaccessible on all screens except the User Options screen. This is to prevent a ‘deleted user’ from being re-added to TCMax®.
Grants the logged in user the ability to create items from the Main Screen.
Grants the logged in user the permission to delete items from the Item Search screen when the editable item search option is checked.

Grants the logged in user the ability to edit the unprotected fields of items on the Main Screen using the edit button on the item details side of the Main Screen and editing unprotected fields for items in the item search grid when the editable item search option is checked.
Grants the logged in user the ability to receive deactivated items.

Grants the logged in user the ability to adjust the issued quantity of expendable items within a 30-day period on the issued expendables tab for a user and receive items beyond their restricted limitations (See Settings > Options > Limit the number of items a user can have issued at one time). This permission also allows the override of custody limitations setup in Catalog Setup.
Allows the logged in user to add or edit calibration due dates on an item. This permission is required if a user will receive an item with an overdue calibration.
documents.s: Manage calibrations and allow receiving custody of items with overdue calibrations

documents.t: Grants the logged in user the ability to mark items with Broken, Unserviceable, Lost and Deactivated statuses as well as returning items from those statuses.
Allows the logged in user to create and manage inspections for items as well as receiving items with overdue inspections and the "Prevent issuing if this inspection is overdue" checkbox.
documents.s: Manage Inspections and allow receiving custody of items with overdue inspections

documents.t: Allows the logged in user to update inspections without granting them the rights to add/edit/delete the inspections being updated.
Each of the ‘Access’ permissions in this section grants the logged in user the ability to access those parts of TCMax®.
Allows the logged in user to access the Tools > Catalog Setup screen.
Allows the logged in user to access Training Completion and Add/Remove Training modes under the Mode = options.
Allows the logged in user to access File > Database Maintenance screen.
Allows the logged in user to access the Report Designer and Custom Tracker Builder section under the Tools Menu Option.
Allows the logged in user to access the Settings > Email Options screen.
Allows the logged in user to access the File > Import/Export Records screen.
If the option to restrict reports to those with permission only is checked, allows the logged in user to access the Reports screen.
Allows the logged in user to access Tools > Shop Code Transfer.
Allows the logged in user to access Options > Sites and Shops screen.
Allows the logged in user to access Settings > Options, Settings > Lock Configuration, and Settings > Dashboard Limits.
documents.s: Access TCMax, Lock, and Dashboard Options

documents.t: Allows the logged in user to access Settings > User Options and Settings > User Profile Setup screens.
Allows the logged in user to select different Modes of Operation in TCMax®.
Allows the logged in user to access the Set Work Location Status screen, add work locations on this screen and change the statuses of the work locations on this screen to blocked or unblocked.

Will show the logged in user all shop codes and items for this computer’s selected site regardless of the shop code options selected in Sites and Shops. In Version 9.9.0 and newer, this will show all shop codes across each site the logged-in user is assigned to, regardless of which shop codes are selected on that computer.

Checking this box will prompt the user to create a new password upon next login. This can often be used when setting up a new user who may need to login to TCMax®. You can simply assign them a generic password such as 01 and check this box. This way they can login using the generic password and create their own password privately.
documents.s: Force Password Reset At Next Login

documents.t: Enter the desired password for the user.
Re-type the password and if you see the prompt "Match" press enter again to submit and you will see "Password Is Set".
The remove password button will remove the password from the user. info You will not be able to remove the Password from the logged in User. The remove password will not be available.
The Email Address section is used to assign or remove an email for a user. Emails may be used with our Emailer Configuration add-on with proper setup.
The User Picture section is used to assign or remove a user image.

User Preferred Items Configuration allows you to assign a User a preferred set of items that is displayed in the bottom left-hand quadrant of the Main Screen of TCMax®. The preferred list of items will only appear when the User is displayed on the Main Screen and the appropriate option, 'Display user preferred items when a user is brought up on the Main Screen', is enabled. This option can be enabled from Settings > Options > Display Options.

To assign a User Preferred Items, display a User on the Main Screen of TCMax®. With a User displayed on the Main Screen of TCMax®, navigate to Settings > User Preferred Items Configuration. note If a User is not displayed on the Main Screen when attempting to navigate to Settings > User Preferred Items Configuration it will be grayed out and a message will appear stating 'Please bring up a user to adjust preferred items'. With the Preferred Items screen displayed, you will notice in the Username field that your displayed User appears. To assign Users Preferred Items, click in the Barcode Id field and scan/type in the Barcode Id of the item(s) you wish to add. Upon entering the Barcode Id into the Barcode Id field, you will notice the Preferred Items appear in the grid. Once you are done adding Items to your selected User, press Done from the Preferred Items screen. Upon selecting Done, the Users Preferred Items will now appear from the Main Screen of TCMax® in the lower left-hand quadrant.

To remove a User Preferred Items, display a User on the Main Screen of TCMax®. With a User displayed on the Main Screen of TCMax®, navigate to Settings > User Preferred Items Configuration. info If a User is not displayed on the Main Screen when attempting to navigate to Settings > User Preferred Items Configuration it will be grayed out and a message will appear stating 'Please bring up a user to adjust preferred items'. With the Preferred Items screen displayed, you will notice in the Username field that your displayed User appears. To remove Users Preferred Items, select the item(s) you wish to remove to highlight them then hit Delete on your keyboard. Upon pressing Delete, the item(s) will be removed from the Preferred Items grid.
User Profiles are beneficial when making bulk edits to multiple users and to limit access to the user options screen.
To access User Profile Setup, select Settings > User Profile Setup from the Main Screen of TCMax®.

To create a user profile, select Create New Profile from the User Profile drop down. Once you select Create New Profile, a message box will ask for the name of the profile in which you are adding. Enter the new profile name, then press OK. The user profile will be added to the User Profiles section.

Once a Profile has been added/selected, refer to the bottom half of the User Profile Setup screen. From the bottom half of the User Profile Setup screen, select the permissions you wish for this profile to have. When the desired permissions for the profile have been selected, refer to the Default Password section located in the upper right-hand corner of the User Profile Setup screen. info A password is only required if you intend on users under this profile to be able to login to TCMax®. Enter the desired password for the User Profile. Once the password has been entered, re-enter the password into the confirm password field. If the passwords match you should see green text that states 'Match'. Once you receive 'Match', press enter again to set the password to the User Profile. Upon doing so, you should see text that states 'Password Is Set'. After permissions and a password have been assigned, click the Save button. note Checking the option Default User Profile will automatically cause all new users added to TCMax® to inherit the profile permissions.

To delete a user profile, use the drop-down menu to select the Profile you would like to delete. With the Profile selected from the drop-down menu, select Delete. You will receive a popup stating 'Continue? Deleting this profile will also set all users tied to this back to their standard permission.' Select OK to delete the profile. Once you have selected OK to delete the profile, you will notice the profile has been removed from your drop-down list. Select SAVE in the bottom right corner of the User Profile Setup screen to save the changes.
Once Profiles have been created, they can be assigned to Users from Settings > User Options or the Main Screen of TCMax®.

From the Main Screen of TCMax®, select Settings > User Options. From the User Options screen, select a user and choose the desired profile from the Current Profile dropdown. Once the User Profile has been assigned, select the Save button located in the lower right-hand corner of the User Options screen.

From the Main Screen of TCMax®, display a User you want to add a profile to. When a user is displayed on the Main Screen, a blue edit button will appear above their name. Select the edit button to display the user details screen. This screen will allow you to assign a specific profile from the drop-down list. After selecting the User Profile, click the Update User button. When clicking the Update User button, a login screen will appear to assign an individual to a profile. The credentials entered on the login screen must be for a user who has the same or more permissions, including the permission Allow Profile Assignment Outside of User Options. If you are unsure which users can elevate the selected user to the desired profile, click the Display Users With These Permissions hyperlink to view eligible user logins. note When a user is under a User Profile the permissions set up for that Profile will override the permissions set up for that user in User Options.

To access User Site Assignments, select Settings > User Site Assignments from the Main Screen of TCMax®. Once you have selected User Site Assignments, a Site Manager screen will appear. The Site Manager screen is broken down into two tabs, Users and Sites. info It is not always necessary to manually modify which users belong to which sites. Users that do not belong to a site are automatically added to the site that has been selected in Sites and Shops. If a user is already associated with a site and is scanned into another site, TCMax® will ask to add that person to the additional site.

The Users tab allows you to manage which sites a user is assigned to. Users can be assigned to multiple sites. This allows them to view the working shop codes that are assigned to that specific site. To add users to a site, select the individual user from the list on the left-hand side of the Site Manager screen or use the search fields in the top left-hand corner to filter the list. With a user selected, click the Add To Site button. The Select Sites window will display and allow you to select which site(s) you wish to associate this user with. Once you’ve selected which site(s) to put your user in, click the Accept button. The site(s) that had been selected will now appear from the Selected User Site List from the Site Manager screen. To remove a site from a user, select the user from the User List section. Once the user has been selected, their site(s) will appear in the Selected User Site List section. Select the site you wish to be removed and hit the Delete key on the keyboard. To remove all sites from a user, select the user from the User List section and hit the Delete key on the keyboard. A Remove Sites screen will appear letting you know selecting Yes will remove all sites from the selected user.

The Sites tab manages which users are assigned to the site(s). It performs the same function as the Users tab but is oriented at managing the site rather than the user. To add users to a site, select the site from the Site List located on the left-hand side of the Site Manager screen or use the search field in the top left-hand corner to filter the list. Once you have selected the Site, select the Add User button. This will bring up a search window which assists with user selection. From the User Search screen, enter in the user's name in the Search by Username field or enter the user's id in the Search by User Id field. Any matching records will appear in the User Search List. Once you have the user(s) displayed in the User Search List, double click on the user's name or highlight the user's name and utilize the >> button to add the user to the site. Once your list contains all the users you wish to add to this site, click OK. To remove a user from a site, select the site from the Site List. Once the site has been selected, click on the user's name and hit the Delete key on the keyboard. To remove all users from a site, select the site from the Site List section and hit the Delete key on the keyboard. A Remove All Users screen will appear letting you know selecting Yes will remove all users from the selected site. The Add Organization button adds an entire organization of users to a site. This feature works the same as the Add User button referenced above.
The Additional Details tab allows you to document additional detailed information for your items. Some of these details will allow the item to appear on corresponding reports.
The Notes field can be used to include any temporary item information and can be changed or deleted at any time. This field will also populate on the Comments section of the USAF MIL Report.

The Item Type dropdown box is where you categorize the type of item. The Item Type will affect how the items are issued and turned in and will also affect how items appear on various reports throughout the software.

Item is the default Item Type in TCMax®. Most customers will enter most, if not all, of their items with this Item Type. For USAF customers, the Item Type must be set to Item for it to appear on the MIL reports.

An item marked as Aerospace Coating will require a weight to be entered when the item is issued and turned in, as well as a weight disposed value to be entered upon turn in. With this Item Type selected a Hazmat tab will appear where you can enter additional Hazmat information about the item. Disposable will be automatically checked under the Hazmat tab for any Aerospace Coating items. info You will not be able to uncheck the Disposable checkbox when an item is marked as Aerospace Coating. Each time you attempt to uncheck the Disposable checkbox, it will revert back.
An item marked as Facility Keys will require another person for turn-in purposes. When an item is marked as Item Type Facility Keys the person who took the key cannot be the one to turn it in.

An item marked as Hazmat will require a weight to be entered when the item is issued and turned in. With this Item Type selected, a Hazmat tab will appear where you can enter additional Hazmat information about the item. note The Item Type Hazmat is designed to comply with US Navy Hazmat requirements. USAF customers are advised to enter Hazmat items under Item Type Item and use a custom checkbox to track their Hazmat items.
An item marked as Hose will have a Hose tab available where you can enter additional information for the item. This Item Type is utilized by Fire Departments.

An item marked as Rags will have special steps it undertakes when being turned in. Instead of being returned directly to stock they are first reissued to a dirty rags location and from there they would be sent to laundry. Once they have returned clean from laundry, they can be returned back to stock.
Manufacturer is the name of the manufacturer for the item.
Manufacturer P/N is the Part Number the manufacturer uses for the item.
Date Received is the date when the item came into the Shop.
Contract Number is the number of the contract for the item.
Mobility Increment is the assigned or noted mobility increment of the item. This is mainly seen used in the Military.
Length is used identify the length of an item.
Width is used to identify the width of an item.
Height is used to identify the height of an item.
Weight is used to identify the weight of an item.
The CACRL checkbox signifies the item is a Custodian Authorization / Custody Receipt Listing.
When CACRL is checked, this text field will appear. The CACRL Value is the value of the Custodian Authorization / Custody Receipt Listing.
The Local Manufacture checkbox signifies the item is made by a local manufacturer.
The Needs Chit for Issue checkbox signifies the item will require a chit in order to be issued. This is mainly used by the Navy.
The Password Required for Issue checkbox signifies the item will require a password in order to be issued.
The Precious Metal checkbox signifies if the item is a precious metal.
The Requires Charging checkbox signifies the item will require charging upon turn-in.

When the Requires Charging checkbox is checked, Charge Duration will appear. This is used to enter the number of minutes the item will need to charge in order to be fully charged. This will also prevent the item from being issued if the charge time is not completed from the previous turn-in.
The Requires Control Number checkbox signifies the item will require a control number in order to be issued.
The Shelf Life checkbox signifies the item has a shelf life.
The Spare checkbox signifies the item is a spare item.
The Technical Order checkbox signifies the item is a technical order item.
The TMDE checkbox signifies the item is a Test, Measure, and Diagnostic Equipment item.
When the TMDE checkbox is checked, TMDE Value will appear. This is the item's Test, Measure, and Diagnostic Equipment's value.
The Warranty checkbox signifies the item has a Warranty.
When the Warranty checkbox is checked, the Warranty Expiration date field will appear. This is where the expiration date can be entered for the item's warranty.

The Attachments tab is utilized to attach any form of Document or File to an item in TCMax® (if Windows knows how to open that file). From the Attachments tab, you can either add an Attachment by Barcode Id or by Part Number. tip In Versions 9.8.x or older if you are ever on the Main Screen of TCMax® and wish to go to the Attachments tab, you can utilize one of our shortcuts by pressing Ctrl + A on your keyboard. In 9.9.x or newer, this shortcut has been updated to Ctrl + Shift + A to avoid conflicts with other shortcuts.

Scan the items Barcode on the Main Screen of TCMax®. Once the item is displayed, refer to the Attachments tab. Once you are on the Attachments tab, press Add Attachment to Barcode Id or Add Attachment to Part Number button depending on the Attachment you need to add. When either option is selected, a File Explorer Window will appear; navigate to the location of the Document/File you want to attach and double click on it. The Document/File will be added to the current attachments section. All attachments are immediately copied to a public TCMax® directory that way all users can interact with the attachments. The Default Directory where a copy of the attachment will be placed is C:\Users\Public\PublicDocuments\TCMax\Images\Attachments\BarcodeNumber or C:\Users\Public\PublicDocuments\TCMax\Images\Attachments\PartNumber. This directory can be adjusted to point to a network folder if needed, for example if your Database Connection is through a Server, you can modify the location by going to Settings > Options > General Options and adjusting the Picture and Attachment Path.
A Part Number Based Attachment can be utilized when you have a single Attachment that applies to all items with the same Part Number. Example: Safety Data Sheets (SDS) or instruction manuals.

A Barcode Number Based Attachment can be utilized when you have a file or document that applies only to this item. Example: A specific maintenance record. note There is no limit to how many Attachments you can have for an item.

Scan the items Barcode on the Main Screen of TCMax®. Once the item is displayed on the Main screen, press the Edit button to edit the items information. info You must be in edit mode of the item in order to remove an Attachment. Refer to the Attachments tab. Select the Attachment you would like to remove by clicking on the Attachment. This will highlight the Attachment. Press Delete on your keyboard and the Attachment will be removed from the item. If you remove an Attachment that is attached to the Part Number, this Attachment will also be removed from any item with that Part Number.

The Certified User tab allows users to be certified on an item before they can use that item. TCMax® allows you to regulate this by utilizing the Certification before use check box. Once checked, you enter the User Id of the certified user. Certifications are tied to an items Part Number, therefore when a user is certified on one item with the listed Part Number, they are certified on all items with that Part Number. info If your item does not have a Part Number in the Part Number field, you will not have the option to select Certification before use since this feature is based on Part Number.

Scan the item's Barcode on the Main Screen of TCMax®. Once the item is displayed on the Main screen, press the Edit button to edit the item's information. Refer to the Certified User tab in the lower right quadrant. From the Certified User tab, select the Certification before use checkbox. Once the item has been marked with 'Certification before use', scan or enter the Users Id to add them to the user certified list for this Part Number. Once the User has been scanned/entered, they will be added to the list on the Certified User tab.
documents.s: Adding Users to the Certified User List

documents.t: note If you are utilizing Version 9.9.0 or newer of TCMax®, you will not be able to modify the expiration date directly. The expiration date will be set to never expire. If you need to assign an expiration date to a Part Number, this can be configured through Courses using Training Completion mode. If a Users Date Certification Expires needs modified, with the item displayed and in editable mode, double click on the users date certification expires. A date picker will appear where you can select the new expiration date for the certification. info In Version 9.8.9580.24506 and older, by default, TCMax® will put the Date Certification Expires to a year from when you enter the user's Id to certify.
documents.s: Modifying a Users Certification Expiration Date

documents.t: If a User needs removed from the Certified User List, with the item displayed and in editable mode, refer to the far left column in the Certified User List. Select the User you wish to delete to highlight the User. Once the User has been highlighted, press Delete on your keyboard, the User will now be removed from the Certified List for items with that Part Number. tip Users whose certification has lapsed are highlighted in red. info When you try to issue an item to a User that is not certified, TCMax® responds by playing a ' User Not Certified' audio warning and the item is not issued. The TCMax® Training Completion mode can have part numbers assigned to courses so that when a course is completed by a user, that user is automatically certified to use any item that is associated with that part number as defined within that course.
documents.s: Removing Users from the Certified User List

documents.t: The Children tab gives you a quick view of all child items when you scan or enter a Barcode Id that has children. You can view and edit the details of the children and you can also mark the children with the status of Broken, Unserviceable, or Lost directly from this tab.

The Custom tab contains four checkboxes, six textboxes, and two combo boxes that you can customize to reflect any additional information about your items that you need that is not already provided within TCMax®. Any Item that is utilizing the Custom tab selections will appear on the Custom Field Reports. You can change the captions of these options to reflect the nomenclature that you need by going to the Settings > Options > Custom Captions tab.
The Hazmat tab appears when the Item Type on Additional Details is selected as Hazmat or Aerospace Coating. This will treat the item as a weighed item with additional properties.

Disposable signifies the Hazmat Item is disposable. When a Hazmat item is disposable, upon turn-in, if the entire weight of the item is not turned in, TCMax® will ask for the disposed quantity for reporting purposes.
Not Weighed signifies the Hazmat Item does not need to be weighed. If the Not Weighed checkbox is checked, TCMax® will not ask you to enter the weight of the item upon issue or turn in.
ABMix Ratio is used to enter the ABMix Ratio. This is used with the Navy Hazmat Report / Aerospace Coating Report.
Application Method is used to enter the Application Method for a Hazmat Item. This is used with the Navy Hazmat / Aerospace Coating Report.
Coating Category is used to enter the Coating Category of a Hazmat Item. This is used with the Navy Hazmat / Aerospace Coating Report.
Current Weight is used to identify the current weight of the Hazmat Item. This is used with the Navy Hazmat / Aerospace Coating Report.
Hazmat Weight is used to identify the hazmat weight of the Hazmat Item. This is used with the Navy Hazmat / Aerospace Coating Report.
SDS is used to enter the Safety Data Sheet of a Hazmat Item. This is used with the Navy Hazmat / Aerospace Coating Report.
Solvent Vp is used to enter the Solvent Vp of a Hazmat Item. This is used with the Navy Hazmat / Aerospace Coating Report.
VCContent As Applied is used to enter the VOCContent As Applied for a Hazmat Item. This is used with the Navy Hazmat / Aerospace Coating Report.
The Hose tab appears when the Item Type on Additional Details is selected as Hose. This tab allows additional details to be input for the hose.
Hose Length is used to identify the length of your Hose.
Hose Size is used to identify the size of your Hose.
Test Date is used to identify the date the testing of your Hose last took place.
Hydro Due Date is used to identify when Hydro Testing of the Hose needs to be completed.
Purchase Date is used to identify the date the Hose was purchased.
Status is used to identify the current Status of the Hose.
Test Pressure is used to identify the Test Pressure of the Hose.

The Inspections tab is where inspections can be added, updated, or modified. Inspections can be tracked by dates, miles, hours, or times used. From the Inspections tab, there are input boxes for the current miles, hours, or times used. The check boxes below each tracker can be checked if you wish for TCMax® to ask you to update the miles, hours, or times used when the item is turned back in.

To add a new inspection or modify an existing inspection click the Add/Modify Inspections button. This will bring up the Inspection Builder. Clicking the New Inspection button will allow you to create a new inspection. You can give it a logical name and then select the inspection type. You can choose to prevent the issuing of each item if its inspection is overdue. This has been a global option in previous versions of TCMax® but you can now decide this on a per-inspection basis.
The Inspection Type dropdown box will allow you to classify which type of inspection you intend to create. This classification helps TCMax® decide how to handle this item and it's inspections.

Generic Inspections are just normal inspections that will become due based on a date, miles, hours, or times used. There are no additional considerations or actions to perform. TCMax® will tell you when it is imminent, if you’ve set a lead time, and when it is overdue.

Pre-Use Inspections will need completed before the item can be issued. If the inspection is not completed when attempting to issue the item, you will be prompted to update it. An example of an item requiring a Pre-Use inspection would be for a fall protection harness. Before using this item, workers must visually inspect the lanyard and make sure it’s safe to use and hasn’t been sprung. Pre-Use inspections will also generate Completed Inspection records to show up in section II of the AF244 Report.

Stop Go Inspections are calculated based on an interval of days but also considers the number of hours the item is in use. TCMax® will calculate the number of hours an item has been issued and consider that time when deciding whether to alert about inspections being imminent / overdue.
Supervisor Review Inspections are just like Generic Inspections but Completed Inspection records will show up on section IV of the AF244 Report.

WRM (War Readiness Material) Inspections are used to track WRM equipment. By using a WRM Inspection you’re telling TCMax®, “If it sits dormant, it needs to be recalibrated in 2 years. If it gets deployed and starts being used, that calibration date needs to be changed to 6 months from its first use.” If you select WRM as the inspection type, the screen of the Inspection Builder changes a bit and you’re prompted to enter how far ahead to set the calibration due date once the item is issued. Once you set this inspection and go about your day, it will remain until you attempt to issue that item. Once that happens you’ll be asked if you are putting this WRM Item into rotation. If you click Yes, the inspection on this item will be removed and the calibration date will be changed to X number of days from then. Where X is the increment you set in the WRM inspection.

You cannot create ATC Inspections from TCMax®. They exist for customers who are using Snap-on Tools’ ATC boxes. The inspection needs to be created and updated at the box. The ATC Bridge will bring over the due date for this inspection with a generic name of ATC Inspection. You can edit the name of the inspection to give it a more specific name so reports and screens are a little easier to read. This new name does not persist to the ATC box; it only remains within TCMax®.
An Inventory Inspection is an inspection that will immediately become overdue when an item is added to an Inventory; forcing the user to complete the inspection on the item at time of inventory.

Post Use Inspections can be completed before the item is turned in. If the inspection is completed when turning in the item, we will update the inspection and write corresponding logs for the turn-in and inspection event. If the inspection is not completed when attempting to turn-in the item, the item will successfully turn-in, but the inspection will become overdue. We will write corresponding logs for the turn-in event.

You can now set individual lead times for TCMax® to warn you when this item’s inspection is coming due. There is a global option for this in the Settings > Options window however you can now override this with individual settings for special inspections. In the Inspection Due Date box, you can type the date this inspection is due next. You can hit T to quickly enter today’s date in this box. M will add a month to the date in this box. Hitting + will add a day. Hitting – will subtract a day. Y will add a year. If your inspection is reoccurring, be sure to select a value other than “None” from the Occurrence combo box. The checkbox to Update from the current due date, if checked, will increment the next due date from the date the inspection was due, not from date you updated the inspection. The overview area will type out your inspection schedule to allow you to confirm that you’ve entered everything in correctly.
The Odometer tab allows you to set a warning threshold for miles, the mileage this inspection will be due next, and the number of miles in between inspections.
The Hours tab allows you to set a warning threshold for hours, the hours this inspection will be due next, and the number of hours in between inspections.
The Times Used tab allows you to set a warning threshold for times used, the number of times this item can be used before this inspection is due next, and the number of uses between inspections.

As long as the logged in User has proper permissions, Inspections can be updated directly from the Main Screen. With the Item displayed, under the Inspections tab, you have the choice to Update Selected or Update All. If your item has more than one inspection, but you would like to only update one, select your inspection by clicking on the Inspection then select Update Selected. If your item has more than one inspection, and you would like to update all inspections at one time, select the Update All.

If an item no longer requires a specific inspection to be done, that inspection can be removed from the item. Click the Add/Modify Inspections button. This will bring up the Inspection Builder. To Remove / Delete an Inspection, select the inspection you would like to Remove and select Remove Inspection. If you would like to remove all inspections for an item at one time, select Remove All Inspections. The changes are not effective until you Accept Changes, so if you remove an inspection you did not intend to, click Cancel Changes and do not save any changes. If you are satisfied with the inspections you have removed, select Accept Changes and you will notice your inspection(s) is now removed from the main screen.

The Lower Right Quadrant is where detailed information about the item will be displayed. This information includes Quantity & Status, Inspections, Additional Details, Certified Users, Children, Custom, Pictures, Attachments, and Log Notes. The tabs not only display more detailed information but show how the item will work or how TCMax® will interact with that item. Each tab will be discussed in the next sections.

The Log Notes tab will display all log notes that have been entered for the item that is currently displayed on the Main Screen. From the Log Notes tab, you will see the specific Log Note with an event timestamp and a user defined date. Log Notes can be added to an item by pressing Ctrl + N when an item is displayed on the Main Screen or you can also add a log note when applying a Status on an item. info Log Notes are permanent details added to an item and they cannot be adjusted or deleted.
The Pictures tab allows you to place pictures on items within TCMax®. Pictures can be set on a per item or per Part Number basis. This way all like items will inherit the same picture.

To set a picture, with your item displayed on the Main Screen of TCMax®, select the Set Picture button and navigate to the picture of the item. A copy of the picture will be placed in a public directory. When setting a picture, if the item you are setting a picture on shares a Part Number with other items, TCMax® will ask if you would like to set the picture for just this item or all items with that Part Number. The Default Directory where a copy of the picture will be placed is C:\Users\Public\PublicDocuments\TCMax\Images. This directory can be adjusted to point to a network folder if needed, for example if your Database Connection is through a Server, you can modify the location by going to Settings > Options > General Options and adjusting the Picture and Attachment Path.
documents.s: Applying a Picture to an Item

documents.t: To remove a picture from an item, with your item displayed on the Main Screen of TCMax®, select the Clear Picture button. If this picture is used for more than one item with the same Part Number, TCMax® will ask if you would like to remove this picture from just this item or all items with this Part Number. note Only one picture can be set for an item.
documents.s: Removing a Picture from an Item

documents.t: The Quantity and Status tab is where you set up each item’s quantity settings and can change the status of an item.

The Multiple Items with the Same Barcode Number checkbox tells TCMax® that the scanned barcode represents more than one individual item. Common examples for this type of item are bench stock (nuts, bolts, or screws) and/or Personal Protective Equipment (safety glasses, reflective vests, earplugs, or rubber gloves). This setting can be used for items that are not individually tracked.
documents.s: Multiple Items with the Same Barcode Number

documents.t: The Issue Multiple Items with a Single Scan checkbox signifies the item is a multi-quantity item and can have more than one quantity issued at a time. When attempting to issue items with this checkbox, TCMax® will prompt you and ask how many you want to issue or turn in. The software plays an “Enter Quantity” audio prompt and then presents an input box on the screen that asks you to enter the desired quantity.
documents.s: Issue Multiple Items with a Single Scan

documents.t: The Consumable checkbox signifies the item is a consumable item within TCMax®. Basically, meaning that items can be used (consumed) on jobs and never returned, but until you tell TCMax® how many are consumed, the full quantity taken is expected to be returned. The software will ask for a consumed quantity if the quantity you are turning in is less than what was issued. TCMax® will adjust the quantities automatically for you based on what quantities have been entered.

The No Turn-In checkbox signifies an item is an Expendable item. In other words when this item is issued we are never expecting the item to be turned in. The quantities for these items will be immediately adjusted at the point of issue. Expendable items are tracked independently of other items. In TCMax® there is a dedicated tab for Expendable items issued to a particular user as Expendables are not tracked via the regular issued items list or reports.
Qty on Hand is the total quantity of the item in the Shop, including what is currently issued.
Qty Available is the total quantity of the item on the shelf that can be issued.

Available by Part Number will only appear if the item displayed has a Part Number assigned to it. This shows the quantity of the Part Number that is available / the quantity of the part number that is on hand. By clicking on Available by Part Number, a grid will populate showing the items that have this part number, along with Quantity, Shop Code, Parent, Calibration Due Date, Storage Location, NSN, and Cost. (This grid can be right clicked on and sent to excel if needed)
Cost is the monetary value associated with the item. This can be entered up to the 4th decimal place.
Vendor is the company that the item is acquired through. Only one vendor can be selected per Barcode Id (Item).

Do Not Reorder signifies this item is not to be reordered and will not populate on the Reorder Report. When an Item is marked as Do Not Reorder, TCMax® will not notify you if the item falls below the Reorder Qty, as the item is not to be reordered.

Max In Stock is the maximum allowed quantity for an item you want to stock at a time. This information will generate on the Reorder Report to help show when an item is ready for reorder and how many will need ordered to raise the item back to the max in stock value.

Reorder Qty is the reorder threshold for multi-quantity items. When TCMax® falls below this specified quantity, it will appear in red signifying it is time to reorder. This is used as a means to prevent from completely running out of an item.
Qty In Unit is the quantity of an item that is contained in each purchased/received unit.
Sold As is the description of how an item is purchased/ordered. Example: Box, pallet, case, or each.
The Broken status checkbox is used to indicate any visual defects on an item. note Items marked Broken in TCMax® can still be issued.
The Unserviceable status checkbox renders the item unusable, and it cannot be issued. Example: A screwdriver that has snapped into multiple pieces.
The Deactivated status checkbox indicates an item is Deactivated and cannot be issued out. Often times this status is used for items past their usable lifecycle and are waiting to be replaced.
The Lost status checkbox is used for items that cannot be located. This can be applied to items after they have been issued or during an inventory.

The Main Screen can be broken down into four sections: Upper Left Quadrant, Lower Left Quadrant, Upper Right Quadrant, and Lower Right Quadrant. We will go more in depth about each piece in the following sections.

The Lower Left Quadrant will display different Data depending on the action being performed in TCMax®. If there is no user displayed on the screen this grid will be a historical event log showing you the actions that have been performed recently within the software. If there is a user displayed on the Main Screen, this grid will change to display the items issued to that user as well as some additional user related tabs.

The Event Logs tab can be used to see what actions have been performed in TCMax®. Example: Issue/Turn-in, Login/Logout, Item Added, Item Modified, and Item Deleted records. note The Event Logs tab displays the most recent 100 events of the current TCMax® session.

The User's Issued Items tab will display when a user has been entered on the screen. You will see a list of items currently issued to that user. During Turn-in, if you scan an issued item, the grid will display the Issued Items tab for the user that the item was issued to.

The User's Expendables tab will show the Expendables (No Turn-in items) that the user has been issued in the last 30 days. tip Expendable Items cannot be turned in, but the quantity issued can be overridden and reduced. To do this, right click on any of the rows highlighted green. Then select Override Expendable Quantity. The quantity can be overrode, but must contain a value less than the current value. Any of the reduced quantity will be returned to stock.

The User Attachments tab will show any files that are attached to the displayed user. Users can have multiple Attachments. Adding an Attachment to a User​ To add an Attachment, click the Add Attachment to User button and use the File Explorer Window to select the file that you would like to attach. All Attachments are immediately copied to a public TCMax® directory that way all users can interact with the attachments. The Default Directory where a copy of the attachment will be placed is C:\Users\Public\PublicDocuments\TCMax\Images\Attachments\UserId. This directory can be adjusted to point to a network folder if needed, for example if your Database Connection is through a Server, you can modify the location by going to Settings > Options > General Options and adjusting the Picture and Attachment Path. Removing an Attachment from a User​ To remove an Attachment, display the User on the Main Screen and refer to the User Attachments tab. Select the Attachment you would like to remove to highlight it. Once the Attachment is highlighted, press Delete on your keyboard. The Attachment will now be removed from the User.

The Upper Right Quadrant is where item Data is displayed. An item's information can be modified by clicking the Edit button (if you have the necessary permission) or a new label can be generated for the displayed item by clicking the Print Item Label button.

The Shop Code displayed in gray is the Shop the Item displayed lives within. The Shop Code drop down menu option can be used to change Shop Codes to display different items that live within different Shop Codes.
Barcode Id is the unique identifying set of characters for an item. This is unique per Shop Code.

Parent Barcode Id is used for items in TCMax® to create kits. When a Parent Barcode Id is used it assigns an item to a parent, creating a parent-child relationship. It signifies the item lives inside of the parent item.
Item Name is used to place a description on your item. This can be as vague or detailed as you would like.

Storage Location is used to identify where a particular item lives. You can use a colon delimiter as well to narrow down the location and to order on the MIL Report. An example of this would be Drawer 1: Spot 2.
NSN refers to the National Stock Number. This is typically used within the Military.

Part Number is used to group like items together in TCMax®. For example, photos / certifications and other features are dependent on it to cascade information to all items with the same Part numbers. Each item can have its own Part Number if desired, or you can group items together utilizing the same Part Number.
Calibration Due Date is used to enter the date the calibration is due on an item.

Days to Calibrate field will be displayed next to the Calibration Due Date. This is used to project how many days the item will be gone for calibration. This is used so all of the same item are not leaving the shop at the same time and you can plan accordingly when calibrations are going to occur.

If the logged in user has the permission to Manage Calibrations and allow receiving custody of items with overdue calibrations, then they can add or edit a calibration due date for an item by displaying the item on the Main Screen and clicking in the Cal Due Date field.
Serial Number is the specific serial number of an item.

The Upper Left Quadrant is known as the Data Entry Section. The User that is logged into TCMax® is displayed above the input box. The input box is where all barcodes are scanned or typed in. The color of the box will indicate what actions can be performed. Yellow: If the input box is yellow, all criteria has not been met to allow the issuing of items, but items that are already issued out can be turned in. Green: If the input box is green, it means that all criteria has been met to allow for items to be issued. Items can also be turned in. Red: If the input box is red, no issue or turn in actions can take place.

The TCMax® Dashboard is a set of status trackers that can help you quickly identify various Data points within your Database. The Dashboard is a standalone application available with the TCMax® Suite as well as integrated within TCMax®.

You can open the Dashboard to full screen or set it to quick view. To open the quick view display, right-click on the blue bar on the right-hand side of the screen. The right-hand side of the Main Screen shows one column of the Dashboard status trackers. To open the Dashboard in full screen, left-click on the blue bar. The Dashboard screen is closed the same way, by either right clicking the blue bar if it is partially open or left clicking the blue bar if it is fully open.

The Status Trackers Tab will display various Data points at a glance. This is Shop Code specific. Therefore, you can use the Shop Code drop down in the upper right-hand corner to view different Shop Code statuses.

Status Trackers can be organized how you want it to be. Simply click on a Blue Group and drag that Group where you would like it to appear. This can become useful if you want to display specific Data in the Mini Pane of the Dashboard. The Mini Pane only shows the left most column of the Dashboard. Therefore, if you would like to view for example, the User Status Group in the Mini Pane, simply click and drag that group over to the left-hand column. Now, when you right-click on the Dashboard, the User Status stays in the Mini Pane while still performing other tasks on the Main Screen of TCMax®.

Status Trackers within Dashboard show numerical Data for the different status's. If you want more detailed Data, click on the status you would like to view. A grid will appear with additional Data regarding that specific tracker. Example: If you have Overdue Inspections under the Inspection Status that show 5, you may want to see more details on what is showing Overdue. By clicking on Overdue Inspections, a grid appears with more details showing what Items have Inspections that are Overdue. tip Captions and warning thresholds (highlighted red) can be set via Settings > Dashboard Limits.
documents.s: Displaying Data for the Status Trackers

documents.t: The Custom Status Trackers tab is where Custom Status Trackers created will be displayed. info If there is a Status Tracker that is not already offered within TCMax®, this can be created using the Custom Tracker Builder. A Custom Status Tracker can be built for you as an additional paid for service.

In the top right of the Catalog Setup screen you will see two Part Specific Features. These will alter the way TCMax® interacts with items that have a specific Part Number. These options don’t need to be pushed out to the inventory, if they’re checked for a Part Number, that feature now applies to that Part Number.
Restrict Quick Turn will prevent items with this Part Number from being able to be transferred using the Item Quick Turn @ Shift Change function.

This option works with Part Numbers that are assigned to Parent (kit) items. When this option is enabled for a Part Number that is assigned as the Parent of a kit, upon issuing the Parent item (kit), TCMax® will issue all its children (components) separately. The log records and issued item screens will show an issue record for not only the parent item, but the children as well. This option should be used with caution as there is no way to rapidly turn in all of the child items. Each component would need scanned/entered to turn it in separately.
documents.s: Create Individual Issue Records for all Available Children when Issuing a Kit

documents.t: If you’re adding new items from the Main Screen of TCMax® and you have the catalog enabled with autofill, you can enter the Part Number first and TCMax® will fill out any of the other fields you have setup for this Part Number. This will make sure that your new items comply with the same Data formatting that you are already using.

Template Barcodes allow you to create multiple labels with different barcode numbers for items of the same Part Number. The use of this type of label could be very beneficial when adding your initial inventory into TCMax® when you have several individual items of the same Part Number. For instance, if you have several individual items that have the same Barcode create the Part Number in the Catalog screen then click the Print Template Barcode button. This will display the Template Barcode Setup screen. On this screen, you will need to select what Printer (Label Printer or Page Printer) that you want the labels to print from. Once the appropriate Printer has been selected, in the Quantity field, enter how many template labels you want printed for this Part Number and in the Barcode Prefix / Suffix fields, enter the values for each label. This will be the unique identifier for each item. In the example below, there will be 50 labels printed all with the same Part Number of M-4/5.56 with the barcode numbers ranging from SSS001 to SSS050. Click Print on the Setup screen to print the labels. When one of these barcodes is scanned, TCMax® will create the new item, and it will also cascade all the details you have setup for that Part Number; essentially allowing you to create an item and input all of the details by simply scanning a preset barcode.

The Item Creation Prompts section allows you to add item details that you want to prompt for upon creating a new item with the selected Part Number. Clicking the Set Prompts button will display a screen where you can choose the information to be prompted for and after clicking Save they will be listed in the Item Creation Prompts section. An example of this may be to ask for the cost of the item upon creating it or the quantity. When an item gets added via a Template Barcode or from simply inputting the Part Number on a new item (with AutoFill enabled) TCMax® will then prompt you for the cost and quantity of the item.

The Quantity section allows you to setup how this item behaves and details for the item. It is worth noting that this section in Catalog Setup is the only place in TCMax® where you can restrict the quantity of an item that's issued to the same person within a specific number of days. A good example of this is if utilizing the Consume by Control Number for vouchers, you may want to restrict your users to only receive one voucher per year. Another example is setting up a limit of consumables / expendables of a particular Part Number that can be issued within a week.
The Additional Details section allows you to setup additional details you would like for items with that specific Part Number.
The Custom section allows you to apply any Custom Fields to Part Numbers you may have already set up through Settings > Options > Custom Captions.
The Pictures sections allows you to set or remove a Picture for a specific Part Number.

In this section, you can compile a list of Generic Notes for rapid input for use in Physical Inventory (Touch Enabled) mode. To add a Generic Note, select the Add Generic Note button. An input box will pop up prompting you to enter a name for the note that you want to add. Once you have given your note a name, select the OK button. Now a new input box will pop up prompting you to enter the note itself. After you have entered the Generic Note, select the OK button and the new Generic Note will now appear on the list. This feature can be seen when running a Physical Inventory. During the inventory session, if there is a discrepancy for an item (with the Part Number that the Generic Note was added to) you can resolve the discrepancy with a note. The Generic Note will appear on the Discrepancy Notes / Resolve Discrepancy pop up window as a button. This simply allows touchscreen only users to use a predefined note. You can delete a Generic Note from the Catalog by highlighting it in the list and then hitting the Delete key on your keyboard.

The Inspections section allows you to add or remove inspections for a specific Part Number. This is useful if all items that share a Part Number have the same inspection at the same interval. This helps speed up adding inspections to items, as you would not have to add the same inspection to each item, but rather if the items share the same Part Number, you can add the inspection via Catalog and push that Inspection to all items you wish that have this Part Number.

Catalog is a list of all of the Part Numbers that exist within your Database. Part Numbers are used throughout the software to group similar items and cascade uniform Data to the various Data entry fields. Catalog allows you to make sure that the Data entered for your items is accurate and formatted properly. The Catalog Setup screen can be accessed by going to Tools > Catalog Setup from the Main Screen of TCMax®. The user that's logged in must have the Access Catalog Setup permission. TCMax® will dynamically build this Catalog based off the Part Numbers you enter for your items. If you create a new item and give it a Part Number, it will automatically be added to the Catalog. In addition, you can add Part Numbers directly to the Catalog without having to create inventory items. All changes made to the Catalog Setup screen are saved automatically. There is no undo button so make sure your actions on this screen are deliberate and access to this screen is tightly controlled. info Additional logging information has been added in Version 9.9.0 and higher when using Catalog Setup. The functions of the Catalog will depend on what you have selected in the Catalog Settings area. You can disable autofill, activate it, and activate it with overwrite. If you have Activate AutoFill selected, the catalog will fill out missing information but will not modify a field that has different Data in it. If you want the catalog to overwrite any existing values, you must have Activate AutoFill W/ Overwrite selected. AutoFill will ensure that any item in your Database with the same Part Number will inherit the same properties and uniform Data points. All details in the Catalog will cascade to the item details for a new item with the same Part Number. To add a new Part Number to your Catalog, type the desired Part Number into the input box in the top left of the screen and hit Enter. The Part Number will get added to the list on the left side of the screen. On the right side of the screen you can input any additional Data you might want for items with this Part Number.

You can push out information from Catalog Setup for items that have already been created. For example, you may want to push out a standard inspection for all items with the same Part Number, rather than creating an identical inspection multiple times for each separate item. The Data entry fields are laid out in Catalog the same way they’re grouped on the Main Screen of TCMax®. The Push check box on the outer edge of each field will force the Data in that field out to the items with the selected Part Number. The Check All and Uncheck All buttons can be used to configure the Data that you would like to send out. The Overwrite existing values checkbox will replace any existing Data in the selected fields. Once you have configured the Data to be pushed, click the Push Selected Fields button. It is important to note that Part Numbers are universal and not bound to any Shop Code or Site. If you push the update, TCMax® will want to update every item with that Part Number in your entire Database. To help prevent against unwanted or intrusive updates, we’ve added the confirmation window. After you’ve clicked the Push Selected Fields button, you will be shown this window: The above screen lists every item with the particular Part Number TCMax® intends to update and shows you the Barcode Id and the Shop Code of that item. You can deselect any items that you don’t want to update and click the Accept button. The software will notify you when the push is successful and complete.
documents.s: Pushing Out Changes To Existing Items

documents.t: Quick Functions are used to perform various actions within TCMax® by scanning a structured barcode to automate a process and quickly perform tasks on the fly. Utilizing these barcodes saves the end user from having to navigate around the Main Screen.

To access the setup screen, navigate to Tools > Configure Quick Functions from the Main Screen. From the Configure Quick Functions screen, expand the node for the action that you wish to set up a barcode for. The sections are labeled according to the name of the action that they will perform. For example, if you want to create a structured barcode that will mark an item as broken, you’d expand the Broken node and click the plus sign to create the new preset configuration.

The Broken, Unserviceable, and Deactivated functions behave similarly with the exception that one will mark the item as Broken, one will mark it as Unserviceable, and the other will mark it as Deactivated.

Name is the description that will print with the Barcode when you generate the physical label. The Open Log Note Screen checkbox will open a Log Notes Screen when scanning the Quick Function Barcode. This works as if you are marking an item status on the Main Screen with Log Notes. Leaving the checkbox unchecked will not populate the Log Notes Screen. You can predefine a Log Note to be automatically placed on items when scanning the Quick Function Barcode by entering the Log Note into the box under the checkbox in the Note Value. Part Number Filters can be set if you only want this barcode to work for certain items. TCMax® will only accept this barcode scan for an item with matching text in the Part Number field. If you try to scan a Quick Function Barcode with a Part Number Filter for an Item that does not have that Part Number, you will receive a message in Blue above the Input Box stating Part number does not match filter - No action taken. Item Name Filters can be set if you only want this barcode to work for certain items. TCMax® will only accept this barcode scan for an item that contains the text in the Item Name. info This is a contains option. This means the Quick Function will work for any item that contains the Item Name Filter, it does not have to match exactly. Print will print the barcode for the Quick Function to easily be scanned. This can be placed by the computer for quick use when needed. The Preset value is an alias that TCMax® associates with the settings you’ve made for this Structured Barcode. Presets allow you to include additional settings in the quick function that wouldn't otherwise fit into the physical barcode label. The Full Value will work without the need to set this up in the Quick Function Configuration. Presets also have the ability to work without a scanner if you do not have one. Right clicking on Preset will allow you to copy the Preset or Full Barcode. Left clicking on Preset will show you the Preset Value and Full Value. Example: If you wanted to apply a defect to batteries that will no longer hold a charge, you could set the Structured Broken Barcode up as follows: When scanned, this Quick Function Barcode will mark the Item on the Main Screen as Broken and write a Log Note saying, “The battery will no longer hold a charge.” TCMax® will only perform these functions if the item displayed on the Main Screen has the text “battery” somewhere in the Item Name Field. The filters are used to ensure that the actions are performed on only the intended items. If you left click on the ‘Preset 1’ link, you’ll be shown the two values associated with this example Structured Barcode.

The Return to Service function allows you to take an item that has been marked Broken, Unserviceable, or Deactivated and unmark the Item, placing it back into service. This behaves similarly to unchecking the status boxes on the Main Screen of TCMax®.

Name is the description that will print with the barcode when you generate the physical label. The Open Log Note Screen checkbox will open a Log Notes Screen when scanning the Quick Function Barcode. This works as if you are marking an item status on the Main Screen with Log Notes. Leaving the checkbox unchecked will not populate the Log Notes Screen. You can predefine a Log Note to be automatically placed on items when scanning the Quick Function Barcode by entering the Log Note into the box under the checkbox in the Note Value. Part Number Filters can be set if you only want this barcode to work for certain items. TCMax® will only accept this barcode scan for an item with matching text in the Part Number field. note If you try to scan a Quick Function Barcode with a Part Number Filter for an Item that does not have that Part Number, you will receive a message in Blue above the Input Box stating Part number does not match filter - No action taken. Item Name Filters can be set if you only want this barcode to work for certain items. TCMax® will only accept this barcode scan for an item that contains the text in the Item Name. note This is a contains option. This means the Quick Function will work for any item that contains the Item Name Filter, it does not have to match exactly. Status is how you can indicate how or why your item is being returned to service. You can note the Item was Fixed or Replaced when the barcode is scanned, or you can have the barcode Prompt the User every time to make the appropriate selection. Print will print the barcode for the Quick Function to easily be scanned. This can be placed by the computer for quick use when needed. The Preset value is an alias that TCMax® associates with the settings you’ve made for this Structured Barcode. Presets allow you to include additional settings in the quick function that wouldn't otherwise fit into the physical barcode label. The Full Value will work without the need to set this up in the Quick Function Configuration. Presets also have the ability to work without a scanner if you do not have one. Right clicking on Preset will allow you to copy the Preset or Full Barcode. Left clicking on Preset will show you the Preset Value and Full Value.
This Transfer function will allow you to create a barcode that will transfer the item on the Main Screen into a different shop.

Name is the description that will print with the barcode when you generate the physical label. Shop code to transfer item to is the Shop Code you will specify you want the item transferred to when scanning this Quick Configuration Function. The Issue item after transfer checkbox will issue the item to the User on the Main Screen after transferring the Item to a different Shop Code. The Ask for tracking number checkbox will prompt for a tracking number after scanning the Item to transfer to a different Shop Code. Audio File will allow you to select any wave file to be played when this Quick Function is scanned. When clicking Audio File, a File Explorer screen will open for you to point TCMax® to and select your wave file to be played. Print will print the barcode for the Quick Function to easily be scanned. This can be placed by the computer for quick use when needed. The Preset value is an alias that TCMax® associates with the settings you’ve made for this Structured Barcode. Presets allow you to include additional settings in the quick function that wouldn't otherwise fit into the physical barcode label. The Full Value will work without the need to set this up in the Quick Function Configuration. Presets also have the ability to work without a scanner if you do not have one. Right clicking on Preset will allow you to copy the Preset or Full Barcode. Left clicking on Preset will show you the Preset Value and Full Value.

The Arrival / Departure function allows you to create either an Arrival or Departure barcode to track where your Users are. When scanning this barcode it will keep track of where Users are or are going.

When first Selecting the + to add an Arrival / Departure, you will be prompted for a Location to Set for the barcode. This is the Location you will want displayed when this barcode is Scanned. Name is the description that will print with the barcode when you generate the physical label. Type is the type of barcode that is being created. You have the choice of Arrival or Departure to show what the User is doing at this Location. The Prompt for next destination checkbox will only be active when selecting Departure. When scanning this barcode for a Departure, you can have TCMax prompt for the next destination to be entered. Audio File will allow you to select any wave file to be played when this Quick Function is scanned. When clicking Audio File, a File Explorer screen will open for you to point TCMax® to and select your wave file to be played. Print will print the barcode for the Quick Function to easily be scanned. This can be placed by the computer for quick use when needed. The Preset value is an alias that TCMax® associates with the settings you’ve made for this Structured Barcode. Presets allow you to include additional settings in the quick function that wouldn't otherwise fit into the physical barcode label. The Full Value will work without the need to set this up in the Quick Function Configuration. Presets also have the ability to work without a scanner if you do not have one. Right clicking on Preset will allow you to copy the Preset or Full Barcode. Left clicking on Preset will show you the Preset Value and Full Value.

The User Certification Revoking function allows you to revoke a User's Certification temporarily for Items based on a Course, Part Number, or a List of selected Part Numbers. This Quick Function Barcode will be used when a User is on the Main Screen.

Name is the description that will print with the barcode when you generate the physical label. Revoke Type is how you will Revoke a User temporarily. If you Revoke based off a Course, Part Number, or Part Number List. Once you select your Revoke Type click the Set button and you will be prompted for a Course Barcode Id, a Part Number, or to select a Part Number List that is pre-created in Revoke List Setup. Expires In (Days) allows you to set a Number of Days you would like the Revoking to Expire and the User to become Certified again. info If you leave this at 0, the certification will remain revoked until an Un-Revoke Barcode is Scanned. The Revoking: Open log note Screen checkbox will open a Log Notes Screen when scanning the Quick Function Barcode. This can allow you to add details to the Log Notes about why a User is being Revoked or Unrevoked. Print Revoke will print the barcode for Revoking Users Certifications. This can be placed by the computer for quick use when needed. Print Unrevoke will print the barcode for Un-revoking (Or Re-Establishing) Users Certifications. This can be placed by the computer for quick use when needed. The Preset value is an alias that TCMax® associates with the settings you’ve made for this Structured Barcode. Presets allow you to include additional settings in the quick function that wouldn't otherwise fit into the physical barcode label. The Full Value will work without the need to set this up in the Quick Function Configuration. Presets also have the ability to work without a scanner if you do not have one. Right clicking on Preset will allow you to copy the Preset or Full Barcode. Left clicking on Preset will show you the Preset Value and Full Value.

Go to Settings > Revoke List Setup from the Configure Quick Functions screen. Once on the Revoke List Setup screen, you will need to give a name for the list you are creating. To do this, click the Add New button and type the name for this list. Then, enter the Part Numbers/Barcode Ids that this revocation pertains to and click the Submit button. Those items will be added to the grid on the right. When you are done adding, click the Close button. Now that the list has been generated, you will be able to apply it to your preset. Under the ‘User Certification Revoking’ node, click the Part Number List radio button, and then click the Set button. From the ‘Revoke List’ screen, click the appropriate pre-configured list and click Select.
documents.s: Setting up a Part Number List for Revoking Certifications

documents.t: Structured Barcodes are intended to be scanned while there is a user or item displayed on the Main Screen of TCMax®. They can also be stacked together to perform multiple operations at once. For example, if we wanted to mark our battery as broken and then transfer it to a manufacturer for warranty replacement, you could set up a preset for marking it as broken and then set up a preset for transferring it to a specific shop. Each individual preset barcode would decode into the following strings: <B pSet='1'/>: This tells TCMax® to run through the Preset 1 code for a Broken structured barcode. <TR pSet='1'/>: This tells TCMax® to run through the Preset 1 code for a Transfer structured barcode. If you encode your barcode with both values, TCMax® will run through both procedures in the order they appear. So, if your barcode decodes into <B pSet='1'/><TR pSet='1'/>, the software will follow the Broken Preset 1 input and then immediately go through Transfer Preset 1.

Consume by Control Number can be used by an organization to consume items issued to users based off the control number assigned at the time of issue. This functionality can be used along with a voucher system for organizations that pay for a user’s PPE, but have the user purchase the PPE themselves.

For example, a facility requires a user to purchase their own steel-toed boots, but the company will reimburse the employee for the purchase. They issue the user a voucher instead and when the employee purchases the boots they ‘turn in’ the receipt for the purchase at which time the voucher is consumed. This allows the organization to keep track of what users have been reimbursed for their PPE purchases. This also allows organizations to limit the number of reimbursement vouchers a user can be issued in a given time frame when used in conjunction with the allowed quantity functionality found in Catalog Setup.

To utilize this feature, you will need to check the Requires Control Number checkbox for the consumable item. The Requires Control Number checkbox is located on the Additional Details tab from the Main Screen of TCMax®. When this box has been checked, each time you go to issue this item, there will be a prompt to Enter Control Number. This value gets written to the issued record in the EventLog for tracking. Once the voucher or item is issued, navigate to Tools > Consume by Control Number. From this screen, users can select from a list of items issued by the control number that was assigned during the issue process. When a control number is selected, a box in the lower right-hand corner will display details about the item, who the item was issued to, and when the item was issued. To complete the process, select the item you wish to consume by a control number then Double Click the record or press Enter on your keyboard. A pop-up box will appear asking if you consumed the item(s). Click Yes if you are consuming the item. Once Yes has been selected, the quantities will be adjusted to reflect the change. Click No if you do not want to consume the item. Once No has been selected, you will return to the Consume Consumables by Control Number screen.
The Control Number Filter box allows for the user to search through a list of assigned control numbers more efficiently.

Status Trackers provide information about your Database day to day operations in TCMax®. There are a handful of built-in trackers included in the TCMax® Dashboard that can be viewed. You may however, want to create your own Status Tracker that is better suited for your environment or to track a specific event that is not a part of our built-in trackers. The Custom Tracker Builder screen is accessed from Tools > Custom Tracker Builder and requires the person logged in to have the Access Designers permission. In the Dashboard, there is a tab for Custom Status Trackers which is where custom trackers are displayed. The Custom Status Tracker Builder screen has three main steps and two preview areas. Trackers are displayed in groups which can be expanded or collapsed. The groups exist to help organize the custom trackers you build. Each individual tracker can have “child” trackers which allow you to quickly limit the displayed data further. To help illustrate the difference between Groups and Trackers, below is a screen shot of the Custom Status Tracker tab in the Dashboard. note For a fee, we can provide Custom Trackers based on your requirements that you can import into your copy of TCMax®.

Deployment Inventory allows you to run an inventory against any items in your system that have been assigned to a deployment. To access the Deployment Inventory menu, select Tools > Inventory > Deployment Inventory or press Ctrl + Shift + I on your keyboard then press Deployment Inventory.
