Upon selecting Deployment Inventory, the Deployment Inventory screen will appear. From the Deployment Inventory screen, you can select which Deployment you would like to perform an inventory on.

At any point during the Deployment Inventory, if you need to leave the screen to perform other tasks, you can select Close in the bottom right-hand corner of the inventory screen. Upon selecting Close, your inventory session will be paused giving you the option to pick up where you left off when returning to the Deployment Inventory screen. If you started an inventory session and did not complete it before leaving the Inventory mode, you can complete the inventory by selecting the Join Existing Inventory tab, highlighting the inventory you wish to complete, and clicking the Join Selected Inventory button. If all your Deployment Inventories have been completed and you do not have one that is waiting to be completed, you will not see this tab. The Join Existing Inventory tab only appears when there is an inventory that was started and not completed. If you are not joining an existing inventory, press the Start button from the Deployment Inventory screen. This will take you into the Inventory screen. The Deployment Inventory screen has been optimized to work on both tablet and desktop PCs. You can inventory an item by either double clicking (tapping for touch-enabled devices) on the item in the list or by scanning the item’s Barcode Id. In either case, inventorying the item will place a green checkmark next to the item indicating that it has been inventoried during this session. If you are using a barcode scanner and interact with an item that has been set up as a multiple quantity item, you can enter the quantity for that item in the upper right-hand corner of the screen. The expected quantity will be listed in the Item Details section. If the inventoried quantity matches the expected quantity the item will be marked as inventoried with a green checkmark. If the Expected Quantity and Inventoried Quantity don’t match, it will be recorded as having been inventoried with a discrepancy. If you inventory an item in error, you can right click on the item and select Reset from the menu that appears. This will reset the item as if it had not been inventoried.

During the inventory process, you can apply Conditions to items. The conditions that are available during the Deployment Inventory process are Excellent (E), Good (G), Fair (F), Poor (P), and None (N). Before an item is inventoried, select the button for the condition you would like to apply from the top of the Inventory screen. Once the condition has been selected, scan, type, or double-click on the Barcode Id that you wish to inventory. Upon inventorying the Barcode Id, the item will be Inventoried and display with a green checkmark and the condition that was applied.

During the inventory process, you can apply Statuses to items. info Versions 9.8.9329.21809 or older will not have the ability to apply Statuses to an item within the Inventory Session. The statuses that are available during the Deployment Inventory process are Broken, Unserviceable, Deactivated, and Lost. To apply a status to an item that has been inventoried or has not been inventoried, select the item you would like to apply the status to from the Items list then select the status you would like applied. Once the status has been applied, we will mark that item with the selected status within TCMax® and write corresponding log records.

Discrepancies are inconsistencies with items that have been discovered/entered during the inventory process. Quantity Did Not Match: This discrepancy is generated during Deployment Inventory when the Inventoried Quantity does not match the Expected Quantity. Generic: This discrepancy is generated during Deployment Inventory when you right click on the item and select Add Generic Discrepancy. Upon selecting Add Generic Discrepancy, a Discrepancy Note entry screen will appear where you can enter information about the discovered discrepancy. A red X will then appear in the inventory status button for that item. A Discrepancy can be resolved before completing the inventory by clicking on the Discrepancy and selecting the Resolve button. Once you have selected the Resolve button, you will then get a Resolve Discrepancy entry screen which allows you to update the discrepancy’s note. Selecting the Accept button will accept the resolution. The Discrepancy will then be marked as resolved in the Discrepancy List. The item will then be updated with a green checkmark instead of a red X in the inventory status. Does Not Belong in this Inventory: This discrepancy is generated when an item that is not listed is inventoried. Not Inventoried: This discrepancy is one that cannot be manually added to an item. The discrepancy is generated when you did not inventory items before selecting the Complete Inventory button. This discrepancy cannot be resolved other than re-inventorying the deployment and making sure all items are accounted for.

Inventory Notes can be added to items during the Deployment Inventory process by highlighting an item and clicking the Add/Edit Note button on the right side of the screen or by right clicking on the item and selecting Add/Edit Note. These Notes are added to the log records and kept for reporting purposes.

To complete the Deployment Inventory and commit the records to your Database, click the Complete Inventory button in the bottom right-hand corner of the Inventory screen. If any items have been missed from being inventoried, an Items Not Inventoried popup will appear letting you know not all items have been accounted for. You can then choose Yes to complete the inventory anyways, which will create Discrepancies for any item that has not been inventoried, or choose No to go back and inventory any item that was missed.

General Inventory is used to inventory any assets in a selected Shop Code. To access the General Inventory menu, select Tools > Inventory > General Inventory or press Ctrl + Shift + I on your keyboard then press General Inventory. The left-hand side of the General Inventory screen is where most of the interaction for the Inventory Mode will take place. The right-hand side of the General Inventory screen is where you can select a Condition or apply Statuses (Lost, Broken, Unserviceable, Deactivated) to an item. When Statuses are applied to an item it is updated in real time and will generate corresponding log records. The right-hand side will also display a list of your inventoried items. info Versions 9.8.9329.21809 or older will not have the ability to apply Statuses to an item within the Inventory Session.

To inventory items, start by selecting a Shop Code from the Select a shop code drop down menu. Once a Shop Code is selected, refer to the Scan or enter an item's barcode id to inventory text box. Scan/type in the items Barcode Id you wish to Inventory. If a Kit (Parent) needs inventoried, there is an available option from General Inventory which allows you to Auto Inventory all children when parent is scanned. By turning on the Auto inventory all children when parent is scanned option, you can allow the General Inventory Mode to inventory all of the children when the parent barcode id is scanned. Often times this is utilized to speed up the inventory process. note If you decide to utilize the Auto inventory all children when parent is scanned option, make sure that the items are in the kit before scanning its Barcode Id as it will create an inventory record for all items in the kit. These records cannot be removed or deleted. Upon entering/scanning the Barcode Id, TCMax® will state 'Inventory' and add the item(s) to the right-hand side of the Inventory screen. When entering/scanning the Barcode Id, if the item is a multiple quantity item, TCMax® will prompt you to enter the quantity of the item. By default, the expected quantity will populate in the Enter Quantity box. This will show how many TCMax® is showing should be there and you can adjust after counting the quantity before selecting OK. If you enter a value that is different than the expected quantity, the items quantity will be adjusted, and an inventory record will be created recording the Inventory Discrepancy. info If the Auto inventory all children when parent is scanned option was enabled then all children items of the scanned parent would display from the Inventoried Items grid.

If you scan an item in General Inventory that is not found in your selected Shop Code, TCMax® will state 'Attention' and display a red exclamation point letting you know Item '****' not found. If you wish to record a log record with details about this item, you can select Click to add not found event log record which will open a dialog box where you can record details about this action. Selecting the Save button will save an Inventory Not Found Log Record which can be viewed from Log Search or select Reports.

info Versions 9.8.9329.21809 or older will allow you to add a log note only to the last inventoried item. Under the Item input box, you will have the ability to press "Click to add log note" or you are able to press Ctrl + N on your keyboard (reference image below). If you would like to add a log note, select the item you wish to have a log note applied to then select Add Log Note or press Ctrl + N on your keyboard. A Log Note Dialog screen will appear allowing you to add a log note to the inventoried item. Once the log note has been added, press Save which is located in the lower right-hand corner of the Notes screen.

During the inventory process, you can apply Conditions to items. The conditions that are available during the General Inventory process are Excellent (E), Good (G), Fair (F), Poor (P), and None (N). Within the General Inventory process, there are two ways to apply a condition to an item. Option 1​ Before an item is inventoried, select the button for the condition you would like to apply from the right-hand side of the Inventory screen. Once the condition has been selected, scan/type in the Barcode Id that you wish to inventory. Upon entering/scanning the Barcode Id, the item will be added to the Inventoried Items grid and display the selected condition. Option 2​ To apply a condition after the item has been inventoried, select the item you would like to apply the condition to from the Inventoried Items grid then select the condition you would like applied to the item. Once the item/condition has been selected, click the Apply button in the Tools section of the Inventory screen. Option 2 can also be utilized to change an items condition before the inventory session has been completed. Once Apply has been selected from the Tools section, the condition will be updated from the Inventoried Items grid.

During the inventory process, you can apply Statuses to items. info Versions 9.8.9329.21809 or older will not have the ability to apply Statuses to an item within the Inventory Session. The statuses that are available during the General Inventory process are Broken, Unserviceable, Deactivated, and Lost. To apply a status to an item that has been inventoried, select the item you would like to apply the status to from the Inventoried Items grid then select the status you would like applied. Once the status has been applied, we will mark that item with the selected status within TCMax® and write corresponding log records.

General Inventory provides a reporting feature that allows you to see what items have not been inventoried in your selected Shop Code within a certain time frame. To adjust the date that is displayed in the Reporting section, click the Set Date button. Upon pressing the Set Date button you will be presented with a date picker to select the beginning date for the report. When you click Accept the selected date will be placed in the Date From box. After the date has been selected, click the Display button to view the Report of items that have not been inventoried within the selected date range. Upon selecting the Display button, you will be displayed with an Items Not Inventoried screen.
Condition Barcodes can be generated through the Label Maker screen for a quicker inventory method when scanning items that you would like to apply conditions to.

Condition Barcodes will be created the same way for each Inventory Mode. note Condition Barcodes cannot be used within Shift Inventory because empty holes on the shelf or location is what is being inventoried and not the physical item itself. To generate the condition barcodes, navigate to Tools > Label Maker. From the Label Maker screen, adjust the Label Type to Generic. Upon setting the Label Type as Generic, the right-hand side of the Label Maker screen will display four columns, Number of Labels, Message, Barcode Id, and Description. Manually enter the Conditions into the Barcode Id and Description fields.
The Barcode Id field needs to state <E/> and Description field needs to state Excellent.
The Barcode Id field needs to state <G/> and Description field needs to state Good.
The Barcode Id field needs to state <F/> and Description field needs to state Fair.
The Barcode Id field needs to state <P/> and Description field needs to state Poor.
The Barcode Id field needs to state <N/> and Description field needs to state None.

Once the Condition Barcodes have been printed, you can use your scanner to mark items with a condition during the specific inventory session. During an inventory session, before scanning an item, scan the condition barcode. When the condition barcode has been scanned, the specific condition will be highlighted to show what condition will be applied. Once the condition has been highlight, scan the item you wish to inventory and apply the selected condition to. tip The condition you scan will remain selected until you tell TCMax® otherwise. You will need to scan the condition of 'None' to set the condition back to nothing. For further information on the Generic Label Type and utilizing Label Maker, refer to the Label Maker section in the User Manual.

The Inventory menu option brings up different Inventory Modes that are designed to help you create records and reports that indicate when items have been inventoried, discrepancies that have been generated for items, any Statuses that have been applied to items, or determine the conditions of the items that have been inventoried. To access the Inventory menu with the different Inventory Modes, select Tools > Inventory or press Ctrl + Shift + I on your keyboard. Upon selecting Tools > Inventory or pressing Ctrl + Shift + I, an Inventory Selection menu will appear. The Inventory Selection menu can be utilized to select the specific Inventory Mode you would like to run. The Inventory Selection menu will display four different Inventory Modes, General Inventory, Physical Inventory, Shift Inventory, and Deployment Inventory.

note In TCMax® Version 9.9.0 and newer, physical inventory will account for temporarily transferred or deployed items. If you have an item temporarily transferred or deployed, it will add the temporarily transferred/deployed item to the inventory. The item will appear to be auto inventoried. Under the discrepancy list, the items temporarily transferred/deployed will appear with the Discrepancy of "Not Inventoried", which will show resolved. Select View Notes for those items and this will show you what temporarily transferred location/deployment the item is on.

Physical Inventory is used to inventory a specific kit or collection of items that are associated by parent/child relationships. To access the Physical Inventory menu, select Tools > Inventory > Physical Inventory or press Ctrl + Shift + I on your keyboard then press Physical Inventory. Upon selecting Physical Inventory, the Physical Inventory Setup screen will appear. The Setup screen allows you to set up how you would like the Physical Inventory to be run. From the Physical Inventory Setup screen you will see four different steps. These steps will need information entered into them before you can proceed with the Inventory session. In Step 1, you will select the type of inventory to be performed. Your options are either Full or Partial. A Full Physical Inventory will inventory the kit, its children, and sub-kits (depending on the settings in Step 2). A Partial Physical Inventory is used to inventory a specific sub-kit or storage location within a kit. Step 2 allows you to decide how many generations of the kit you would like to include in the inventory session. To set the generation that you would like to include in the inventory session, move the slider arrow up or down until the generation limit you want is selected. All will include all generations of the kit. Great Grandchildren will inventory three generations of the main kit. Grandchildren will inventory two generations of the main kit. Children will inventory one generation of the main kit. In Step 3, select the Shop Code in which your kit exists from the drop-down menu. note You can only inventory kits from one Shop Code at a time. In Step 4, scan or enter the Barcode Id of the kit to be inventoried.

At any point during the Physical Inventory, if you need to leave the screen to perform other tasks, you can select Close in the bottom right-hand corner of the inventory screen. Upon selecting Close, your inventory session will be paused giving you the option to pick up where you left off when returning to the Physical Inventory Setup screen. If you started an inventory session and did not complete it before leaving the Inventory mode, you can complete the inventory by selecting the Join Existing Inventory tab, highlighting the inventory you wish to complete, and clicking the Join Selected Inventory button. If all your Physical Inventories have been completed and you do not have one that is waiting to be completed, you will not see this tab. The Join Existing Inventory tab only appears when there is an inventory that was started and not completed. If you selected Full Inventory in Step 1, the Physical Inventory screen will open. If you had selected Partial > Kits or Storage Locations, a selection window will open asking you what sub-kit(s) you would like to perform the inventory for. You can select the sub-kit(s) or locations then select the Start button to begin the Physical Inventory for the selected items. The Physical Inventory screen has been optimized to work on both tablet and desktop PCs. You can inventory an item by either double clicking (tapping for touch-enabled devices) on the item in the list or by scanning the item’s Barcode Id. In either case, inventorying the item will place a green checkmark next to the item indicating that it has been inventoried during this session. If you are using a barcode scanner and interact with an item that has been set up as a multiple quantity item, you can enter the quantity for that item in the upper right-hand corner of the screen. The expected quantity will be listed in the Item Details section. If the inventoried quantity matches the expected quantity the item will be marked as inventoried with a green check mark. If the Expected Quantity and Inventoried Quantity don’t match, it will be recorded as having been inventoried with a discrepancy. If "Auto inventory children when parent is scanned" is enabled, through the Options Menu, the system can automatically inventory the children, speeding up the inventory process. When enabled, the user can simply scan/select a parent to inventory all of its components. This feature works for any smaller, sub-kits/item groups that are part of the larger kit (Example - A set of sockets that are stored in a larger tool box). If you inventory an item in error, you can right click on the item and select Reset from the menu that appears. This will reset the item as if it had not been inventoried.

For items with inspections, the item will be red for required/overdue inspections or orange for imminent inspections. There will also be an Inspections group box that appears on the right side of the screen when you select the item. If the item is underlined, then it has an Inventory Inspection loaded against it that must be updated to complete the inventory. To update the inspection, click on it then select the Complete button.

During the inventory process, you can apply Conditions to items. The conditions that are available during the Physical Inventory process are Excellent (E), Good (G), Fair (F), Poor (P), and None (N). Before an item is inventoried, select the button for the condition you would like to apply from the top of the Inventory screen. Once the condition has been selected, scan, type, or double-click on the Barcode Id that you wish to inventory. Upon inventorying the Barcode Id, the item will be inventoried and display with a green checkmark and the condition that was applied.

During the inventory process, you can apply Statuses to items. info Versions 9.8.9329.21809 or older will not have the ability to apply Statuses to an item within the Inventory Session. The statuses that are available during the Physical Inventory process are Broken, Unserviceable, Deactivated, and Lost. To apply a status to an item that has been inventoried or has not been inventoried, select the item you would like to apply the status to from the Items list then select the status you would like applied. Once the status has been applied, we will mark that item with the selected status within TCMax® and write corresponding log records.

Discrepancies are inconsistencies with items that have been discovered/entered during the inventory process. Quantity Did Not Match: This discrepancy is generated during Physical Inventory when the Inventoried Quantity does not match the Expected Quantity. Generic: This discrepancy is generated during Physical Inventory when you right click on the item and select Add Generic Discrepancy. Upon selecting Add Generic Discrepancy, a Discrepancy Note entry screen will appear where you can enter information about the discovered discrepancy. A red x will then appear in the inventory status button for that item. A Discrepancy can be resolved before completing the inventory by clicking on the Discrepancy and selecting the Resolve button. Once you have selected the Resolve button, you will then get a Resolve Discrepancy entry screen which allows you to update the discrepancy’s note. Selecting the Accept button will accept the resolution. The Discrepancy will then be marked as resolved in the Discrepancy List. The item will then be updated with a green checkmark instead of a red X in the inventory status. Does Not Belong in this Inventory: This discrepancy is generated when an item that is not listed as being part of the kit is inventoried. Not Inventoried: This discrepancy is one that cannot be manually added to an item. The discrepancy is generated when you did not inventory items before selecting the Complete Inventory button. This discrepancy cannot be resolved other than re-inventorying the kit and making sure all items are accounted for.

Inventory Notes can be added to items during the Physical Inventory process by highlighting an item and clicking the Add/Edit Note button on the right side of the screen or by right clicking on the item and selecting Add/Edit Note. These Notes are added to the log records and kept for reporting purposes.

If, during the Physical Inventory Session, you have discovered an item that does not belong in the kit, you can remove the item from the selected kit. This function can be accessed by right clicking on the item in question and selecting Remove From Kit.

To complete the Physical Inventory and commit the records to your Database, click the Complete Inventory button in the bottom right-hand corner of the Inventory screen. If any items have been missed from being inventoried, an Items Not Inventoried popup will appear letting you know not all items have been accounted for. You can then choose Yes to complete the inventory anyways, which will create Discrepancies for any item that has not been inventoried, or choose No to go back and inventory any item that was missed. note In TCMax® Version 9.10.0 and newer, you can ask or require for a reviewer to sign off on the inventory. Please see Settings > Inventory Options If the option to Ask or Require a reviewed by user during a Physical Inventory is enabled you will see an additional popup asking for a user id and password. Any TCMax® user with a password can successfully review a Physical Inventory, including the logged in user who is performing the inventory. This user will be logged accordingly.

Shift Inventory is used to account for items that are still issued or multi-quantity items at the time of a shift change. To access the Shift Inventory menu, select Tools > Inventory > Shift Inventory or press Ctrl + Shift + I on your keyboard then press Shift Inventory. Upon selecting Shift Inventory, the Shift Inventory Setup screen will appear. The Setup screen allows you to set up how you would like the Shift Inventory to be run. From the Shift Inventory Setup screen you will see three different steps. These steps will need information entered into them before you can proceed with the Inventory session. In Step 1, you will select the type of inventory to be performed. Your options are either Beginning of Shift or End of Shift. The difference between these two inventory types are the log records that are generated. In Step 2, select the Shop Code you would like to conduct the inventory for. note A Shift Inventory instance can only be ran against one shop at a time. Step 3 can be used to set additional options for your Shift Inventory session. Once you have setup your Shift Inventory, press the Start button on the Shift Inventory Setup screen to start the Shift Inventory.

At any point during the Shift Inventory, if you need to leave the screen to perform other tasks, you can select Close in the bottom right-hand corner of the inventory screen. Upon selecting Close, your inventory session will be paused giving you the option to pick up where you left off when returning to the Shift Inventory Setup screen. If you started an inventory session and did not complete it before leaving the Inventory mode, you can complete the inventory by selecting the Join Existing Inventory tab, highlighting the inventory you wish to complete, and clicking the Join Selected Inventory button. If all your Shift Inventories have been completed and you do not have one that is waiting to be completed, you will not see this tab. The Join Existing Inventory tab only appears when there is an inventory that was started and not completed. Once the Shift Inventory session has been started, you will see your items displayed from the Inventory screen. The Shift Inventory screen has been optimized to work on both tablet and desktop PCs. You can inventory an item by either double clicking (tapping for touch-enabled devices) on the item in the list or by scanning the item’s Barcode Id. In either case, inventorying the item will place a green checkmark next to the item indicating that it has been inventoried during this session. If you are using a barcode scanner and interact with an item that has been set up as a multiple quantity item, you can enter the quantity for that item in the upper right-hand corner of the screen. The expected quantity will be listed in the Item Details section. If the inventoried quantity matches the expected quantity the item will be marked as inventoried with a green checkmark. If the Expected Quantity and Inventoried Quantity don’t match, it will be recorded as having been inventoried with a discrepancy. If you inventory an item in error, you can right click on the item and select Reset from the menu that appears. This will reset the item as if it had not been inventoried.

During the inventory process, you can apply Statuses to items. info Versions 9.8.9329.21809 or older will not have the ability to apply Statuses to an item within the Inventory Session. The statuses that are available during the Shift Inventory process are Broken, Unserviceable, Deactivated, and Lost. To apply a status to an item that has been inventoried or has not been inventoried, select the item you would like to apply the status to from the Items list then select the status you would like applied. Once the status has been applied, we will mark that item with the selected status within TCMax® and write corresponding log records.

Discrepancies are inconsistencies with items that have been discovered/entered during the inventory process. Quantity Did Not Match: This discrepancy is generated during Shift Inventory when the Inventoried Quantity does not match the Expected Quantity. Generic: This discrepancy is generated during Shift Inventory when you right click on the item and select Add Generic Discrepancy. Upon selecting Add Generic Discrepancy, a Discrepancy Note entry screen will appear where you can enter information about the discovered discrepancy. A red x will then appear in the inventory status button for that item. A Discrepancy can be resolved before completing the inventory by clicking on the Discrepancy and selecting the Resolve button. Once you have selected the Resolve button, you will then get a Resolve Discrepancy entry screen which allows you to update the discrepancy’s note. Selecting the Accept button will accept the resolution. The Discrepancy will then be marked as resolved in the Discrepancy List. The item will then be updated with a green checkmark instead of a red X in the inventory status. Does Not Belong in this Inventory: This discrepancy is generated when an item that is not listed is inventoried. Not Inventoried: This discrepancy is one that cannot be manually added to an item. The discrepancy is generated when you did not inventory items before selecting the Complete Inventory button. This discrepancy cannot be resolved other than re-inventorying and making sure all items are accounted for.

Inventory Notes can be added to items during the Shift Inventory process by highlighting an item and clicking the Add/Edit Note button on the right side of the screen or by right clicking on the item and selecting Add/Edit Note. These Notes are added to the log records and kept for reporting purposes.

To complete the Shift Inventory and commit the records to your Database, click the Complete Inventory button in the bottom right-hand corner of the Inventory screen. If any items have been missed from being inventoried, an Items Not Inventoried popup will appear letting you know not all items have been accounted for. You can then choose Yes to complete the inventory anyways, which will create Discrepancies for any item that has not been inventoried, or choose No to go back and inventory any item that was missed.

The Kit Builder screen helps you to build, modify, and duplicate item kits or tool boxes. To access Kit Builder, go to Tools > Kit Builder from the Main Screen of TCMax® or hit Ctrl + K. The Kit Builder screen is divided into two main sections. The left-hand side of the Kit Builder screen will provide a list of different functions that this screen provides. The right-hand side of the Kit Builder screen will display the item/kit layout.
From the File menu, you can select any of the following three options, Add a New Item to the Selected Item/Kit, Print Labels for Selected Item/Kit, or Close.
This option is used to add a new item to the kit (or you could utilize the F3 key on your keyboard).
documents.s: Add a New Item to the Selected Item/Kit

documents.t: This option is used to generate labels for the selected item/kit (or you could utilize Ctrl + P on your keyboard).
This option is used to close the Kit Builder screen and return to the Main Screen of TCMax®.
From the Create/Display Kit to Build section in Kit Builder you will need to select the Shop Code that your kit is or will be in.

To create a new kit, select the Create New Kit button. This will bring up the Add New Item Record screen where you can enter the new kit's information. By default, the Barcode Id will pre-generate with your prefix and suffix that was set from Settings > Options > User and Item Barcodes or the Configure Barcode Format section in Kit Builder. info When adding a new kit, the Barcode Id must be unique within the selected Shop Code. If the value entered is already used by another item in the selected Shop Code, a red exclamation point will appear next to the Barcode Id field. Once you have entered the Items information, press the Save button. note If you need to enter more information for an item than what is shown in the Add New Item Record screen, you will need to edit the item from the Main Screen of TCMax® or Item Search. In Kit Builder, the only information you can enter for a new item is the Barcode Id, Item Name, Storage Location, NSN, Part Number, and Serial Number.

To add items to an already existing kit, type the item/kits Barcode Id into the Enter Kit Id text box, then select the Load Kit button. Once the kit has been loaded, the item layout section will populate with the selected item’s layout. Anything displayed in purple text from the item layout section will indicate the Storage Location that the particular item(s) lives within.

Once you have created a new kit or selected an already existing kit an Enter Item Id section appears under the Create/Display Kit to Build section. In the Enter Item Id textbox enter the Barcode Id of the item you would like to add/remove from the kit and then hit the Enter key on your keyboard or click the Add Item button on the screen.
documents.s: Adding Items to a New/Existing Kit

documents.t: From the Configure Barcode Format section in Kit Builder, you can set the format of the Barcode Ids that TCMax® will assign to items when they are created or duplicated within Kit Builder. In the Parent/Item group box, the barcode Prefix and Suffix can be set. The Prefix is a constant set of characters that start your Barcode; this Data can be alphanumeric. The Suffix is the set of numeric values that TCMax® will automatically increment as new items are created. The Child Suffix can be set so that children of the kit are assigned a Barcode based on their Parent’s Barcode Id. info Both suffix values must be numeric as these fields auto increment.

The Create New Item section will add new items to TCMax® and place them in the selected kit. Selecting the Add New Item button will display the Add New Item Record prompt where you can fill in your new item's information. Once you have filled out the new item’s information, press the Save button to add the item to the selected kit. If you enter a new Storage Location when creating the item, you will see a new Location appear in purple text under the item layout section.

The Duplicate Item(s) from Inventory section is used to duplicate items that already exist within your TCMax® inventory. Within the Kit Builder screen, you can also duplicate items by right clicking them from the item layout section and selecting Duplicate Item. Upon selecting Duplicate Item from the item layout section, you will be prompted with a Duplicate Item screen asking if you wish to duplicate this item inside or outside of the current kit. If you chose to duplicate the item inside the kit, a Barcode Configuration screen will be displayed where you can enter the Times you wish to have this item duplicated, the Barcode Prefix, the Barcode Suffix, and the Child Suffix. If you chose to duplicate the item outside the kit, a Shop Code List screen will be displayed asking which Shop Code you would like to duplicate the item(s) into. Upon selecting the Shop Code, you will be prompted with an Item Duplication screen asking if you would like to duplicate using the same barcode values, if not then you will be prompted with a Barcode Configuration screen. From the Duplicate Item(s) from Inventory section, if you would like to keep the same Barcode Ids for the duplicated items then utilize the Keep the same barcode values from the selected items checkbox. note The Barcode values can only be kept if you are copying the item(s) to a different Shop Code as Barcode Ids must be unique across Shops. To choose which item(s) will be duplicated, select the Search Inventory button. You will notice an Item Search screen appears, this version of the Item Search screen is slightly different than the one accessed via the Main Screen of TCMax®, as it has functionality that will pass our selected items to the Kit Builder screen. From the Item Search screen, you can highlight a row and add the item to your Selected Items grid by clicking the Add Selected Rows button or by double clicking the item you wish to add. You can also use the Item Search functionality to limit the grid and then select the Add All Rows button to add all of the results in the search grid to the Selected Items grid. If you select an item to duplicate that you did not mean to, you can remove it from the Selected Items grid. From the Selected Items grid, select the item you do not want duplicated and click delete on your keyboard. This will remove the item from the list, but not from TCMax® itself. Once you have all the items you wish to duplicate added to the Selected Items grid, select the Finished button located in the bottom right-hand corner of the Item Search screen. Upon selecting the Finished button, you will then be presented with a Barcode Configuration dialog box where you can confirm what Barcode Ids you would like assigned to the item(s), and how many times you want to duplicate the items(s). Once you are satisfied with the Barcode Configuration, select Done. You will then see a Duplicated Items list where you can see what items will be duplicated and what their Barcode Ids will be. Selecting Yes from the Duplicated Items list will duplicate the items. Selecting No from the Duplicated Items list will cancel the duplication. If Yes was selected, you will see a Duplication Successful popup appear indicating the duplication was successful. Press OK through the Duplication Successful popup to view your duplicated items in the kit layout. If No was selected, you will be taken back to the Kit Builder screen.

The Move Item(s) from Inventory section is used to relocate items from your TCMax® inventory and place them in your selected item/kit. To choose which item(s) will be moved, select the Search Inventory button. You will notice an Item Search screen appears, this version of the Item Search screen is slightly different than the one accessed via the Main Screen of TCMax®, as it has functionality that will pass our selected items to the Kit Builder screen. From the Item Search screen, you can highlight a row and add the item to your Selected Items grid by clicking the Add Selected Rows button or by double clicking the item you wish to add. You can also use the Item Search functionality to limit the grid and then select the Add All Rows button to add all of the results in the search grid to the Selected Items grid. If you select an item to relocate that you did not mean to, you can remove it from the Selected Items grid. From the Selected Items grid, select the item you do not want relocate and click delete on your keyboard. This will remove the item from the list, but not from TCMax® itself. Once you have all the items you wish to relocate added to the Selected Items grid, select the Finished button located in the bottom right-hand corner of the Item Search screen. Upon selecting the Finished button, you will then be presented with a Relocated Items list where you can see what items will be relocated. note If the item(s) you selected already live within a kit then you will be prompted with a Child Item(s) screen. This will indicate if you continue with this selection that the item will be removed from the original kit and added to the selected item/kit. Selecting Yes from the Child Item(s) screen will move the item(s) to the selected kit. Selecting Yes from the Relocated Items list will relocate the item(s). Selecting No from the Relocated Items list will cancel the relocation. If Yes was selected, you will see a Relocation Successful popup appear indicating the relocation was successful. Press OK through the Relocation Successful popup to view your relocated items in the kit layout. If No was selected, you will be taken back to the Kit Builder screen.
From Kit Builder, there is two options on removing items from kit.
To remove items from a kit, right click on the item to be removed from the kit layout section and select Remove Item from Parent.

To remove items from a kit, drag and drop the selected item to the tool-box icon located in the bottom right-hand corner of the kit layout screen. info By removing an item, you are not deleting the item from TCMax®. The item being removed will still exist in the Database, it will just no longer be a child of the parent and have no relationship to that parent.

The View Selected Item Details section is used to show you the details of the item you have selected from the kit layout section of Kit Builder. The only information that can be adjusted from this section is the item’s Storage Location.

The Kit Builder has a drag and drop feature to easily move or adjust the layout of the kit. From the Kit Layout, you can click and drag an item to a new storage location to relocate that item within the kit. You can also click and drag an item into another item to create a separate parent-child relationship and create a grandchild of the overall kit. TCMax® offers a drag and drop for ease of use when viewing and changing the layout of a kit.

Course Labels are used with the Training Completion and Add/Remove Training Modes of Operation. These Labels are utilized to add or complete courses for a user. When Course is selected in the Label Type drop down, a Courses section will appear on the left-hand side of the Label Maker screen. The Load All Courses button will load all of the courses that are in the current visible shop codes drop down. The Load From Course Search button will open the Course Search screen from which you can select the courses you would like to print labels for. The Add Selected Rows button from Course Search will add the highlighted row to the grid in the lower right-hand corner of the screen. The Add All Rows button from Course Search will add all of the rows displayed in the main grid to the grid in the lower right-hand corner of the screen. The lower right-hand grid is the selection that will be passed to Label Maker. When you have all the Courses selected that you would like to print Labels for, select the Finished button to return to the Label Maker screen. When you return to the Label Maker screen, the Courses you selected in Course Search will populate in the grid on the right-hand side of the Label Data tab. The columns within the preview grid can be sorted by clicking on the specific column header. Once the specific column header is selected, the column will order ascending to descending or vice versa. For example, the image below will display the Barcode Id column ascending to descending. The image below will display the Barcode Id column descending to ascending. Along with the sorting feature, you can also reorder columns to move them to a different location. For example, the image below will display the Name column in between the 'Number of Labels' column and the 'Course Number' column. The image below will display the reorder of the Name column. You will notice the Name column is now the first column and is located next to the 'Barcode Id' column. info If at any point you need to remove a row from the preview grid, select the row you wish to remove and hit the Delete key on your keyboard.

The Generic option allows the user to print generic Labels. When Generic is selected in the Label Type drop down, you will have the capability of creating a Generic Label. To create a Generic Label, click into any field in the new row (the row is indicated by an asterisk) and enter Data.

To access Label Maker, select Tools > Label Maker. The Label Maker feature in TCMax® can be utilized to print labels in bulk, as opposed to one at a time from the Main Screen. The Label Maker screen is separated into two tabs, Label Data and Print.
The Label Data tab will provide different options that allow you to select what Label Type you are printing for along with different options that allow you to gather information for the Labels.

The Tools option allows you to preview the labels to be printed by clicking the Show Label Preview button. If you have Data displayed in the grid on the right-hand side of the Label Maker screen that information will be added to the label preview. If no information is loaded into the grid, sample Data will be included. Within the Tools option, you will also have the capability of selecting the Clear All Label Data button which will clear the grid on the right-hand side of the Label Maker screen.

The Label Maker screen can load and save Data Files. Data Files are Files containing a list of Data to be printed. To create a Data File, populate the grid with the items you would like included and select the Save Data File button. A File Explorer Window will be displayed where you can set the name of the File and the location for the File to be saved to. To load a pre-existing Data File, select the Load Data File button then select the File you would like to load. This will populate the grid with the items that had been saved to that File.

TCMax® allows you to print several types of labels for various uses within TCMax®. The Label Types consist of Course, Generic, Item, Template, or User. To view further information on specific Label Types, select the link above for the specific Label Type you wish to view.

The Custom Message menu option allows you to include a custom message on Labels. The Placement drop down allows you to select where the message will be displayed on the Label. The Message text box allows you to set the message to be printed on the Labels.

The Print tab will have options/settings that allow you to print your Labels to your specifications. This tab is split into two sections. The left-hand section of the Print tab allows you to modify your label definition and details, select your printer, and print your Labels. The right-hand section of the Print tab allows you to preview the Label(s) that will be printed. Within the preview section (at the bottom of the screen), you can set the preview zoom setting and also view the label material dimensions. info The Label Material Dimensions are not editable from the Label Maker screen. The values that are listed are pulled from the selected print driver, if the Dimensions need adjusted, please refer to your Windows System Settings.
The Modify Label Definition button will open the Label Configuration screen. See the Label Configuration section for a walkthrough of this screen.
The Modify Label Details button will open the Configure Label Details screen. See the Configure Label Details section for a walkthrough of this screen.
The Printer menu allows you to select which printer the Labels will be sent to.
The Print button will send the Labels to the printer to be printed.
Label Configuration allows you to configure the Labels to be printed.

The Label Definition tab allows you to load settings from a definition file by clicking the Load Definition from File button. Within the Label Definition tab you will also have the capability to save the current settings to a Label Definition File by clicking the Save Definition to File button.

The Page Layout tab allows you to set the Page Settings for the Label. The Settings include Unit of Measure (inches or millimeters), Margins (left or right), and Columns and Rows such as Number of Columns, Number of Rows, and distances between the Columns and Rows. tip From the Page Layout tab, under the Margins section, you can select the blue question mark to provide information on what left margin and right margin signify. tip From the Page Layout tab, under the Columns and Rows section, you can select the blue question mark to provide information on that section.

The Barcode/Label tab allows you to set the Label Settings and Barcode Settings for the Label(s) that will be printed. Once you have your settings the way you would like them you can hit the Save Changes button. tip From the Barcode/Label tab, under the Label Settings section, you can select the blue question mark to provide information on that section. tip From the Barcode/Label tab, under the Barcode Settings section, you can select the blue question mark to provide information on that section.

The Label Details screen allows you to set what information you would like printed on a specific type of Label. From the Configure Label Details screen, select the Label Type you wish to set information for. With each Label Type you will have four details that can be set. Selecting the dropdown boxes for Details #1-4 allow you to set what information you would like to print on that type of Label.

The Hidden Character Prefix will append a prefix to the Barcode that will not appear in the text that is displayed on the Label. This feature helps you track exactly how users are issuing and turning in items. For example, place any character in this box, one character only, example: T. When you print your Barcode Labels, the Label Maker program will automatically embed another character and the character of your choice in the Barcode. The clear text of the Barcode will appear on the Label without both characters. TCMax® will automatically strip both characters when you scan this Barcode, and it will place the characters in front of the user’s name in the log entry. This allows for you to know automatically if the user scanned a Barcode or typed the Barcode from the keyboard.

When Item is selected in the Label Type drop down, an Items section will appear on the left-hand side of the Label Maker Screen. The Load All Items button will load all of the items that are in the current visible shop codes drop down. The Load From Item Search button will open the Item Search screen from which you can select the items you would like to print labels for. The Add Selected Rows button from Item Search will add the highlighted row to the grid in the lower left-hand corner of the screen. The Add All Rows button from Item Search will add all of the rows displayed in the main grid to the grid in the lower right-hand corner of the screen. The lower right-hand grid is the selection that will be passed to the Label Maker. When you have all the Items selected that you would like to print Labels for, select the Select button to return to the Label Maker screen. When you return to the Label Maker screen, the Items you selected in Item Search will populate in the grid on the right-hand side of the Label Data tab. The columns within the preview grid can be sorted by clicking on the specific column header. Once the specific column header is selected, the column will order ascending to descending or vice versa. For example, the image below will display the Barcode Id column ascending to descending. The image below will display the Barcode Id column descending to ascending. tip If at any point you need to remove a row from the preview grid, select the row you wish to remove and hit the Delete key on your keyboard.

Template Labels allow you to create multiple Labels with different Barcode numbers, while having the same Part Number. To utilize this feature, you first must have the specific Part Numbers created in Tools > Catalog Setup as template Barcodes require the use of existing Part Numbers to be generated. When Template is selected in the Label Type drop down, a Template section will appear on the left-hand side of the Label Maker screen. The Create Template Barcodes button will bring up the Template Barcode Setup screen. On the Template Barcode Setup screen, enter the Part Number into the Catalog Entry field and select the Search button or hit Enter on your keyboard. If the Part Number entered is found, it will be displayed next to Barcode Preview. In the Quantity field, enter how many template labels you want printed for this Part Number. In the Barcode Prefix and Barcode Suffix fields, enter the prefix and suffix that you wish to be used for each Label. info This will be the unique identifier for each item. When you have the Template Barcode Setup screen filled out, select the Done button to return to the Label Maker screen. When you return to the Label Maker screen, the Items you created Template Barcodes for will populate in the grid on the right-hand side of the Label Data tab. The columns within the preview grid can be sorted by clicking on the specific column header. Once the specific column header is selected, the column will order ascending to descending or vice versa. For example, the image below will display the Barcode Id column ascending to descending. The image below will display the Barcode Id column descending to ascending. Along with the sorting feature, you can also reorder columns to move them to a different location. For example, the image below will display the Barcode Id column next to the 'Part Number Value' column. The image below will display the reorder of the Barcode Id column. You will notice the Barcode Id column is now the first column and is located next to the 'Number of Labels' column. tip If at any point you need to remove a row from the preview grid, select the row you wish to remove and hit the Delete key on your keyboard.

When User is selected in the Label Type drop down, a Users section will appear on the left-hand side of the Label Maker screen. The Load All Users button will load all of the users assigned to your selected site. The Load Specific Users button will open the Select Users to Add screen. From the Select Users To Add screen, select a user by highlighting their row and clicking the Add Selected button. This will display the user in the main grid in the right-hand side of the screen. The right-hand grid is the selection that will be passed to Label Maker. When you have all the Users selected that you would like to print Labels for, select the Done button to return to the Label Maker screen. When you return to the Label Maker screen, the Users you selected will populate in the grid on the right-hand side of the Label Data tab. The columns within the preview grid can be sorted by clicking on the specific column header. Once the specific column header is selected, the column will order ascending to descending or vice versa. Along with the sorting feature, you can also reorder columns to move them to a different location. For example, the image below will display the Username column next to the 'Number of Labels' column. The image below will display the reorder of the Username column. You will notice the Username column is now the first column and is located next to the 'Number of Labels' column. tip If at any point you need to remove a row from the preview grid, select the row you wish to remove and hit the Delete key on your keyboard.
The Log Search menu option brings up a search screen that allows for you to view the log entries created by any event in TCMax® and filter them. To access this screen, select Tools > Log Search.
The File menu option located in the upper left-hand corner will allow for you to Close the Log Search screen.

The Export to Excel menu option located in the upper left-hand corner will allow for the user to export the results that are displayed in the table to an Excel spreadsheet. tip You can also right-click in the table at any time and send the displayed Data to an Excel spreadsheet.
The Print menu option located in the upper left-hand corner will allow for the user to print a report with the records that are displayed in the results table.

Log Search gives the user several search options. These Search Options can be located from the upper left-hand corner of the Log Search screen. Search Options > Grid Limit will allow for you to adjust the Log Search grid limit. The default grid limit is 1,000 records. This Search Option allows for you to set the value up to 10,000 records. Search Options > Add Shops across Sites will display Log Records for Shop Codes even if they exist in other Sites.
The Help menu option located in the upper left-hand corner will contain information on Search Filters and the Log Search Grid Limit.

To utilize the Log Search feature, enter text in any of the search text boxes and hit Tab or Enter. The results table will show you only the entries that match the criteria that was entered into that specific field. Along with the search text boxes, the Log Search screen offers a Filters section that allows for you to search and limit the results to a Specific Event Type, Shop Code, and Username. The Username option within the Filters section allows for you to Filter by Logged in Username which will display results based on what user was logged into TCMax at the time. If you wish to clear the Log Search criteria, select the Clear Search Criteria button located in the upper right-hand section of the screen.
For example, if 751 is entered into the Barcode Id field the results grid will immediately reflect any actions that happened with Barcode Id '751'.

For example, if you wanted to run a log search on just the issue/turn records for all items in a specific shop code that were issued by a certain user you can do so by using the Event Type, Shop Code, and Username options. Once the Filters section has been filled out, the results grid will adjust accordingly to locate any results that match the selected criteria. note All columns can be arranged and sorted by dragging the column header to a new position and/or selecting the column header to order them by ascending or descending.

To access the Maintenance History menu, select Tools > Maintenance History or press Ctrl + W on your keyboard. note If there is an item displayed on the Main Screen when you access the Maintenance History screen, the item displayed will be selected by default.
The File menu option located in the upper left-hand corner will allow you to Close the Maintenance History screen.
The Settings menu option located in the upper left-hand corner will allow you to Load an Existing Work Order.
The Print Work Order History menu option located in the upper left-hand corner will print a Report that shows the Work Order History for the Item loaded on the Maintenance History screen.

If you enter the Maintenance History screen without an item displayed on the Main Screen or wish to work with a different item than the one originally selected, enter an Item Id in the Enter Item Id text box then hit the Enter key on your keyboard or click the Load Item button. Once an item is displayed in the Item Maintenance History section, causes can be added to the item by right clicking on the item and selecting Add Cause or by clicking the Add Cause button on the right-hand side of the screen. A cause refers to the reason for which a problem was found. You can enter information for the cause on the right-hand side of the screen when you have a cause selected. If you have more than one cause for an item, you can enter more than one cause by right clicking on the item and selecting Add Cause again, or by selecting the item and clicking the Add Cause button again. Once a cause has been added you can add a discrepancy to the cause. You can right click on the cause and select Add Discrepancy or click the Add Discrepancy button on the right-hand side of the screen. A discrepancy refers to the specific issue needing addressed. When you have a discrepancy selected, you can enter in further information about the discrepancy on the right-hand side of the screen. The Completed checkbox can be checked to indicate all work needed for that discrepancy has been completed. You can always come back and select the discrepancy to complete at a later date. If you have more than one discrepancy for an item, you can enter more than one discrepancy by right clicking on the cause and selecting Add Discrepancy again, or by selecting the cause and clicking the Add Discrepancy button again. Once a discrepancy has been added you can add Actions to that discrepancy. An action is the work required to mitigate the discrepancy. You can add multiple Actions to a discrepancy if multiple actions are required. To add multiple Actions, after adding the Action either right click on the discrepancy and select Add Action or click on the discrepancy and select the Add Action button again on the right. You can also print a work order at this point by clicking the Print Work Order button with a discrepancy highlighted. The work order that is generated will list all actions that have been entered for the discrepancy.

If you would like to load an existing work order for an item that may need completed or more actions added to, press the Load Existing Work Order button. note You will need to know your Work Order Number in order to Load an Existing Work Order. Once you have entered a Work Order Number, press OK. Your item that Work Order Number is associated with will appear on the screen. You will see not only the Work Order Number you loaded, but you will see any causes, discrepancies, or actions that are associated with this item. To view information for the causes, discrepancies, or actions, select the specific one you wish to view details for and the details will display on the right-hand side of the Maintenance History screen. info If a discrepancy has not been marked completed, the discrepancy will be in Red writing. If the discrepancy has been completed, the discrepancy will be in Green writing.

A Maintenance Procedure is a specific task within an organization that requires a certain set of items and/or equipment to perform. From the Main Screen, you can scan or type a Maintenance Procedure barcode number into the input box and TCMax® will print a complete list of the items and/or equipment required for this procedure, where they are stored, and who is currently using them.
Maintenance Procedures will be setup and managed through the Setup Maintenance Procedures / Bulk Issues screen. To access this screen, select Tools > Maintenance Procedure / Bulk Issue Setup.

To create a new Maintenance Procedure, select the Add New Maintenance Procedure button and enter in the procedure’s information. Once all Data is entered, press the Save button to create the Maintenance Procedure.
From the Maintenance Procedure screen, refer to the Select Maintenance Procedure section and utilize the drop down to select a Maintenance Procedure.
Once you have selected a Maintenance Procedure, a table will display with the items and/or equipment that have been added to the selected procedure.
documents.s: Viewing Items that are Assigned to a Maintenance Procedure

documents.t: To add items to a Maintenance Procedure, refer to the Add Item to Maintenance Procedure box then enter/scan the Part Number/Barcode Id of the item you wish to add. note The item in which you are adding must have a Part Number assigned. Upon entering/scanning the Part Number/Barcode Id, the table will display the Quantity and Part Number of the Item you added. For multi-quantity items, click in the Quantity column, enter the desired amount, and hit Enter. info When adding items to a Maintenance Procedure, you will notice the Part Number is what appears in the details for each item. Therefore, if you require two items with the same Part Number, you will need to increase your quantity of the Part Number.
documents.s: Adding Items to a Maintenance Procedure

documents.t: To remove an item from a Maintenance Procedure, select the item from the table to highlight the entire row then press the Delete key on your keyboard. Upon hitting Delete, the item will be removed from the table.
documents.s: Deleting Items from a Maintenance Procedure

documents.t: To delete a Maintenance Procedure, select the Procedure you wish to delete then press the Delete button from the Setup Maintenance Procedures / Bulk Issues screen. A confirmation window will appear asking if you are sure you want to continue with the Delete. Press Yes. Upon hitting Yes, the Maintenance Procedure will be removed.

Bulk Issues are designed to issue several items (usually expendables) with a single scan. This works similar to items in a kit (toolbox) but does not require the items to be within the same kit. note If you are issuing multiple items using a bulk issue that will need turned in, these items will have to be turned in individually. Bulk Issue will issue the items out in bulk with a single scan but will not return the items with a single scan. They would need returned individually.

To access this screen, select Tools > Maintenance Procedure / Bulk Issue Setup. Once on the Setup Maintenance Procedures / Bulk Issues screen, select the Bulk Issues tab located at the bottom of the screen.
To create a Bulk Issue, select the Add New Bulk Issue button and enter in the bulk issue information. Once all Data is entered, press the Save button to create the Bulk Issue.
From the Bulk Issue screen, refer to the Select Bulk Issue section and utilize the drop down to select a Bulk Issue.
Once you have selected a Bulk Issue, a table will display with the items that have been added to the selected Bulk Issue.
documents.s: Viewing Items that are Assigned to a Bulk Issue

documents.t: To add items to a Bulk Issue, refer to the Add Item to Bulk Issue box then enter/scan the Barcode Id of the item you wish to add. Upon entering/scanning the Barcode Id, the table will display the Quantity, Barcode Id, and Item Name of the Item you added. For multi-quantity items, click in the Quantity column, enter the desired amount, and hit Enter.
documents.s: Adding Items to a Bulk Issue

documents.t: To remove an item from a Bulk Issue, select the item from the table to highlight the entire row then press the Delete key on your keyboard. Upon hitting Delete, the item will be removed from the table.
documents.s: Deleting Items from a Bulk Issue

documents.t: To delete a Bulk Issue, select the Bulk Issue you wish to delete then press the Delete button from the Setup Maintenance Procedures / Bulk Issues screen. A confirmation window will appear asking if you are sure you want to continue with the Delete. Press Yes. Upon hitting Yes, the Bulk Issue will be removed.

To go along with the Report Designer and Status Tracker Builder, we have included a Package Builder which allows a user to import/export their custom reports, trackers, and charts. The Package Builder is located under Tools > Package Builder from the Main Screen of TCMax®. When a package is imported/exported from Package Builder it will be saved as a SDP file type.

To import a package, select the Import tab. From the Import tab, select the Load button, which will bring up a File Explorer Window that will allow you to select the package to import. Once the package is selected you can click the Open button and you will see a list of custom items that are included in the package. Once the information has been loaded on the Import tab, select the items you wish to import into TCMax® then select the Import button. TCMax® will prompt you to select which Shop Codes the items will be imported to. Select the Shop Code(s) and click the Accept button. Your custom items will be imported. If there are conflicts you will be presented with a screen explaining what issues exist and how you would like to proceed. In this case, we can choose to update them or ignore them. You can make your selection and click Continue. Once the import process finishes you will be presented with a dialog screen and will see the results in the Package Builder Output Window.

To export a package, select the Export tab. From the Export tab, select the custom items you want to export by checking the checkbox next to the items to be included in the package. Once the information has been selected from the Export tab, select the Export button. A File Explorer Window will appear that will allow you to select where the package will be exported to.

Discontinued The hardware and operating system used for the PPC Sync has been discontinued by their manufacturers and distributors and is no longer advised to use from Soaring Software Solutions, Inc.

To access PPC Sync, select Tools > PPC Sync from the Main Screen of TCMax®. If your device is connected, the PPC Sync screen will appear. For Windows to handshake with your Pocket PC’s operating system you need to have Windows Mobile Device Center installed. To sync, you must close TCMaxMobile™ on the Pocket PC.

The Purge PPC Database button from the PPC Sync screen will remove all records currently within the Pocket PCs Database. The status message thread will change and let you know what specific action is being performed in this operation. When this operation is complete you will see a ‘Purge Complete’ message.

The Shop Codes section from the PPC Sync screen gives the user the ability to select which shops records you want to sync with. Select All and Clear All buttons help the user in selecting their shops. Once the appropriate Shop Codes have been selected, click the Sync button and the sync process will begin. You will notice that the message thread and status bar will update the user on what function of the sync process is being performed. When the sync is complete, TCMax® will return the user back to the Main Screen. The user can then undock the PPC device and run TCMaxMobile™. note Pocket PCs have very little RAM and limited processor speeds. It is considered best practice to only sync shops that you intend on working into the Pocket PC. This will minimize the amount of time it takes to sync and will help keep the Pocket PC operating as fast as possible.

info It’s important to remember that the PPC and TCMaxMobile™ do not interact in real time with your desktop version of TCMax®. While some models have Bluetooth or wireless capabilities, these technologies are not utilized by TCMaxMobile™. The PPC has its own Windows operating system and Database and operates independent of any connection to the desktop version of TCMax®. Typical Use​ (Optional) Purge old Data from PPC Database Sync the shops required to perform your tasks Take the PPC to wherever you need it and do your inventory, update quantities, issue or turn-in items, etc. When you’re done doing the work on the PPC you need to dock it and sync to bring over the records of everything you did on the PPC to your desktop version of TCMax®.
info Reports that are not already offered within TCMax®, can be created as a Custom Report. A Custom Report can be built for you as an additional paid for service.

The Report Designer can be used to create a brand-new report or edit an existing TCMax® report. It can be accessed by navigating to Tools > Report Designer from the menu bar on the home screen of TCMax®.
There are two major screens to the Report Designer, Designer, and Preview screens. These screens are located near the bottom left-hand corner of the window.
When entering the Report Designer, the Designer screen is the first visible screen. The Designer window is where the report controls and fields are created and customized.

The Preview screen will show a preview of the reporting window while running the report. This preview window is limited to 10 pages of Data which will truncate additional pages. If there are any errors in the report design or script, those will display at the top of the report preview. note Due to the complexity and variables of reports, the next sections cover basic features, not specific scenarios.

To modify a built-in TCMax® report, the report must first be imported to the Report Designer. Once imported, modifications can be made to the layout and design of the report. However, changes cannot be made to the underlying data or data source of the report. To enter the Report Designer, navigate to Tools > Report Designer. From the Report Designer, go to File > Import or press Ctrl + Shift + I on your keyboard. This will bring up the import window where you can browse for an existing exported report or choose to import one of the built-in reports that TCMax® already has. To import an exported report file, use the Browse button in Option 1 to navigate to that file. To import the desired built-in report, clicking Option 2’s dropdown box will display a list of built-in reports. note Not all built-in reports can be selected for import. With the report selected from Option 1 or Option 2, select the Import button at the bottom of the Import window. Step 1 from the Save Report window will ask for a report name. Step 2 from the Save Report window can limit the report to specific shops. If any shop should be able to access the report, select No and click Save. Once the report has been saved, TCMax® will ask to enable the new report for end users. Selecting Yes will make the report accessible from the Reports screen under "User Generated Reports" tab. To enable the report later, select the Tools > Manage Reports menu option within the Report Designer window once the report has been finalized. From the Report Management screen, you can also set a description for the report and if desired, you can let the report override one of the built-in reports within TCMax®. For example, you may repurpose a Part Number field on a report such as Item Inventory Report to instead reflect a custom text box field that is a part of the items details. By overriding the original report you will now see the modified report when you run the Item Inventory Report.

The Database Enumerations window will assist you with locating the enumeration associated with certain item, inspections, and event logs. For example, you may want to create a report to see all the log history of items being marked as Deactivated. This tool helps you quickly find the EventType used in the script/query.

Refer to the Help Menu for information regarding the Report Parameters, Script Functions, and searching the Database Enumerations. Report Parameters Window Script Functions Window Database Enumerations Window
Although not required, it is good practice to use a lower-case p in front of your report parameters.

This prefix is used when we want the group box containing the parameter to be red (denoting the parameter is required for the report to run). Any required parameter that has not been filled out before the report is attempted to be run will cause the report viewer to display a warning about filling out required criteria and cancel the report run.
This prefix is used to look for settings for the report that are not asked as criteria in the right-hand pane of the viewer. (Example: Report Options screen to configure the MIL.)
This parameter must be of type string. We use this to capture signature data to display on the report.

This parameter must be of type boolean. This adds the parameter to a special list denoting that it must be grouped with other sort parameters allowing the user to only choose one. When we have only one parameter with this prefix, the control generated will be a checkbox. When we have more than one parameter with this prefix, the controls generated will be radio buttons. If you set the default value of one of the parameters to true, the viewer will start with that option already selected.

This parameter must be of type boolean. This adds the parameter to a special list denoting that it must be grouped with other parameters with the same prefix; allowing the user to only choose one. When we have only one parameter with this prefix, the control generated will be a checkbox. When we have more than one parameter with this prefix, the controls generated will be radio buttons. If you set the default value of one of the parameters to true, the viewer will start with that option already selected.
