Often times it is easiest to import an existing report and strip out the unnecessary elements to use it as a template. However, in some situations you may want to design your very own report from scratch. The left hand side of the Report Designer screen gives you access to create or drag and drop different elements into your report to begin your design. When creating a report you will want to pay attention to the upper right-hand corner of this Report Designer screen. The upper right-hand corner is where the report elements are displayed and grouped. Within the image below, you will notice there is a report that contains a PageHeader, Detail, and a PageFooter. There is also a Parameters element that can include many pre-built parameters that you want to include prior to running the report, such as the Shop Code or Date and Time. The lower right-hand corner of the screen is where you modify and configure your elements. From here you can also adjust the ScriptLanguage to VB.NET.

By navigating to the Report Query menu option you can Create/Modify Query. This is referred to as the Query Builder. In the Query Builder you can select the fields for the report and set any conditions, grouping, or sorting from this window. When building the query, be sure to occasionally switch over to the Data tab to verify this query is returning Data as expected.

Adding parameters to a report is also done through the Query Builder. You will notice, from the image above that @pShopCodeID and @pCustomCombo1 is referenced in the query/table Criteria. Once you have called a parameter navigate to Report > Report Parameters. The Query Parameters window is displayed, showing you all the parameters that have been called. As directed in the message at the bottom of this window, double click in the Value cell to configure your parameter. In this case, @pShopCodeID refers to a built-in parameter and @pCustomCombo1 is a user-defined parameter and will be a generic input box. You can decide how you want to configure your parameters and how they should behave. For a list of built-in parameters and functions check out the sub-sections under the Help Menu Options.

The Restock feature allows you to restock items with like Part Numbers when your quantities fall below set values. Before using the Restock functionality, there are few key points you must be aware of: The item to be restocked must have a Max in Stock value set for that item. This value is needed as it is how TCMax® knows how many items are needed to restock the item to par value. Items marked as spares are given a higher restock priority than items not marked as spares. Items may need to be restocked because they are consumable/expendable items that have been issued and their quantity on hand has fallen below the Max in Stock value or the item quantity was found to be deficient during a physical inventory. To use the restock functionality, go to Tools > Restock or press Ctrl + Shift + R on your keyboard to open the Item Restock screen.

Selecting the Stock button will bring up a dialog box where you can load an item directly from your stock. You need to specify the Shop Code the item to be restocked is in and enter its Barcode Id into the Enter Barcode Id entry box. If you hit the Enter key some of the important item’s details will be displayed on this dialog box. You can also specify the Shop from which you will pull the item from. Once your Data has been entered, you can click the Select button and the Item Restock screen will display the item you selected. Your results will appear as either green, yellow, or red. When you expand the details for an item you will see a breakdown of the item you are restocking (left) and the stock you are pulling from (right). Green indicates that not only has a match been found but the stock you are pulling from has a sufficient available quantity to top off the item to its max in stock value. Yellow indicates that a match has been found but the quantity available is not enough to fulfill the max in stock threshold for the item. Red indicates that either no match has been found or there is no available quantity to pull from. At this point you can either manually enter information to pull stock from or correct any identified discrepancies. The lookup button will allow you to query the Item Search screen to locate an item on several parameters. Once you are satisfied with the results and everything looks good you can select the Accept button to transfer the available stock into the destination stock, properly updating quantities and creating corresponding log records. info If more than one match has been found then the corresponding Shop Code and Barcode Id dropdown box will allow you to change where you are restocking from. TIP: You can restock an entire kit by entering the Parent Barcode Id and pulling several items at once. TIP: Pay attention to the icon in the lower right corner of the results. If there is a discrepancy, then a tooltip will be displayed upon hovering over this icon for details.

The restock screen can also populate Data based off shortages discovered during Physical Inventories. To load the screen based on this information click the Previous Inventories button. You will then need to select the kit containing the items you would like to restock by selecting it from the Select a kit dropdown menu. You can optionally select the Shop which the stock will be pulled from. Once you have made your choices, click the Select button. Once you have matched the items you would like to restock with the stock that they will pull from, the Accept button can be clicked to make the changes in TCMax®. When you click the Accept button, you will be asked if you would like to perform the restock automatically. Clicking Yes will remove the items from spare stock and replenish the items being restocked.

Clicking No will remove the items from spare stock but will not replenish the items being restocked. You will have to go back into the Inventory Selection screen to complete the restock process. To do an Inventory Restock you will then need to navigate to Tools > Inventory and then click the Restock button. A Physical Inventory Setup dialog will open where you can choose the kit that contains the items you need to restock. Highlight the kit you want to restock and click Perform Restock. This will open a modified Inventory screen with the items that need restocked listed, so you can inventory the items as they are replenished. To restock your items, you can scan, tap, or double click the listed item or single click it and adjust the Inventoried Quantity. Finally, Select the Complete Inventory button in the bottom right corner of the screen to complete the process.

If you checked the option to Check to print receipts, two receipts will be generated. One will include the list of items that need restocked and the other is a list of items to pull from spares to restock those items.

Selecting the Tools > Set Location Status menu option from the Main Screen allows you view, enable or disable a Work Location in TCMax®. Work Locations are used to show you where items have been issued. From this screen, you can add new locations and block/unblock specific work locations from having items issued to them. note It is possible for users to caption the Work Location field to something more consistent with their issue operations. For example, many customers will change the caption from Work Location to Job Number for them to track which job(s) assets are being used on. That caption will change to Job Number on many reports and screens. For this document, we will refer to these fields as the Work Location or Location. The same functionality will exist regardless of how you’ve changed that caption.

To add a new Work Location, click Location Options > Add New Location and the Add New Location screen appears. From the drop-down box, select the Shop Code that this Work Location is associated with or if it should be visible for all Shop Codes, select the All Shops option. Once the Shop Code or Shop Codes have been selected, enter the Location Name into the Location Name textbox then click the Save button. The Work Location should now be visible from the Set Location Status screen. info By default, the newly added Work Location will be blocked (red), meaning that no items can be issued to it.

TCMax® can temporarily prevent certain Work Locations to be used by blocking them from the Set Location Status screen. Example: A Work Location may be blocked if the Location is hazardous/dangerous due to an incident, etc.

To block a Location, locate the Location you wish to block from the Set Location Status screen then press the Location button. note From the Set Location Status screen, you will notice under the Location you can view how items are currently issued to that particular Location. With that being said, you can block a Location that still has items issued to it, however, no new items would be able to be issued to that Location. The Location will then appear red which indicates the Location is blocked and cannot be used as an issue Location. info If from Settings > Options > Work Location Options, the Display Location Button option is enabled when a Location is blocked it will be removed from that window when issuing items.

To unblock a Location, locate the Location you wish to unblock from the Set Location Status screen then press the Location button. The Location will then appear blue which indicates the Location is unblocked and can be used as an issue Location.

To delete Locations that are appearing on the Set Location Status screen, you must go to Settings > Options. From Options, navigate to Work Location Options. Under Work Location Options, select Display Location Buttons. Work Locations will appear based on the Shop Code selection from the Options menu. Once you have selected your Shop Code, select the Work Location you wish to delete then hit the Delete key on your keyboard. Upon hitting Delete, the Work Location will be removed from the grid on the Options menu. Once you are finished deleting locations, select the Save button at the bottom of the Options menu.

Shop codes in TCMax® are used to separate Data between shops or organizations. When/if you want to transfer ownership from one shop to another shop you can utilize the Shop Code Transfer feature in TCMax® to transfer single items, kits, or an entire shop code.

The Shop Code Transfer feature can be accessed by selecting Tools > Shop Code Transfer. Once Shop Code Transfer is selected, a separate Transfer Shop Code screen will be displayed where you can enter the appropriate information to transfer single items, kits, or the entire shop.

In Step 1, you will see two sections of information that need filled in, Select Shop Code To Transfer From and Select Shop Code To Transfer To. In the Select Shop Code To Transfer From section, select the Shop Code you want the item(s) to be transferred from. Next, in the Select Shop Code To Transfer To section, select the Shop Code you want the item(s) to be transferred to. If the Shop Code you want to transfer items to does not yet exist, select the Create New Shop option from the dropdown list. Once you perform an action in Step 2 you will be prompted with a New Shop Code Name screen. This screen will allow for you to enter the name of the new Shop Code you wish to transfer the item(s) to. After the new Shop Code name is entered in the text box, select OK to save the changes. TCMax® will take you back to the Shop Code Transfer screen where the newly created Shop Code will be available to transfer more items to.

In Step 2, you will see two options that are available, Option A: Transfer Single Item/Kit and Option B: Transfer Whole Shop. If you are transferring individual items or an entire kit, refer to Option A: Transfer Single Item/Kit. With the focus in Option A, scan or type in the desired Barcode Id of the item/kit that you wish to transfer from one shop to another. Once the desired Barcode Id has been entered, TCMax® will say 'Transferred' after each scan. If you are transferring an entire Shop Code, refer to Option B: Transfer Whole Shop. In Option B, select the Transfer Entire Shop button. A dialog box will appear asking you to confirm that you want to transfer the entire Shop Code. If you click Yes, TCMax® will say 'Transferred', letting you know that the action has been performed. If you click No, the process will be cancelled. warning Event logs tied to items do not update with the new Shop Code during transfers. As a result, reports relying on Shop Code parameters may not function correctly for historical data, as the logs retain the original Shop Code. All logs remain preserved in the database. info Note: When transferring an entire Shop Code into an existing shop, if all items successfully transfer without conflict then the previous Shop Code will be deleted (Only if there are zero items left). note If a new Shop Code is created then you will likely need to toggle on the new Shop Code by navigating to Settings > Sites and Shops.
To exit the Shop Code Transfer screen, select the Close button. Once the Close button is selected you will be taken back to the Main Screen of TCMax®.
documents.s: Exiting the Shop Code Transfer Screen

documents.t: To transfer items for Deployment, refer to the Deployment tab once entering the Temporarily Item Transfer/Deploy window. In Step 1 you will either add a new Deployment or select an already existing Deployment. To create a new Deployment, click in the textbox and type in the name you want to give this Deployment and then click the Add button. You should now see this Deployment appear in the drop-down box. You can also remove a Deployment you no longer using by selecting the Deployment from the drop down and selecting the Remove button. Once you have the Deployment selected, Step 2 requires you to select the Shop Code that the item(s) you want to deploy belong to. In Step 3 you will scan (or type) the Barcode Ids of the item(s) you are taking on the Deployment. You can also remove a Barcode that you do not need to take on Deployment or that may have been added by mistake by scanning (or typing) the Barcode Id(s). After each Item is scanned/entered you will hear the “Transferred” audio play and the item will be displayed in the grid to the right. If you are sending an entire kit out, you can deploy the kit and all children at one time by scanning (or typing) the Barcode Id of the parent that is being deployed. This will transfer the parent and all children will one scan. In Step 3 you also have the option to Add Items From Item Search. When selecting this option, the Item Search Screen will appear where you can add multiple items to the Deployed location at one time. To deploy items from Item Search, double click on the item(s) you would like to add or highlight the item and click Add Selected Rows. The item will then appear in the Selected Items box in the lower right-hand corner. From the Item Search screen, you can also utilize the search options to narrow down what is showing in the Item Search grid. When/if the grid is narrowed down you can click Add All Rows to add all rows currently showing in the Item Search grid. Once you are satisfied with what is being deployed, click Select and the items will appear in the Deployment screen. You can right-click on the Deployment list when finished and select Send to Excel or Send to 1297 for an accurate list of what has been deployed. info Each item can only exist in one deployment location. If you attempt to send an item on Deployment that is currently part of a different Deployment, you will receive a popup stating the item cannot be added to the deployment due to it belonging to a different one. info Items cannot exist on deployment and temporary transferred lists. If any item or children (components) of a kit are part of a temporarily transferred location, when attempting to add the item to the deployed location, you will receive a popup stating it is currently temporarily transferred somewhere. You will be presented with the option to move that temporarily transferred item off the temporary transferred list and add it to the deployment list by clicking Yes, or leaving the item at the temporarily transferred location it is residing in by clicking No.
With the .sedf file on your deployed computer, you are ready to establish connection to your deployed Database. Follow the outline from Deployment Connection Options.
With the .xedf file on your deployed computer, you are ready to establish connection to your deployed Database. Follow the outline from Deployment Data Manager.

info If you are utilizing Version 9.8.8992.16156 or newer of TCMax®, we have implemented a new Deployment feature that now exports your Deployment file as an .xdef file versus an .sedf file. You'll notice the Import/Export section will look slightly different and now has 2 Export Options, one for exporting the Deployment with the .xdef file or one for exporting the Deployment the "legacy" way with the .sedf file. The capability of switching to legacy mode was removed in TCMax® Version 9.9.0 and newer. Therefore, users will only have 1 Export Option, which is the.xdef file, in Version 9.9.0 and newer

info If you are utilizing Version 9.8.8922.28031 or older of TCMax®, the Import/Export section will only contain one Export option. This generates the .sedf file. Users can switch to legacy mode, if needed, in versions prior to TCMax® Version 9.9.0. This capability was removed in TCMax® Version 9.9.0 and newer. danger There are compatibility constraints when deploying a Database, therefore it is essential when using the legacy deployment system that your home station and deployment systems are utilizing the same Microsoft SQL Server® / Microsoft SQL Server® LocalDB versions as well as TCMax® product versions. Once all necessary items have been added to the Deployment List, refer to the Import / Export section. From the Import / Export section, select the Export For Deployment button. note The logged in user must have the Access Import/Export permission in order to use this feature. This will display the Deployment Export screen. From the Destination Database section, select the Set Destination button. Select a Location where you want this Deployment to be saved to, enter a File name, then press Save. From the Deployment Selection section, select the Deployment that you want to export. To select a Deployment, click the Deployment Selection drop down and a list of your Deployment will appear. From the Options section, you will have the Option to check or uncheck the box for Only copy users from site. If you are on a Database with more than one site, this will only bring users from that specific site to the Deployment Database. By leaving this unchecked all users from the Database will be added to the Deployment. When you have the destination set, Deployment selected, and the option checked or unchecked, you can click the Export button to create the Deployment Database. You will see the Deployment Export Status as the progress is made to export the Deployment. When the export is finished, the following message will appear: Click the OK button to return to the Deployment Export screen. Once the .sedf file is created, move that file to the computer that will be used on Deployment. note We do limit what information is exported to a Deployment Database.

info If you are utilizing Version 9.8.8992.16156 or newer of TCMax®, the Import/Export section will appear with two Export options. The new Export method, which generates an .xedf file, is located from the Export For Deployment button. The other/legacy Export method, which generates an .sedf file, is located from the Legacy Export For Deployment button. If you are using TCMax® Version 9.9.0 or newer, you will only see the new Export method. The capability to switch to legacy mode was removed in TCMax® Version 9.9.0 and newer. If you are using 9.8.8922.28031 or older on either machine (Deployment or Home Station), you will need to revert to the legacy mode, which is referenced in (Legacy) Exporting for Deployment. Once all necessary items have been added to the Deployment List, refer to the Import / Export section. From the Import / Export section, select the Export For Deployment button. note The logged in user must have the Access Import/Export permission in order to use this feature. This will display the Deployment Export screen. From the Deployment Selection section, select the Deployment you would like to export. To select a Deployment, click the Deployment Selection drop down and a list of your Deployment will appear. From the Options section, you will have the Option to check or uncheck the box for Only copy users from site. If you are on a Database with more than one site, this will only bring users from that specific site to the Deployment Database. By leaving this unchecked all users from the Database will be added to the Deployment. When you have the Deployment selected and the option checked or unchecked, you can click the Export button. You will be prompted to Save the export file (.xedf). Select a Location where you want this Deployment to be saved to, enter a File name (by default, a name will be provided that matches the Deployment you are exporting, this can be changed, if desired) then press Save. The Deployment will Export and you will see the Export Status as the progress is made to export the Deployment. Once the .xdef file is created, move that file to the computer that will be used on Deployment. note We do limit what information is exported to a Deployment Database.

Creating a Deployment in TCMax® will allow you to take the users and some of your assets from home-station and populate an offline (deployed) Database. The general idea will be to connect to that Deployment Database while you’re deployed and then when you come back, return your Deployment Data back to the home-station Database.

info If you are utilizing Version 9.8.8992.16156 or newer of TCMax®, we have implemented a new Deployment feature that now returns your Deployment file with an .xdif file versus an .sidf file. You'll notice the Import/Export section will look slightly different and now has 2 Return Options, one for returning the Deployment with the .xdif file or one for returning the Deployment the "legacy" way with the .sidf file. If you are utilizing Version 9.9.0 or newer of TCMax®, you will no longer see the option to return the Deployment using the "legacy" way with the .sidf file. This capability was removed in TCMax® Version 9.9.0 and newer. You'll notice you only have the new option to use the .xdif file.

info If you are utilizing Version 9.8.8922.28031 or older of TCMax®, the Import/Export section will only contain one Return option. This accepts the .sidf file during return. If you are utilizing Version 9.9.0 or newer of TCMax®, the Import/Export section will only contain one Return option. This accepts the .xdif file during return, not the "legacy" .sidf file. danger There are compatibility constraints when deploying a Database, therefore it is essential when using the legacy deployment system that your home station and deployment systems are utilizing the same Microsoft SQL Server® / Microsoft SQL Server® LocalDB versions as well as TCMax® product versions. Follow the outline on how to prepare a Deployment for return from the Deployment Connection Options. Once you have your sidf file and you are back at home station, you are ready to return your items. To import the Data generated on Deployment navigate to Tools > Temporary Item Transfer / Deploy or press Ctrl+T on the keyboard then select the Deployment tab. From the Import/Export section, click the Return From Deployment button and the Deployment Import screen will appear. Refer to the Source Database section and click the Set Source button. A window will appear where you can navigate to the location of the Database you want to import. You can import from a .sidf file created from TCMax® or from a .bak backup file created either through TCMax® or Microsoft SQL Server® Management Studio. Once the Deployment Database file has been selected, click the Open button. Once the file has been selected, refer to the Deployment Selection section, select the Deployment you would like to return. tip You can only return one Deployment at a time. However, if your .sidf or .bak file contains more than one Deployment that was merged, you can return both Deployments using the same file, just do them one at a time. Before pressing Import, refer to the Options section. There are two option checkboxes that will need to be checked/unchecked depending on the desired outcome of the import: Update Destination with Deployment Data: This option will update all home station items that correspond to their deployed counterparts and ensure the information that has been updated such as inspections, and issue/turn in history will be brought back home. Return items from the selected Deployment: This option will automatically return all items from their deployed state upon importing the Deployment Database. If this option is left unchecked, then you will have to manually scan each item to return them otherwise they will remain 'hidden'. Once ready, click the Import button on the Deployment Import screen. You will see a progress bar as the Database is unpacked. Upon completion you will be notified of its success.
documents.s: (Legacy) Returning from Deployment at Home Station

documents.t: info If you are utilizing Version 9.8.8992.16156 or newer of TCMax®, the Import/Export section will appear with two Return options. If you are utilizing Version 9.9.0 or newer of TCMax®, the Import/Export section will appear with only one Return option. The "legacy" Return option has been removed. The new Return method, .xdif file return, is located from the Return From Deployment button. The other/legacy Return method, .sedf file return, is located from the Legacy Return From Deployment button. If you are using 9.8.8922.28031 or older on either machine (Deployment or Home Station), you will need to revert to the legacy mode, which is referenced in (Legacy) Returning from Deployment. Follow the outline on how to prepare a Deployment for return from the Deployment Data Manager. Once you have your .xdif file and you are back at home station, you are ready to return your items. To import the Data generated on Deployment navigate to Tools > Temporary Item Transfer / Deploy or press Ctrl+T on the keyboard then select the Deployment tab. From the Import/Export section, click the Return From Deployment button and the Deployment Import screen will appear. Before pressing Import, refer to the Options section. There are two option checkboxes that will need to be checked/unchecked depending on the desired outcome of the import: Import Log Records: This option will import corresponding Deployment log records. If this option is left unchecked, no logs from Deployment will be returned in the Database. Return items from the selected Deployment: This option will automatically return all items from their deployed state upon importing the Deployment Database. If this option is left unchecked, then you will have to manually scan each item to return them otherwise they will remain 'hidden'. note You can only return one Deployment at a time. Once ready, click the Import button on the Deployment Import screen. A window will appear where you can navigate to the location of the Deployment you want to import. You can import from a .xdif file created from TCMax®. Once the Deployment Database file has been selected, click the Open button. The Deployment will Import and you will see the Import Status as the progress is made to return the Deployment. Once the .xdif file is returned successfully, you will be taken back to the Deployment Import screen. You can now Close this screen along with the Temporary Item Transfer / Deploy screen.
documents.s: Returning from Deployment at Home Station

documents.t: Most information from the Deployed Database does carry back to the Home Database, if changed on Deployment. TCMax® has the following exceptions for logical reasons: Storage Location: The storage location of a deployed item will not overwrite its original home-station location when returned. Items typically return to their original storage spot. Parent/Child Associations: To maintain data integrity, parent/child associations may be dropped if only the child item returns from Deployment. New Items: New items created during Deployment will be added to the home Database only if the new item prompt option (when adding new items prompt for a deployment to assign the item to) is enabled on the Deployment Connection Options / Deployment Data Manager screen. New Users: Additional users created on Deployment will not be merged into home-station. Deleted users will also not be overwritten—and removed on home-station. User Permissions: Elevated permissions granted during Deployment do not overwrite existing home-station permissions upon return. Event Log Records: Only relevant Event Log records—those related to the home station or its items—are imported back from Deployment. Unrelated records are excluded. Shift Assignments: Any modified shift assignments or shifts will not overwrite existing home-station assignments. Inventory Sessions: Any incomplete inventory sessions will not carry over to home-station. Catalog: Catalog information will not be returned to home-station. Maintenance History: Any maintenance history on an item will not be returned to home-station. Vendors: Modified Vendor information will not overwrite home-station. warning If you are utilizing Version 9.8.8922.28031 or older of TCMax®, there are compatibility constraints when deploying a Database, therefore it is essential when using the legacy deployment system that your home station and deployment systems are utilizing the same Microsoft SQL Server® / Microsoft SQL Server® LocalDB versions as well as TCMax® product versions.
documents.s: What Information Comes Back to the Home Station?

documents.t: To access the Temporary Item Transfer / Deploy screen, select Tools > Temporary Item Transfer/Deploy or press Ctrl + T.

Temporary Item Transfer can be utilized to hide the items that are currently out of the Shop for Maintenance or Calibration. To temporarily transfer the items, refer to the Temporary Transfer tab once entering the Temporarily Item Transfer/Deploy window. Temporary Item Transfer allows a user to send an item out for calibration (or to another location) without breaking a parent/child relationship. It also allows a user to hide that item in the tool room so it cannot accidentally be issued or modified while it is not currently on the shelf.

In Step 1 you will need to select the destination. If an item is going out for calibration, you can select the default Cal Lab location, or you can create a new location by typing the new location name into the input box and clicking the Add button. You can also remove a location you no longer using by selecting the location from the drop down and selecting the Remove button. Once you have the destination selected, Step 2 requires you to select the Shop Code that the item(s) you want to transfer belong to. In Step 3 you will scan (or type) the Barcode Ids of the item(s) that need to be transferred. After each Item is scanned/entered you will hear the “Transferred” audio play and the item will be displayed in the grid to the right. If you are sending an entire kit out, you can transfer the kit and all children at one time by scanning (or typing) the Barcode Id of the parent that is being sent out. This will transfer the parent and all children will one scan. In Step 3 you also have the option to Add Items From Item Search. When selecting this option, the Item Search Screen will appear where you can add multiple items to the transferred location at one time. To transfer items from Item Search, double click on the item(s) you would like to add or highlight the item and click Add Selected Rows. The item will then appear in the Selected Items box in the lower right-hand corner. From the Item Search screen, you can also utilize the search options to narrow down what is showing in the Item Search grid. When/if the grid is narrowed down you can click Add All Rows to add all rows currently showing in the Item Search grid. Once you are satisfied with what is being Temporarily Transferred, click Select and the items will appear in the Temporary Transfer screen. You can right-click on the Temporary Transferred list when finished and select Send to Excel or Send to 1297 for an accurate list of what has been transferred. info Each item can only exist in one temporarily transferred location. If any item or children (components) of a kit are part of another temporarily transferred location, when attempting to transfer to the current location, you will receive a popup stating it is currently temporarily transferred somewhere else. You will be presented with the option to then move the Item to the location you have selected by clicking Yes or leaving the item at the location it is residing in by clicking No. info Items cannot exist both on temporary transferred and deployed lists. If you attempt to send an item to a Temporarily Transferred location and that item is currently at a Deployed location you will receive a popup stating the item cannot be transferred due to it being deployed.
documents.s: Sending Items to a Temporary Transferred Location

documents.t: This same screen will be utilized to remove items from the Temporary transfer list when they return. The same steps would be performed by selecting the destination the item is currently at, the Shop Code where it belongs, then scan/type the Barcode Id. You will hear the “Transferred” audio prompt and the item will disappear from the grid. If you are returning an entire kit that was sent out, you can scan or type in the Parent Barcode Id and TCMax® will display a prompt to give the option if you would like to return the children / grandchildren along with the parent, all in a single scan. By clicking Yes the parent and all children / grandchildren will be returned at once. By clicking No, only the Parent Barcode Id that was scanned or typed in will be returned. If you are returning an item from the Cal Lab location, you will be prompted to enter a new calibration due date for the item. Use the date picker to select the new calibration due date and click Accept. If you do not want to update the calibration due date for the item, you can click the Cancel button. Temporarily transferred items are hidden from other TCMax® screens and reports by default, but you can change this setting to fit your specific environment. To do this go to Settings > Options, under the Display Options section, uncheck the box Exclude temporarily transferred items on screens.
documents.s: Returning Items from a Temporary Transferred Location

documents.t: Vendor Setup can be used to create vendors to further track information on an item such as where the item was supplied from. From the Main Screen of TCMax®, navigate to the menu bar at the top of the screen and select Tools > Vendor Setup. Once Vendor Setup is selected, a separate Vendor setup screen will be displayed where you can Add, Edit, or Delete vendors.

From the Vendor Setup screen, select the New Vendor button. You will now be able to enter information for your vendor. note Vendor Name is required, all other fields are optional. After entering the information for the new vendor, click the Save button to add that vendor to the TCMax® Database. tip If you accidentally click on New Vendor but do not wish to add a vendor, select the Cancel button to go back into the Vendor Setup screen or select the Close button to return to the Main Screen of TCMax®.
From the Vendor Setup screen, select the Vendor you wish to edit then press the Edit button. After editing the vendor information, click the Save button to update the changes.
From the Vendor Setup screen, select the Vendor you wish to delete then select the Delete Vendor button. danger Deleting vendors is a permanent action. All changes are final.

Once a vendor is created, they can be assigned to items for further tracking. Assigning a vendor is done through the Quantity and Status tab from the Main Screen of TCMax® when editing an item or from the Catalog Setup feature.

Within the Reports screen, select Report Options > US Air Force to navigate to the available Report Options for the U.S. Air Force Reports.

The Set Report Versions menu option allows you to change the report version footers as updates are made to the Air Force forms. note We are not notified of changes that are made to the Air Force forms when they are rolled out to Users. If footers need updated, please feel free to reach out to our Soaring Software Solutions, Inc. Support Department and we would be happy to make necessary changes when a new Version 9 build is released.
The Set 1297 Captions menu option allows you to set certain captions that will display on the 1297 Report.

The Set 2005 Captions menu option allows you to make appropriate entries for report captions that will display on the 2005 Report and the 1348-6 Report. This screen can also be accessed from the Main Screen of TCMax® by pressing Alt + 5 or Alt + 6.
The Set AF55 PPE menu option allows you to set what checkboxes will be checked in sections I and II of the AF55 Report.

The Set AF55 Display Details menu option allows you to set what courses in a particular shop you would like to run the AF55 Report for. info One course must be selected to be able to run the AF55 Report for that specific shop.

The Set MIL Captions menu option allows you to set the organization caption and the captions for the signature lines that appear on the MIL Report. From the MIL Captions screen, you have the capability of adding a third signature line if desired.
The Set MIL Options menu allows you to set which version of the MIL Report you wish to run along with what information you would like displayed on the MIL Report.
This report is a Top Secret Register Page used to originate or receive Top Secret/SAR information to establish accountability.
This report is used to organize the inventoried item records from within the armory during multiple shifts.
This report can be utilized for reordering items based on your selected criteria.
The form is used to formally document the transfer, receipt, or destruction of material.
This report will display the courses that are currently assigned to a User.
This report will display the most recent 55 courses that have been completed by a User.
This report will display the inspection update records that have taken place on an item.
This report displays the records of issue, turn-in, and inventory of items marked as a Facility Key or with the custom checkboxes.
This report displays the issue and turn-in times for items with a new page for each parent on an ACC 140 branded form.
This report displays the issue and turn-in times for items with a new page for each parent on an AFRC 177 branded form.
This report displays the inspection history on an item.
This report displays the history of updated inspections for items that have the T.O. checkbox checked.
This report displays the historical lost records for the item that you specify. The report will generate a new page for each lost instance that is found.

This report displays the issued items that are marked as "No Turn-In", type of "Hazmat". By default, all No Turn-In Hazmat Items will appear on the Report unless the Report is filtered down by Issued Location, which can be specified in the EU# field (block 6).
This report displays everything that has the ‘No Turn In’ box checked.
This report displays all items that have the 'T. O.' check box checked.
This report displays all items that have a negative status applied to them. This report can be limited to a specific parent if desired.
This report is a Top Secret cover sheet.
This report is a Top Secret cover sheet.

This report generates the MIL for items not in a kit (no Parent Barcode Id) based on the specified options that were configured fromReport Options > U.S. Air Force > Set MIL Options. The captions that are generated on this Report are based on the specified captions that were configured from Report Options > U.S. Air Force > Set MIL Captions.
documents.s: MIL for items not in a kit

documents.t: This report generates the MIL for items that are in a kit (with a Parent Barcode Id) based on the specified options that were configured fromReport Options > U.S. Air Force > Set MIL Options. The captions that are generated on this Report are based on the specified captions that were configured from Report Options > U.S. Air Force > Set MIL Captions.

The AF 1297 Temporary Issue Receipt can be generated for a User in several ways, depending on how you have your Options set in TCMax®. The AF 1297 can generate automatically at the end of the issue/ turn-in process if the option to do so is checked or it can be ran by hitting Ctrl + 4 on your keyboard.

The AF 1348-6 DOD Single Line Item Requisition System Document can be generated by bringing an item up for display on the Main Screen TCMax® and hitting Ctrl + 6. The AF 1348-6 can also be printed from the Item Search and Show Issued Items screen.
Within the Reports screen, select Report Options > US Army to navigate to the available Report Options for the U.S. Army Reports.

The Set Report Versions menu option allows you to set the U.S. Army Report versions and also reset back to default values. From the Army Report Versions screen, you will have the capability of modifying the following U.S. Army Report Versions, CCAD Form 5220-E, DA From 2062, DA From 3161, DA Form 5519-R.
The Set 2062 Options menu allows you to set how the information will appear on the 2062 Report.
The Set Commander Information menu option allows you to set the Commander Information that will be displayed on the 2062 Report.
This report provides a listing of Items in the selected shop.
This report displays the historical lost records for the item that you specify. The report will generate a new page for each lost instance.
This report displays the issue history with a new page for each employee on a Change Document form.
This report displays the turn-in history with a new page for each employee on a Change Document form.
This report shows issue and turn-in history on a DA Form 5519-R.
This report shows issued items that are currently marked as broken on a DA Form 3161.
This report is used as a hand receipt to show items that are issued (or not) and can be filtered by the user that they are issued to.
documents.s: Hand Receipt DA Form 2062 with 2062 Settings

documents.t: This report is a simplified version of the 2062 that shows only items issued to users.
This report shows the issue, turn-in, and consumed records for your consumable items.
Within the Reports screen, select Report Options > US Navy / Marines to navigate to the available Report Option for the U.S. Navy and Marines Reports.
The Set Squadron Information menu option allows you to set Squadron Information for various Navy and Marines Reports.

Version 9.9.2 and older of TCMax®​ The Inventory report displays the monthly inventory statuses of all items within the specified year. Version 9.10.0 and newer of TCMax®​ The Inventory report displays the monthly inventory statuses of all items within the selected kit(s) and specified year based on the most recent completed full Physical Inventory for each month, including item status details, item notes, inventory review information, and applicable Reviewed By details when enabled (Settings > Inventory Options). note In order to populate the Reviewed By User within the report, the Physical Inventory must be against All generations.
This report shows the issue/turn-in records for a selected shop within the selected date range.
This report shows the sum of weight used and disposed for items. For this report to be utilized the Aerospace Coating Item Type will need to be selected.
This report is the NAVSUP Form 306 Controlled-Equipage Custody Record (4442).
This report shows the sums of weight used and disposed for items that have the Hazmat Item Type selected.
This report displays the Broken/Worn Tool Report (BTR) for the specified tool as outlined in COMNAVAIRFORINST 4790.2E. This requires the tool to have the 'Broken' status.
This report shows the issued assets from the selected shop code with the NAVAIR required data.
This report displays the Missing Tool Report (MTR) for the specified tool as outlined in COMNAVAIRFORINST 4790.2E. This requires the tool to have the 'Lost' status.
This report shows the movement of items from the selected shop code. You can filter this report by a specific Work Location, limit it to just Broken items, or run it for a selected date range.

Introduction to Guides of the TCMax® Asset Management suite. TCMax® has numerous built-in options. In the next pages, you will find guides and walkthroughs of some features available within the TCMax® Asset Management suite. note If you do not find a guide or walkthrough of a feature that you are looking for, our support staff is available by phone or email to assist.
This video provides a guide of the advanced features that have been implemented into TCMax®.
This video walks through the basic Issue / Turn-in functions of TCMax® using the default Demo Data.

info Attachments can be added to assets or users. Below demonstrates how to add an attachment to any item. Press ‘Esc’ key to clear the Main Screen if anything is displayed. Type ‘118’ in the Main Input box then press the ‘Enter’ key, TCMax® displays the item ‘7/16 Deep Socket’. Navigate to the ‘Attachments’ tab (located below the Item Serial Number). Press ‘Add Attachment to Barcode’. Navigate to any appropriate Attachment, then press ‘Open’. ➤ This will add an Attachment to this specific Barcode Id. On the ‘Attachments’ tab, select ‘Add Attachment to Part Number’. Navigate to the appropriate Attachment, then press ‘Open’. ➤ This will add an Attachment to this specific Part Number. ➤ If another item has the same Part Number, then the Attachment will cascade to that Item. Press ‘Esc’ key to clear the Main Screen. Type ‘118’ in the Main Input box then press the ‘Enter’ key, TCMax® displays item ‘7/16 Deep Socket’. Navigate to the ‘Attachments’ tab (located below the Item Serial Number). Verify the Attachments saved to the ‘Barcode Id’ section and the ‘Part Number’ section. ➤ By double clicking on the specific Attachment, it will open the file.

info There are numerous ways to add items within TCMax®. The easiest ways to add items within TCMax® are to simply enter or scan the Barcode Id directly from the Main Screen. Type ‘100’ in the Main Input box then press the ‘Enter’ key, TCMax® says “New Item”. ➤ If you are adding Items to the ‘TCMax® Demo Shop’ for the first time, the following message will appear, press ‘OK’ through the message. Enter the item information you wish to have for this item. Press the ‘F5’ key to save the item or press ‘Save’. Press ‘Esc’ key to clear the Main Screen.

info Adding a new User can easily be done directly from the Main Screen of TCMax® within seconds by simply scanning or entering the User Id in the Input Box. Type ‘33’ in the Main Input box press the ‘Enter’ key, TCMax® says New User. Type a ‘Name’ in the Username box then press ‘Save’. ➤ Your User is now created, and you can issue items to that User. Press ‘Esc’ to clear the Main Screen. Type ‘33’ in the Main Input box then press the ‘Enter’ key, TCMax® says “User”. Type ‘Building 900’ in the Location box then press the ‘Enter’ key, TCMax® says “Location”. Type ‘117’ in the Main Input box then press the ‘Enter’ key, TCMax® says “Issue”. Press ‘Esc’ key to clear the Main Screen.

info Items with overdue calibration can be issued to users with the Allow Override Constraint permission. Type ‘06’ in the Main Input box then press the ‘Enter’ key, TCMax® says “User”. Type ‘Building 72’ in the Location box then press the ‘Enter’ key, TCMax® says “Location”. Type ‘114’ in the Main Input box then press the ‘Enter’ key, TCMax® says “Overdue Calibration” and the message reads “Item Not Issued”. [Demonstrate the ability to change a calibration due date easily] Press the ‘Esc’ key to clear the Main Screen. Type ‘114’ in the Main Input box then press the ‘Enter’ key, the overdue Torque Wrench is displayed. Click in the Calibration Due Date box. Press ‘T’ for today. Press ‘Y’ to add years. Press ‘M’ to add months. Press ‘+ OR -’ to add or subtract days. Press the ‘Enter’ key to save the updated calibration date. ➤ After the Calibration Due Date has been updated, you will be able issue the item as long as it is no longer Overdue. Press ‘Esc’ key to clear the Main Screen.

info Below you will find an example of a User trying to issue an item they are NOT certified to take, along with an example of certifying the User for that item and completing the issue process. Type ‘02’ in the Main Input box then press the ‘Enter’ key, TCMax® says “User”. Type ‘Building 1200’ in the Location box then press the ‘Enter’ key, TCMax® says “Location”. Type ‘704’ in the Main Input box then press the ‘Enter’ key, TCMax® says "User Not Certified". ➤ This item will not be issued because the User is not certified to take this item. Adjust your Mode from ‘Mode = Issue/Turn-In’ to ‘Mode = Training Completion’. Type ‘02’ in the Main Input box then press the ‘Enter’ key, TCMax® says “User”. Type ‘7004’ in the Main Input box then press the ‘Enter’ key, TCMax® says "Completed". ➤ The User will now be certified to take the Wire Welder with the Barcode ID, 704. Adjust your Mode from ‘Mode = Training Completion’ to ‘Mode = Issue/Turn-In’. Type ‘02’ in the Main Input box then press the ‘Enter’ key, TCMax® says “User”. Type ‘Building 1200’ in the Location box then press the ‘Enter’ key, TCMax® says “Location”. Type ‘704’ in the Main Input box then press the ‘Enter’ key, TCMax® says "Issued". ➤ You will now see that the User is certified to issue the item. ➤ Certifications can also be assigned from the Main Screen from the Certified User tab. The example provided above is an example of how our Course Feature is used to certify a User. ➤ An unlimited number of Certifications can be added to a User, granting permissions to an unlimited number of Part Numbers with a single barcode scan.

info The TCMax® Dashboard was designed to help a supervisor, manager, etc. quickly and visually monitor the status of many of their items, users, and courses all from a single display. The blue line running along the right-hand side of the Main Screen is used to open the Dashboard. ➤ ‘Left click’ on the blue line to fully open the Dashboard. ‘Right click’ on the blue line to partially open the Dashboard. ‘Left click’ on the blue line to fully open the Dashboard. With the Dashboard opened, you will see different Categories in blue. With the Categories expanded, you will see your Subcategories. Select the ‘Overdue Item Calibrations’ Subcategory under the ‘Calibration Status’ Category, you will notice a table with the information for that Subcategory will appear. You can send this table to Excel if it is something you need to save or share. To close the table, simply press ‘Close’ or press ‘X’ in the upper right-hand corner. This will take you back to the Dashboard. ➤ Within the TCMax® Dashboard, different Categories can be moved around. Press and hold the ‘Kit Status’ Category. ‘Drag’ this to the top left, above the ‘Current Issue Status’ Category. You will notice the Kit Status was rearranged to appear as the very first Status. ‘Right’ click on the blue line now running along the left-hand side of the screen. This will show you the Dashboard in a mini pane along with the Main Screen. ➤ The mini pane will only show the left column of the Dashboard. ➤ This is useful if you need to move status headers to the left side and keep them open in a mini pane to monitor, while completing actions on the Main Screen within TCMax®. ‘Right’ click on the blue line again to close the Dashboard.

info The Database Maintenance screen is used to create Backups of your Database (if connected locally), Change Database Connections, restore to TCMax® Demo Data, Migrate Special Options used in TCMax® Version 8, Delete Logs and Rebuild Indexes, Delete Sites and Shop Codes, activate Asset History Tracking, and enable Auto Load Presets per Shop Code. From the Top Toolbar, select ‘File’ then select ‘Database Maintenance’ . TCMax® says “Enter User Id”. Type ‘01’ in the User Id box then press the ‘Enter’ key, TCMax® says “Enter Password”. Type ‘01’ in the User Password box then press the ‘Enter’ key. ➤ If connected locally, you will notice 9 (nine) different tabs starting with Backup Database. If connected through a Microsoft SQL Server® then you will notice 8 (eight) different tabs starting with Change Database Connections. To close Database Maintenance press ‘Close’.

info There are four different inventory modes to help you record your sessions and conditions of your assets. The following demonstrates the Physical (Kit) Inventory mode. From the Top Toolbar, select ‘Tools’ then select ‘Inventory’ or press ‘Ctrl+Shift+I’ on your keyboard from the Main Screen to enter the Inventory Selection screen. Select ‘Physical Inventory’. From Step 1, select ‘Full’ for the type of Inventory being performed. From Step 2, select ‘Children’ for the generation level. From Step 3, verify ‘TCMax® Demo Shop’ is selected. From Step 4, type ‘121’ and press the ‘Enter’ key. With your focus in the Inventory screen, type ‘521’ then press the ‘Enter’ key, TCMax® says “Inventoried”. ➤ The inventory screen does not have an input box, but as long as your cursor is focused within the screen then you will be able to enter the appropriate Barcode Id of the item you wish to inventory. Type ‘522’ then press the ‘Enter’ key, TCMax® says “Inventoried”. Type ‘523’ then press the ‘Enter’ key, TCMax® says “Inventoried”. Type ‘524’ then press the ‘Enter’ key, TCMax® says “Enter Quantity”. Notice that TCMax® shows you that there are “20” Steel Carbiners that should be in the Pumper Truck by displaying a “20” on the screen. If any are missing from your actual count then you would want to adjust the Inventoried Quantity to show what is physically there. Adjust this quantity to '19' and press the 'Enter' key, TCMax® says “Discrepancy”. ➤ You will notice that the Item will appear under the Discrepancy List and display a Discrepancy Type of 'Quantity Did Not Match'. Type ‘16’ under Inventoried Quantity then press the ‘Enter’ key, TCMax® will display a 'No Item Found' popup. This is showing the item does not exist. Press 'OK' on the popup. Type ‘525’ then press the ‘Enter’ key, TCMax® says “Inventoried”. Type ‘526’ then press the ‘Enter’ key, TCMax® says “Inventoried”. Type ‘527’ then press the ‘Enter’ key, TCMax® says “Inventoried”. Type ‘121’ then press the ‘Enter’ key, TCMax® says “Inventoried”. Pretend you find one more item (that does not belong in the Pumper Truck, 121). Type ‘007’ then press the ‘Enter’ key, TCMax® says “Discrepancy”. ➤ You will notice that the Item that was entered will appear from the Discrepancy List and display a Discrepancy Type of ‘Does Not Belong To This Inventory’. From the Discrepancy List, click on the ‘Information Tool Tip’ directly next to the 1/4 Deep Socket 3/8 Item Name. ➤ This will show information about the item including what Kit this item belongs to. Select the Discrepancy for the 1/4 Deep Socket 3/8 then select ‘Resolve’. ➤ After selecting resolve TCMax® will provide a ‘Resolve Discrepancy’ screen where you can enter the action that was taken to resolve the discrepancy, if you cancel out of this screen then it will be listed as a discrepancy for the Inventory of Item 121. Enter the action that was taken to resolve the discrepancy then select ‘Accept’. Select ‘Complete Inventory’ at the bottom of the screen. The Physical Inventory will now be completed, press ‘Close’ to exit the ‘Physical Inventory Setup’ screen and ‘Inventory Selection’ screen.

info Items with the ‘No Turn-In’ box checked are considered Expendable Items. When checking this box, it automatically checks the ‘Multiple items with this same barcode number’ box. Items with the ‘Issue multiple of this item with single scan’ box checked causes TCMax® to ask how many of these items you wish to take. Type ‘02’ in the Main Input box then press the ‘Enter’ key, TCMax® says “User”. Type ‘Building 99’ in the Location box then press the ‘Enter’ key, TCMax® says “Location”. Type ‘702’ in the Main Input box then press the ‘Enter’ key, TCMax® says “Enter Quantity”. Type ‘6’ in the Multi-Item Issue box then press the ‘Enter’ key, TCMax® says “Issue” and the ‘Quantity On Hand’ and ‘Quantity Available’ on the Main Screen decreases by two. If your ‘Quantity On Hand’ of this item goes below the “Reorder Qty” then TCMax® will announce “Attention” to tell you that you need to reorder this item. ➤ Your Expendable Items issued will only appear under the Users Expendables tab when a User is displayed on the Main Screen of TCMax®. Press ‘Esc’ key to clear the Main Screen.

info If a Work Location won't be used in your environment, this prompt can be turned off within Options. Type ‘02’ in the Main Input box then press the ‘Enter’ key, TCMax® says “User”. Type ‘Building 127’ in the Location box then press the ‘Enter’ key, TCMax® says “Location”. Type ‘003’ in the Main Input box then press the ‘Enter’ key, TCMax® says “Issue”. Type ‘005’ in the Main Input box then press the ‘Enter’ key, TCMax® says “Issue”. Type ‘006’ in the Main Input box then press the ‘Enter’ key, TCMax® says “Issue”. Type ‘605’ in the Main Input box then press the ‘Enter’ key, TCMax® says “Overdue Calibration” but does not say Issue. Press ‘Esc’ key to clear the Main Screen.

info Items without the ‘No Turn-In’ box checked are considered Non-Expendable Items. These are items that are expected to be returned. Type ‘02’ in the Main Input box then press the ‘Enter’ key, TCMax® says “User”. Type ‘Building 56’ in the Location box then press the ‘Enter’ key, TCMax® says “Location”. Type ‘116’ in the Main Input box then press the ‘Enter’ key, TCMax® says “Issue”. ➤ The ‘Quantity On Hand’ remains the same since this item will eventually be returned. The ‘Quantity Available’ on the Main Screen decreases by one. ➤ Non-expendable items are not just single quantity items, they can also have multiple of an item with the same barcode number depending on the way they are setup in TCMax®. Press ‘Esc’ key to clear the Main Screen.

info Rags are an item that has its own Item Type. This allows for TCMax® to recognize these item types as an item that goes through the laundry process before returning to stock. Type ‘02’ in the Main Input box then press the ‘Enter’ key, TCMax® says “User”. Type ‘Building 78’ in the Location box then press the ‘Enter’ key, TCMax® says “Location”. Type ‘141’ in the Main Input box then press the ‘Enter’ key, TCMax® says “‘Enter’ Quantity”. Type ‘2’ in the Multi-item Issue box then press the ‘Enter’ key, TCMax® says “Issue”. ➤ The ‘Quantity On Hand’ remains the same since this will be returned eventually. The ‘Quantity Available’ on the Main Screen decreases by two. Also, the Rags appear in the list of issued items. Type ‘141’ in the Main Input box then press the ‘Enter’ key (as if you are turning them in), TCMax® says “Enter Quantity”. ➤ You will notice you can issue more out at the bottom, or you can select other options before turning in the Rags. In ‘Step 2: Select the amount to transfer’, ensure ‘2’ is entered. In ‘Step 3: Select Location (Turn-in clean rags)’, Select ‘Mark as Dirty’. TCMax® will say “Transferred” and you will notice the Multi-item box shows “Sent to Dirty Rags”. ➤ If you select close and leave this screen you will notice the User no longer has Rags Issued to them. If you look at Issued Items, by going to the ‘Show Issued Items’ screen from the Top Toolbar or selecting the ‘Issued Items List’ at the bottom right-hand corner of the Main Screen, you will notice the Username is no longer specific to that User it states ‘Dirty Rags’. Press ‘Esc’ to clear the Main Screen if anything is displayed. Type ‘141’ in the Main Input box then press the ‘Enter’ key, TCMax® will say “Make Selection”. Select the column to the left of the Rags to highlight the 2 that are Marked Dirty. ➤ You will notice in Step 2 that a quantity of 2 is auto populated by highlighting the row. In ‘Step 3: Select Location (Turn-in clean rags)’, Select ‘Send to Laundry’, TCMax® will say “Transferred” and you will see ‘Sent to Laundry’ appear in the Multi-Item box. Close the Multi-Item box and navigate to the ‘Issued Items List’ from the bottom right-hand corner of the Main Screen or the ‘Show Issued Items’ screen from the Top Toolbar. Once you have navigated to the ‘Issued Items’ screen, you will see that your Rags are still issued to ‘Dirty Rags’, but the Location has adjusted to ‘Laundry’. With the Main Screen cleared, type in ‘141’ in the Main Input box then press the ‘Enter’ key, TCMax® will say “Make Selection”. Select the column to the left of the Rags to highlight the 2 that are being Returned. ➤ You will notice in Step 2 that a quantity of 2 is auto populated by highlighting the row. In ‘Step 3: Select Location (Turn-in clean rags)’, Select ‘Turn-In and Close’, TCMax® will say “Turn-In”. ➤ The Rags are now turned back into inventory. You will notice your ‘Quantity Available’ has adjusted accordingly. Press ‘Esc’ key to clear the Main Screen.

info Item Search will display your Items based on your Search Options, if you enter criteria into the Search Fields it will narrow down your search. The Search Fields are ‘AND’ not ‘OR’. From the Top Toolbar, select ‘Item Search’. In the ‘Item Name box’, type ‘Wrench’, and press the ‘Enter’ key. Notice TCMax® now shows only items with ‘Wrench’ in the name. Press the ‘Close’ button.

info By default, you're not required to have a user or work location displayed to turn items in. Type ‘003’ in the Main Input box then press the ‘Enter’ key, TCMax® says “Turn In”. Type ‘005’ in the Main Input box then press the ‘Enter’ key, TCMax® says “Turn In”.

info The Kit Builder screen helps you quickly build, modify, and duplicate kits or toolboxes. From the Top Toolbar, select ‘Tools’ then select ‘Kit Builder’ or press ‘Ctrl-K’ on your keyboard from the Main Screen to open the Kit Builder screen. Under Kit Shop Code, select ‘TCMax® Demo Shop’. Under Enter Kit Id, enter ‘600’ then press the ‘Enter’ key or press ‘Load Kit’. ➤ You will see your Kit displayed under the Kit Layout section. Once your Kit is displayed you can adjust Storage Locations, Remove Items, Add or Duplicate Items, and View the Selected Item’s Details. Click ‘Clear Display’. Under ‘Enter’ Kit Id, press ‘Create New Kit’. Under Barcode Id, enter ‘400’. Now you will be able to type in an Item Name, Storage Location, NSN, Part Number, and Serial Number for the Kit. After the information is entered, press ‘Save’. ➤ You will now see your Kit displayed under the Kit Layout section. Once your Kit is displayed you can Add, Move, or Duplicate Items from Inventory, Create New Items, Adjust the Storage Location, and View the Selected Item’s Details. Close the Kit Builder screen by pressing the ‘Close’ button or the ‘X’ in the upper right-hand corner.

The following outline provides guidance on familiarizing yourself with TCMax® and the TCMax® Demo Shop. Each steps input can be scanned or entered depending on if you have a barcode scanner setup or a keyboard setup. Also, be sure to turn on your PC or laptop speakers, after all TCMax® is Software that Talks™. Trial Version If you are using a 90-day trial version of our software, after the 90-day period is up you must have proper License information loaded in order to continue using TCMax®. Start by launching TCMax® by double-clicking on the white TCMax® icon.

info Log Search will display historical records based on your Search Options, if you enter criteria into the Search Fields or Filters it will narrow down your search. From the Top Toolbar, select ‘Tools’ then select ‘Log Search’. In the ‘Barcode Id box’, type ‘100’, and press the ‘Enter’ key. ➤ The grid will be narrowed down to show anything that has ‘100’ within the Barcode Id. Close the Log Search screen by pressing the ‘Close’ button or the ‘X’ in the upper right-hand corner.

info The logged in user will be the 'attendant' or the user who is displayed with each event log during their session. A logged in user by default is required to issue tools to other users. ➤ If you see the Sites and Shop Codes screen upon launching TCMax®, select the TCMax® Demo Shop and select Save. If you are not greeted with a login box navigate to File > Log In/Out (F12). TCMax® will say "Enter User Id", type ‘01’ in the User Id box then press the 'Enter' key, TCMax® will say "Enter Password". Scan or type ‘01’ in the User Password box then press the 'Enter' key, TCMax® says "Logged In". Observe Lederman, Richard A [Demo Admin] Logged In in the upper left hand corner.

info A Maintenance Procedure is a specific task within an organization that requires a certain set of items and equipment to perform. From the Top Toolbar, select ‘Tools’ then select ‘Maintenance Procedure / Bulk Issue Setup’. Ensure the Tire Change List – 807 is selected under ‘Select Maintenance Procedure’. Under ‘Add Item to Maintenance Procedure’, type ‘111’ and press the ‘Enter’ key. Under ‘Add Item to Maintenance Procedure’, type ‘114’ and press the ‘Enter’ key. ➤ Notice we are typing in Barcode Id Numbers, but the Part Numbers are displaying. This is because TCMax® associates Maintenance Procedures with Part Numbers. Therefore assets that are added to a maintenance procedures must have a Part Number. Close the Maintenance Procedures / Bulk Issues Setup screen by pressing the ‘Close’ button or the ‘X’ in the upper right-hand corner. On the Main Screen of TCMax®, type ‘807’ then press the ‘Enter’ key. The Maintenance Procedure will print as long as a receipt printer is assigned and show where the item is located or who has the item issued and where.

info The Options screen will display all of the built-in Options within TCMax®. You can select or deselect Options depending on how you want TCMax® to operate on the Local Machine. From the Top Toolbar, select ‘Settings’ then select ‘Options’. ➤ Notice the 5 (five) different tabs starting with ‘General Options’ at the top of the screen. These tabs are preloaded with over 140+ built in Options. Once adjusting the Options you wish to have selected within TCMax®, press ‘Save’ in the bottom right-hand corner.

info Reports from the Top Toolbar will display built-in Reports within TCMax® and are designed to help you review your data and organize the different historical events. Select ‘Reports’ from the Top Toolbar. ➤ Notice the 6 (six) different tabs starting with ‘Generic’ at the top of the screen. These tabs are preloaded with over 100+ Reports designed for you to use. When you select different Reports you will notice off to the right-hand side, TCMax® will give you a Report description. From the Top Toolbar of the Reports window, select ‘Tools’. Press ‘Set Favorite Reports’. You will notice a blank check box appear to the left of every Report, select the ‘Login/Logout Records’ box along with a couple more of your choice. Press ‘Save Favorites’ (bottom right of the screen flashing blue). You now created a new tab where all your ‘Favorite’ Reports will be stored for you to easily access them without searching every time. Close the Reports window by pressing the ‘Close’ button or the ‘X’ in the upper right-hand corner.

info There are several shortcut keys that can help speed up access to different features within TCMax®. From the Main Screen of TCMax®, press the ‘F1’ key (Help > About > Shortcuts). ➤ The Shortcuts screen will appear, where you can see everything that can be done with a single keystroke from the Main Screen.

info Each user can be assigned independent permissions depending on their role within the software. Below will outline how to set special access permissions for a User. From the Top Toolbar, select ‘Settings’ then select ‘User Options’. Display a User from the User Permissions tab. This can be done by searching for a User Id in the upper left-hand corner of the screen or by searching for a Username in the upper right-hand corner of the screen.. ➤ If you search by a User’s Id in the upper left-hand corner, your Username will be displayed from the upper right-hand corner. Notice the various permissions a User can be assigned. Notice the User Password box. ➤ If you wish to have a User login to TCMax® then the User will need to have a password assigned to them. ➤ Permissions for TCMax® will go based off the logged in User. Press ‘Save’ to save any changes made.

Type ‘03’ in the Main Input box then press the ‘Enter’ key, TCMax® says “User”. Type ‘Building 1200’ in the Location box then press the ‘Enter’ key, TCMax® says “Location”. Type ‘111’ in the Main Input box then press the ‘Enter’ key, TCMax® says “Issue”. ➤ Let’s look to see who has what. Press ‘Ctrl+S’ this brings up the Issued Items grid to the right of the screen. Press ‘Ctrl+S’ to exit Issued Items and returns to Item Details. From the Top Toolbar, select ‘Show Issued Items’ or press ‘Ctrl+I’. The list of items currently issued appears. Notice you can mark any item in this list as Broken, Unserviceable, Lost, or Long Term. Close the Show Issued Items screen.

info A video walkthrough is available for this process here. tip It is recommended that you reach out to TCMax® Support Staff for assistance on migrating your Data To begin migration you will want to have TCMax® Version 9 installed and licensed on your destination computer as well as your Version 8.10 Microsoft® Access Database (if standalone) or access to the Microsoft SQL Server®. note If you are running 8.9 or earlier you must first upgrade to 8.10.590.

Within TCMax® Version 9, navigate to File > Import / Export Records. We can migrate Data from both Microsoft SQL Server® and Microsoft® Access Databases. Therefore, the remainder of this outline is split up into two categories, Migrating your Data from a Microsoft SQL Server® and Migrating your Data from a Microsoft® Access Database.

If your Version 8 Data is in a Microsoft SQL Server® Database, select the SQL Server radio button and then click the Set Source button which will bring up a Connections Properties window. Enter your Server Name, Authentication Method, and Database. Click the Test Connection button and if it says “Test connection succeeded” you can click OK to proceed. If it gives any result other than “Test connection succeeded.” take note of the error indicated and correct the connection information. When finished select OK. Select the Set Destination button and follow the same steps, except in this case you will enter the destination server’s information. When finished select OK.

To verify that your source Database is up to date and all datatypes are correct you will need to select the Verify Source Database button. This step is not optional and must be completed before progressing to step two.

Once your Database has been verified, select the Sync Data button to move the Data into your destination SQL Server Database. During the sync, information will appear on the screen letting you know what step of the syncing process you are on.

You can remove any old Database tables that will no longer be used by TCMax® by clicking the Remove Old Data button. By opting to leave Old Data, you will notice all the Version 8 tables will still remain intact but will essentially be 'archived' Data from the migration point.

Your Data should now be migrated and by re-establishing your TCMax® connection to the destination server you should see all your Data available. note Often times, unless the destination server Database was empty you will need to enable the new Shop Code within Settings > Sites and Shops.

note If migrating a standalone Database (Microsoft® Access), you will need to be on TCMax® version 9.8.7802 or older. This feature is removed due to deprecated Microsoft Software. If you are using a newer version of TCMax®, contact the Soaring Software Solutions support office for assistance. If you are using a Microsoft® Access Database, select the Access radio button then select the Set Source button to bring up a File Explorer window that can be used to navigate to your Microsoft® Access Database. Ensure your Microsoft® Access Database is local to this computer's hard drive and not on a media or networked location. Locate and select your Microsoft® Access Database and press Open. Set your destination Database by selecting Set Destination or by leaving this default, your Data will be migrated into the currently established connection (the Database you are working in). After you have chosen your Microsoft® Access Database and your destination Microsoft® SQL Database proceed to the next step.

This process requires you to have SQL Server Migration Assistant (SSMA) installed on your computer and also requires some form of the Microsoft® Access Database Engine. By selecting the Transfer Access Database button, TCMax® will launch a command line window which will pause early on and prompt you (indicated green) to enter a password for the Microsoft® Access Database. When prompted, enter the Database password and press Enter on the keyboard. The default Database password is Servic1. Once the password has been entered the query execution will resume and may take some time. If there are no issues you will be taken back to the migration window and may proceed to the next step.

documents.t: Once SSMA has moved all of your old Version 8 Microsoft® Access Data into temporary tables in your new Database, select the Verify Source Database button which will verify the old Microsoft® Access Data is complete and ready to be synchronized.

Select the Sync Data button to move the Data to your Microsoft® SQL Server Database. During the sync process, you will provide input to different prompts, outlined below. Tool Chits Migration​ Select Shop Code​ Migrate Special Options Data​ This window is used to let us know how the Data needs to be copied based off of the options you were using in Version 8 of TCMax®. Select the Shop Code(s) that you would like to run the tool against and click the Migrate button under the Special Options that you were using. Once this is finished you can select the Close button to close this window and return to Migration screen.

You can remove any old Database tables that will no longer be used by TCMax® by clicking the Remove Old Data button. By opting to leave Old Data, you will notice all the version 8 tables will still remain intact but will essentially be 'archived' Data from the migration point.
You can now select Close and verify your items have migrated to your destination Database. note Often times, you will need to select the new Shop Code within Settings > Sites and Shops.
